Geotab fleet administration

You can set up and manage your Geotab fleet in the MyGeotab Portal with the steps below. Get more information by visiting Fleet Management Solutions.

On this page:

  • Check vehicle compatibility
  • Register, log in, and reset admin password
  • Administration in the admin portal
  • Hours of Service (HOS) setup & management

Check vehicle compatibility

If you don’t have a list of the makes/models you’ll be using, here are some general guidelines:

  • Most 1997 and newer light-duty vehicles are compatible if they have the 16-pin connector. This includes cars, minivans, SUVs, and light trucks.
  • Medium duty vehicles, like step-up vans or medium trucks, have varying compatibility and may require an adapter.
  • Most 1997 and newer heavy-duty vehicles are compatible with an adapter if they have the 6-pin or 9-pin connector. This includes buses, tractor trucks, and semi-trucks.
  • Devices without a connector can still get basic GPS functionality with the 3-wire adapter

Register, log in, and reset admin password

Register
  • T-Mobile will initiate the registration of new Geotab customers when you provide the following:
    • Name
    • Phone number
    • Email address for portal registration
  • Once T-Mobile initiates registration, an email is sent to the email address provided and the sales representative.
  • Open the email and follow the instructions to complete registration and create your password. The password must:
    • Be at least 12 characters
    • Have at least one lower case letter
    • Have at least one upper case letter
    • Have at least one number
    • Have at least one special symbol ($, @, etc.)
    • Not be included in the top 100 popular passwords
    • Must not contain emails or phone numbers
Log in
  • On a computer web browser, visit my.geotab.com or on a phone/tablet open the MyGeotab Fleet Management app.
  • Enter your email address and select Next.
  • Enter your password, then select Log in. Choose Go Back if you entered the wrong email address.
Reset password
  • On a computer web browser, visit my.geotab.com.
  • Enter your email address and select Next.
  • Select the question mark ? next to the password field.
  • Enter your email address and database name, then select OK. A reset email is sent to the email used to register.
  • Follow the link in the email to create a new password.
Log out
  • Select your email address.
  • Select Log out.

Administration in the admin portal

  • Influence safe driving behavior with in-vehicle driver feedback and coaching tools.
  • See vehicle location in near real-time and a complete trips history.
  • Reduce vehicle mileage and fuel consumption by creating zones and routes for your drivers.
  • Get alerts for potential critical engine health issues and easily prioritize the repairs for your vehicles.
  • Not all features are available for all rate plans.
Requirements
  • One of the following browsers:
    • Microsoft Internet Explorer 10+
    • The latest versions of Google Chrome
    • The latest versions of Mozilla® Firefox
    • Apple Safari 6.0
  • Microsoft .NET Framework 4.6
  • Also available on modern versions of Android/iOS with the MyGeotab Fleet Management app available in the Google Play Store/Apple App Store.
Dashboards

The application has different options for what you will see when logging in. One of those options is a graphical view of all your reports on one page. The dashboard is intended to highlight critical events and behaviors throughout your entire fleet at a single glance. Listed below are the built-in graphics displayed on the dashboard which help establish insights into your fleet.

  • Driver Score: Rates your drivers based on speeding, after-hours driving, and excessive idling.
  • Idle Time: Compares time spent idling as a percentage of the total driving time.
  • Activity: Analyzes the time spent in different zones: at the office, home, and customer zones.
  • Stops: Visualizes the number of stops made.
  • Business and Personal Use: Shows driver mileage for business and personal use while intelligently filtering away the drive to and from work.
View map

The Map tab allows you to view a list of your Geotab devices and see their location on a map.

  • Across the top you’ll find the following controls:
    • Search: Find devices by Vehicle/VIN/Zone/Route.
    • Map: Clear the map, highlight groups, change your view or map type, and show or hide traffic/legend/zones.
    • Add zone
    • Trip history
    • Nearest: Find the closest device to the center of the map.
    • Refresh
  • Choose a device from the list to zoom in on that specific device location.
  • In the map, select a device to see additional options.
Add a vehicle
  • On the Vehicles tab, choose Add.
  • To add one vehicle, select Add vehicle. Enter the serial number and vehicle description, then select OK.
  • To add multiple vehicles, choose Quick import. Enter one serial number and vehicle description per line, then select Import.
View/edit vehicle information
  • On the Vehicles tab, across the top you’ll find the following controls:
    • Search: Find devices by Name/VIN/Serial number.
    • Show: Choose to show recent, active, or all devices.
    • Add: Add or import a vehicle.
    • More: View additional options, like installation history.
    • View: Change the view between List, Report, Advanced, and Watchdog Report.
    • Download PDF/Excel
  • Select to view device details or see the location on a map next to the desired vehicle.
  • Select the vehicle to view/edit the following information:
    • Device tab:
      • Description
      • Device type (can’t be edited)
      • Serial number (can’t be edited)
      • Vehicle ID number
      • License plate
      • Odometer
      • Current engine hours
      • Comments
      • State/province
    • Driver Feedback tab: Enable/disable device beeping
    • Groups tab: Choose which groups the device belongs in
Check activity

On the Activity tab, view information and reporting on device activity.

  • Trips Street View: View a specific trip on a map.
  • Heat Map: Visualize trip data with a color-coded map of the area a vehicle travels most.
  • Risk Management: View information on risky driving habits like idling and speeding.
  • Speed Profile: View a graph of actual speed vs. speed limits.
  • Driver Congregation: View a report that shows times where drivers overlap locations at a specific time.
  • Work Hours: View time card information and work hours.
  • View Accidents & Log Data: View a detailed log of information recorded.
View engine & maintenance details

The Engine & Maintenance tab lets you view information related to vehicle engine and maintenance.

  • Engine faults
  • Engine measurements
  • Reminders for maintenance
Add a New Zone
  • On the Map tab, navigate to the area you want to create a zone in and select Add Zone.
  • Left-select the map and choose Add square zone here (you can customize this later).
  • Select a starting point on the map.
  • Continue adding additional points to create the boundary. Each new selection creates a line from the previous point directly to it.
  • Fill in the Zone Edit screen:
    • Zone name
    • Group to publish zones
    • Comments about the zone
    • Should the zone be visible on the map
    • Type of zone
    • Color of zone
  • Select Save. You’ll return to the Map tab with the new zone on the screen.
Create Zone spreadsheet.
  • On the Zones tab, choose Import Zones.
  • Select the question mark (?) for instructions on creating the spreadsheet.
    • You should use either a street address or latitude/longitude coordinates, but not both.
    • Do not include column headers in the spreadsheet, just the data.
Upload Zone spreadsheet
  • On the Zones tab, choose Import Zones.
  • Select the spreadsheet you created:
    • Move the spreadsheet onto Drop your files here.
    • Select Click to select them to navigate to and select the spreadsheet
  • Once the upload is complete, you’ll see the number of valid and invalid zones. Select Export to download a spreadsheet of invalid zones to fix them.
Set rules & groups

On the Rules & Groups tab, view and edit rules and groups.

  • Rules: Conditions that outline the ideal behavior of a fleet. When a vehicle event breaks a rule, an exception is recorded within the system and notifications can be sent to specific users.
  • Exceptions: View, add, edit, and delete exceptions to rules.
  • Groups: View an expandable tree of groups and subgroups.
Administration (reports, users, user passwords, and company details

Get administer reports, manage your users, and set up your systems.

  • Reports: Preview and download reports
  • Users: View and edit users’ information.
  • Systems: View and edit company information and user account policies

Hours of Service (HOS) setup & management

Before drivers can use the Geotab GO8 HOS app, you must have a plan that supports it and turn on HOS on the MyGeotab website.

Set up company information

The first thing you’ll need to do is make sure your company information is filled out correctly.

  • On the MyGeotab website, select Administration > System > System Settings.
  • Make sure the following fields are complete:
    • Company name
    • Company address
    • Maximum personal conveyance distance
    • Any other information if applicable
  • Select Save.
Set up vehicle

The next thing to do is make sure the vehicle is set up for HOS.

  • On the MyGeotab website, select Vehicles and choose the desired vehicle.
  • Select More Details.
    • Fill out the license plate, VIN, odometer, and current engine hours fields
    • Switch the Hours of Service switch to On
  • Select Save.
Set up driver

The last thing to do is set up the user so they can take advantage of HOS. For any questions related to the ELD mandate and HOS compliance, please contact your local Department of Transportation or visit fmcsa.dot.gov for more details.

  • On the MyGeotab website, select Administration > Users.
  • Choose the desired user or select Add to add a new one.
  • Fill out the following information (this must be filled out correctly to avoid risk of being out of compliance):
    • User name
    • First and last name
    • Password
    • Security clearance
    • Data access group (drivers can’t see vehicles or HOS logs outside of their group)
    • Additional fields, like Employee Number and Comments, can be filled out as needed
  • Select the Driver tab and fill out the following information:
    • Set “This user is a driver” to Yes.
    • Set “Prevent driver access to shared data” to Yes.
    • Set “Same as data access” to Yes.
    • Drivers license number
    • License state/province
  • Select the UI Settings tab and make sure the following is set up correctly:
    • Distance measurement system
    • Fuel economy measurement
    • Date and time format
    • Time zone
  • Select the HOS Settings tab and fill out the following (this must be filled out correctly to avoid risk of being out of compliance):
    • Ruleset followed by user
    • Exemptions relevant to the driver
    • Home terminal
    • Home terminal address
    • Carrier number
    • Yard Move and Personal Conveyance exemptions
    • Authority name
    • Authority address
View Duty Status logs & generate compliance reports
  • On the MyGeotab website, select Activity > HOS > Duty Status Logs.
  • Choose Options and select the Date Period and the Driver.
  • Select Apply changes to search for applicable duty status logs.
  • Choose from the available options:
    • Choose Add to add a new log.
    • Choose a specific log to edit it. Select Save when done.
    • Choose Compliance Print to generate a compliance report for presentation to law enforcement.
View Availability & Violations reports

Your free SIM replacement is waiting

Why did I get a message about changing my SIM?
  • T-Mobile has America’s largest and fastest 5G network and an LTE network that covers 99% of people in the U.S*.
  • Your current SIM card is not compatible with our network enhancements and must be replaced to avoid service interruptions.
  • Learn more about how our network is evolving.
What to do

Stop by a store, contact us, or contact T-Mobile Prepaid or click on the “Get Help” link below to order a replacement SIM. For your security, the account holder or an authorized user must make the request. Get help activating or installing a SIM. For your security, the account holder or an authorized user must make the request. Get help activating or installing a SIM.

You’ll also want to make sure your LTE/VoLTE settings are turned on and your software is up to date. Get steps!

Remember to update your LTE/VoLTE settings and software

  • We’re transforming our network experience and your device’s LTE/VoLTE settings and software may need to be updated.
  • Learn more about how our network is evolving.
  • Enabling LTE/VoLTE and running the latest software version will help avoid any service interruptions.
  • It’s easy! Just choose your device manufacturer and follow the steps.
  • If your device manufacturer isn’t listed or the steps don’t work, check out our Tutorials for steps specific to your device.
Apple

Steps for Apple software update or LTE/VoLTE settings

Setting

Steps

LTE

  • From the Home screen, choose Settings > Cellular or Cellular Data.

  • If you have an iPhone with an eSIM, select the line you’re making changes to.

  • Select Cellular Data Options, then choose the Enable LTE toggle.

  • If the toggles don’t display, select Voice & Data or Data and choose LTE. VoLTE

  • From any Home screen, choose Settings > Cellular or Cellular Data > Cellular Data Options.

  • If you have an iPhone with an eSIM, select the line you’re making changes to.

  • Select Enable LTE and choose Voice & Data. Software Update

  • From the Home Screen, choose Settings > General > Software Update.

  • If an update is available, select to download and install.

Samsung

Steps for Samsung software update or LTE/VoLTE settings

Setting

Steps

LTE

  • Open the Settings app and choose Mobile Networks. If it’s not there, select Connections first.

  • Select Network Mode and choose an option that says LTE. VoLTE

  • Open the Settings app and choose Connections > Mobile networks.

  • Slide the VoLTE calls switch to the ON or OFF position.

  • If it’s not there open the Phone app, press the Menu icon with three dots, and check in Settings. Software Update

  • From the Home screen, choose Settings > Software update > Download and install.

  • Select OK > Start. When the restart message appears, choose OK.

  • Repeat these steps until the device shows you have the latest software version.

LG

Steps for LG software update or LTE/VoLTE settings

Setting

Steps

LTE

  • From your apps list, choose Settings > Network > Mobile networks.

  • Select Network mode and choose an option that says LTE. VoLTE

  • From any home screen, select Phone.

  • Choose Menu > Call settings.

  • Select the VoLTE switch to turn it on or off. Software Update

  • From the Home screen, choose Settings > System > Update center.

  • Select System update > Check for update.

  • Follow the on-screen prompts to download and install the latest software update.

  • Repeat these steps until the device shows you have the latest software version.

OnePlus

Steps for OnePlus software update or LTE/VoLTE settings

Setting

Steps

LTE

  • From the Home screen, swipe up, then choose Settings.
  • Select Wi-Fi & internet > SIM & network > Preferred network type.
  • Choose an option that says LTE. VoLTE

VoLTE is always enabled when available

Software Update

  • From the Home screen, swipe up, then choose Settings.
  • Select System > System update > Check for update.
  • Follow the onscreen prompts to update to the latest software.
  • Repeat these steps until the device shows you have the latest software version.

Hardware how-tos: TVision HUB

The TVision HUB is a 4K HMDI device with access to over 8,000 video streaming, music, and gaming applications along with programmable Guide and DVR buttons to jump directly into your favorite Live TV application.

On this page:

  • Connect TVision HUB
  • Set up TVision HUB
  • Program TVision HUB remote

Connect TVision HUB

Before you start, check that you have:
  • A Wi-Fi internet connection
  • A Google account (required to download apps and games)
  • A TVision Account (optional, press the Home button on the remote to bypass)
Connect your HUB
  • Turn off your TV or monitor.
  • Connect your TVision HUB device to your TV or monitor with the HDMI cable.
  • Plug your TVision HUB device into an outlet.

Set up TVision HUB

There are three options to set up your TV HUB:

Set up with Quick Start
  • When your TV displays, “Quickly set up your TV with your Android phone,” use your remote to select Continue or Yes. If you don’t have an Android phone, select Skip.
  • On your Android phone, open the pre-installed Google app.
  • Type or say “set up device.”
  • Follow the instructions on your phone.
  • On your phone, select the name of your TV when it shows up.
  • Follow the instructions on your TV to complete setup. Your TV will automatically sign into your Google account and connect to the same Wi-Fi as your phone.
  • Follows steps in ‘Program TVision HUB remote’ when prompted to program remote to TV.
Set up with your TVision HUB remote
  • Program the TVision HUB remote following the on-screen instructions (review Program TVision HUB remote).
  • When your TV displays, “Quickly set up your TV with your Android phone,” use your remote to select Skip.
  • Connect to Wi-Fi (you may need to wait for the system to update).
  • Select Sign in > Use your remote.
  • Sign in to your Google Account.
  • Follow the on-screen instructions to finish setup.
Set up with your phone or computer
  • Program the TVision HUB remote following the on-screen instructions (review Program TVision HUB remote).
  • When your TV displays, “Quickly set up your TV with your Android phone,” use your remote to select Skip.
  • Connect to the same Wi-Fi network as your phone or computer (you may need to wait for the system to update).
  • On your TV, select Sign in > Use your phone or computer.
  • Sign in to your Google Account.
  • Follow the on-screen instructions to finish setup.

Program TVision HUB remote

You will be prompted to connect your TVision HUB remote when turning the device on for the first time. The remote control needs to have line-of-sight with the TV, so make sure you point the remote at the TV when you want to control TV Power, Input, Volume, and Mute.

Program the TVision HUB remote during initial setup

You will be prompted to program your TVision HUB remote when turning the device on for the first time. During the initial set up, the TVision HUB remote will be paired with the TVision HUB and then the TVision HUB remote will be programmed to the TV.

  • Pair the TVision HUB remote to the TVision HUB.
    • Make sure the remote is within 20 cm of the TVision HUB with a clear line of sight.
    • Hold the back and home buttons at the same time. The LED light will blink until the remote is connected and the TV will display a message indicating the remote has successfully connected.
  • Follow the on-screen TVision HUB set up instructions.
  • Program the TVision HUB remote to the TV:
    • Select Get started.
    • Choose how you want to control sound (TV or TVision HUB).
    • Scan for devices and select the brand of TV you’re trying to connect.
    • Use the white power button on your remote to select Yes.
    • Check that the INPUT button on your remote switches the input of your TV and select Yes.
    • Check that the Mute button on your remote is working and select Yes.
Program the TVision HUB remote after Initial Set Up

Follow these steps to pair the TVision HUB remote to a new TV when the TVision HUB is already set up.

  • From the Home Screen, navigate to and select the Settings icon.
  • Select Device Preferences.
  • Select Smart Control.
  • The Smart Control Wizard will begin. Follow on screen instructions:
  • Select Get started.
    • Choose how you want to control sound (select TV or TVision HUB).
    • Scan for devices and select the brand of TV you’re trying to connect.
    • Use the white power button on your remote to select Yes.
    • Check that the INPUT button on your remote switches the input of your TV and select Yes.
    • Check that the Mute button on your remote is working and select Yes.
Program the TVision HUB remote for Power and Input Only

Only follow these steps if you are unable to program the remote during set up or using the Smart Control setting. The power button (white) and the INPUT button on the TVision Remote control can learn the POWER and INPUT IR codes from your TV’s remote control.

  • When the programming the TVision remote control, keep the remotes within three (3) centimeters of each other.
  • If the TVision remote control doesn’t program within 20 seconds, the remote will automatically stop attempting to program.
  • Repeatedly programming the same function will overwrite the previously programmed function.
Unpair the TVision HUB remote from the TVision HUB

Only one TVision remote can be connected to the TVision HUB at a time. To connect a new remote, the old remote must be disconnected as follows:

  • From the TVision HUB Home screen, select Settings.
  • Select Remotes & Accessories > Remote Name > Unpair.
  • Select OK to confirm.
  • Once disconnected, you will be prompted to connect your TVision HUB remote.
Paired remote is unresponsive
  • On the TVision HUB (not the TVision remote), hold the power button for 5 seconds.
  • You will be prompted to connect your TVision HUB remote.

Hardware how-tos: TVision HUB with Google TV

This page provides high-level features and steps to set up. For issues and helpful hints to use or troubleshoot Google TV, go to support.google.com and search for Google TV.

On this page:

  • Connect TVision HUB
  • Set up TVision HUB
  • Program TVision HUB remote

Connect TVision HUB

Before you start, check that you have:
  • A Wi-Fi internet connection (Ethernet cable required for optional use of the LAN port)
  • A Google account is required to download apps and games
Connect your HUB
  • Plug your TVision HUB into any open HDMI port on the TV.
  • Plug the micro-USB cable provided (small end) into the TVision HUB (port marked with “DC 5V”), and plug the adapter into a power outlet or an available USB input on your TV.
    • Use the power adapter provided with the device to ensure the device is receiving the appropriate amount of power.
  • Open the back of the remote and insert the batteries.
  • Follow the on-screen instructions to pair your remote.
  • Follow the instructions on your screen to finish setup and device activation.

Set up TVision HUB

Set up with Google Home App
  • When your TV displays, “Set up with Google Home App”, download and open the Google Home app on your phone and select Set Up Google TV Device (if you don’t want to set up in the Google Home app, select Set up on TV instead).
  • Scan the QR code with your mobile device.
  • Follow the instructions on your phone to connect to create or add to an existing home profile and connect to Wi-Fi.
  • Once completed and all apps have installed, the device will run a remote control set up for control of TV volume, power, and input with the TVision HUB remote.
  • Select Get Started to begin set up.
Set up on TV with your TVision HUB remote
  • After selecting Set up on your TV instead, follow these instructions to sign into wifi and your Google account to complete set up.
  • Select your wifi connection in the list on screen (if connected via ethernet, your device will move to the next step).
  • Enter the password for the chosen Wi-Fi connection.
  • Sign into a Google account (a Google account is required for use of the TVision HUB w/ Google TV).
  • Follow the on-screen instructions to finish setup.
  • Once completed and all apps have installed, the device will run a remote control set up for control of TV volume, power, and input with the TVision HUB remote.
  • Select Get Started to begin set up.

Program TVision HUB remote

You will be prompted to connect your TVision HUB remote when turning the device on for the first time. The remote control needs to have line-of-sight with the TV - so make sure you point the remote at the TV when you want to control TV Power, Input, Volume, and Mute.

Program the TVision HUB remote - During initial setup

You will be prompted to program your TVision HUB remote when turning the device on for the first time. During the initial set up, the TVision HUB remote will be paired with the TVision HUB and then the TVision HUB remote will be programmed to the TV.

  • Pair the TVision HUB remote to the TVision HUB.
    • Make sure the remote is within 8 inches of the TVision HUB with a clear line of sight.
    • Hold the back and home buttons at the same time. The LED light will blink until the remote is connected and the TV will display a message indicating the remote has successfully connected.
  • Follow the on-screen TVision HUB set up instructions.
Program the TVision HUB remote to control TV volume, power and input– After Initial Set Up

Follow these steps to pair the TVision HUB remote to a new TV when the TVision HUB is already set up.

  • Hold the Home button on the remote.
  • Go to the Settings icon and select OK on the remote to select.
  • Go to Remotes & Accessories.
  • Select Smart Control.
  • Follow on screen instructions.
Paired remote is unresponsive
  • On the TVision HUB device, hold the button on side of the device for 5 seconds (this is the button on the TVision HUB, not the remote).
  • You will be prompted to connect your TVision HUB remote using the steps on this page to Program.
Change accounts

Google TV suggestions are based on viewing history. To get personalized results in Google TV and on device apps, make sure you’re signed into the appropriate Google account. To switch accounts:

  • Hold the Home button on the HUB remote.
  • Select settings from the on-screen menu.
  • Select Accounts & Sign In.
  • Select Add another account to create a profile for another user.
  • Select Add a kid for an account with parental controls enabled.
Remove/manage account
  • Hold the Home button on the HUB remote.
  • Select Settings from the on-screen menu.
  • Select Accounts & Sign In.

How to return a new device

If you don’t love your new purchase, we can help you return it so you can find your perfect match. Please review the things to know before you begin, then select the method of how you got your device.

Things to know before you begin

  • This information is for returning a new device. There is a different process for returning your trade-in device.
  • A restocking fee may be charged when returning your new device.
  • Refunds may take up to 30 days to process. We will refund the purchase price, excluding rebates, special discounts, and restocking fees.
  • You must return everything that came in the box with the device, like the USB charging cable. SIM cards do not need to be returned.
  • If any of the returned items are damaged or if the return isn’t completed properly, you will not be refunded.
  • Keep any accessories you bought separately, like media cards or memory cards.
  • Remove your personal data. Review your device’s tutorial for a master reset.

Return your device

How you got your device determines the return process. Select from one of these methods to learn what to do next:

Purchased at a T-Mobile store
  • Return your device at any T-Mobile store within 14 days.
  • Bring proof of purchase such as an emailed or printed receipt.
  • Bring the device, USB charging cable, and any accessories you’ll need to return.
Ordered online using in-store pickup
  • Return your device at any T-Mobile store within 20 days.
  • Bring proof of purchase, such as an emailed or printed receipt.
  • Bring the device, USB charging cable, and any accessories you’ll need to return.
  • If you’re unable to go to a store, begin the return process by using the chat bubble or calling Customer Care at 1-800-937-8997.
Shipped to you: return to a T-Mobile store
  • Return your device or accessory order at any T-Mobile store or contact us within 20 days of when the order shipped.
  • A device condition check will be completed to ensure no damage to the device.
  • Bring proof of purchase, such as an emailed or printed receipt.
  • Bring the device, USB charging cable, and any accessories you’ll need to return.
Shipped to you: ship device or accessory to T-Mobile
  • Contact us to start the return process so we can email you a return shipping label.
    • New account online activations/add-a-line: call 1-800-672-5390.
    • Accounts active more than 30 days: use the chat bubble or call 1-800-937-8997.
  • Once we’ve started the return process, use these guidelines:
    • If you’re returning one device:
      • If you’re using your original box, cover the existing labels and stickers.
      • For battery/power station devices like portable power packs, your email will include a special cargo label that must be printed in color and attached to the outside of the box.
      • T-Mobile return shipping labels can only be used for the intended purpose of returning items covered by the return policy.
      • If non-T-Mobile items are sent to us in error, please call Customer Care within 60 days. After that, unclaimed items may be considered abandoned and we’ll dispose of them.
    • If you’re returning multiple devices:
      • Print the cargo/hazardous material label in color if your box doesn’t already have this label.
      • Important: Do not shrink or scale the color image when printing.
    • Returns must be postmarked within 20 days of when the order shipped.
    • Securely pack returns to prevent damage during shipment.
    • Print the UPS return shipping label that we emailed you and apply to your package. Cover any existing shipping label.

What’s included with P360

Protection 360® is a complete device protection program that covers repair or replacement for loss, theft, accidental damage (including $0 front screen repairs), and mechanical & electrical failure, even after the manufacturer’s warranty expires.

  • For complete coverage details, benefits, limitations, exclusions, and costs, visit mytmoclaim.com/terms.

  • Device protection is not required to activate service with T-Mobile, but without protection, you may be responsible for the full replacement cost of your device if it is accidentally damaged, lost, stolen or suffers a mechanical breakdown.

  • Protection 360 gives you access to both an insurance plan and a service contract plan. In New York, these options can be bought separately. In New York:

  • The Insurance Device Protection Plan provides coverage for accidental damage, loss, and theft. For BYOD customers, this benefit starts after the manufacturer’s warranty expires.

  • The Service Contract Device Protection Plan provides coverage for mechanical and electrical failure, JUMP!® Upgrades, unlimited screen protector replacements, and access to tech support and mobile security apps.

  • Discount for both plans: If you buy both the Insurance Device Protection Plan and the Service Contract Device Protection Plan, you’ll get a discount of up to $1.50 on the Insurance Device Protection Plan, depending on the device tier.

  • • If you choose to buy a service contract from another provider and want to enroll in the Insurance Device Protection Plan and receive the same discount, please visit a T-Mobile store or Contact Us within 30 days of enrollment. You must show proof of service contract.

How claims work
  • File claims online at www.mytmoclaim.com or in the Protection 360 app on Android or iOS.
  • Once your claim is approved, a deductible based on your device tier and the type of claim plus tax, if applicable, will be collected from you by credit card, debit card or eCheck.
  • $5 processing fee for mechanical and electrical failure exchanges through T-Mobile.
    • No processing fee for eligible hardware service claims handled by the manufacturer. All BYOD hardware service exchanges must be handled by Assurant.
    • No processing fee for BYOD coverage (add savings and overnight shipping.)
Protection 360 benefits
  • Unlimited claims for accidental damage.
  • Unlimited claims for mechanical and electrical failure, even after the manufacturer warranty expires.
  • Up to five total device replacements for loss or theft in any rolling 12-month period based on the date of the first replacement.
  • Unlimited $0 front screen repairs and $29 back glass repairs for eligible smartphones.
  • Unlimited screen protector replacements for eligible protectors bought at T-Mobile.
  • McAfee Security for T-Mobile with ID Theft Protection
    • Secures your digital life with safe browsing, antivirus/malware, identity theft, and lost wallet protection.
    • McAfee Security for T-Mobile with ID Theft Protection is provided by McAfee.
    • For more information and legal disclaimers, visit: mcafee.com
  • If you purchase Protection 360, Apple may provide service and technical support for eligible devices through AppleCare Service.
  • Your new Apple device is eligible for AppleCare Services during the first 24 months from the date you enroll in Protection 360 and as long as your plan coverage remains uninterrupted.
  • JUMP! Upgrades: Available on EIP devices when 50 percent of the device cost has been paid. (No BYOD)
  • Protection 360 app by Assurant - File and track a claim or get live technical support for your connected devices like routers, game consoles, and smart TVs.
    • Download and register the Protection 360 app by Assurant for full feature access.
    • Availability and features may vary by device and operating system.
Standard Device Protection benefits
  • One claim for loss, theft, or accidental damage, including $29 screen repair, in any rolling 12-month period.
  • Unlimited claims for mechanical and electrical failure, even after the manufacturer warranty expires.
  • Not available in NY.
Bring your own device (BYOD) P360 benefits
  • All items as listed in P360 section except JUMP!® Upgrades and AppleCare.
  • Mechanical and electrical failure benefit starts after the manufacturer’s warranty expires.
  • Learn more about BYOD coverage, on the BYOD page.

You can enroll or cancel at any time. At enrollment you do not need to make a device purchase or register the devices you want to cover.

Enroll
  • Add the Protection 360® HomeTech feature in T-Life or your T-Mobile account.
    • Make sure you can access the Primary Account Holder’s email.
    • This is where the Welcome/Enrollment email will be sent.
  • Download the Protection 360® HomeTech app on your Android or iOS device.
  • You will receive a Welcome email with enrollment instructions:
    • Open the Protection 360® app & follow the on-screen steps to create an account.
    • You must enter the same email address that the Welcome message was sent to.
    • Once your email is verified, your contact information will populate. You can also enroll on a desktop computer by visiting Protection360HomeTech.com.
Cancel

Cancel at any time by removing the Protection 360® HomeTech feature in T-Life or your T-Mobile account.

Add your devices

Adding a device ahead of time makes it faster to get live tech support or start a claim. You don’t have to register any of your devices for them to be covered, but if you need to file a claim your device must be in the device inventory list.

HomeTech app
  • Open the Protection 360® HomeTech app.
  • Select My Devices.
  • Use the search bar to find and add your device.
  • If you don’t see your device, choose Add device details and fill them in.
Protection360HomeTech.com
  • Log into Protection360HomeTech.com.
  • Select My Devices.
  • Use the search bar to find and select your device.
  • If you don’t see your device, choose Enter device details and fill them in.

File a claim

Before you file a claim, check the following:

  • It has been more than 30 days since adding Protection 360® HomeTech unless your device was damaged by a power surge.
  • You have the make and model of your devices.
  • Your devices have been added to the app or website. To file a claim, follow these steps:
HomeTech app
  • Open the HomeTech app.
  • Choose File a claim on the My Account tab.
  • Select your device. If you haven’t added the device, add it now.
  • Answer questions about the device condition.
  • Confirm your contact details, then select Submit.
  • You’ll receive an email when your claim is approved or denied and next steps.
Protection360HomeTech.com
  • Log into Protection360HomeTech.com.
  • Select My Devices.
  • If you haven’t added the device, add it now.
  • Select the device you need to file a claim for, then choose Claims & Support.
  • Choose File a claim and answer questions about the device condition.
  • Confirm your contact details, then select Submit.
  • You’ll receive an email when your claim is approved or denied and next steps.
Tracking your claim
  • In the HomeTech app, your claim is shown on your My Account tab.
  • On Protection360HomeTech.com, select My Devices and choose the device to view the claim status.

Contact support

HomeTech app

PUK code unlock

If a SIM PIN security code has been entered incorrectly multiple times, the SIM will lock and require you to enter a PUK code to use your device again. Be careful! If you incorrectly enter your PUK code 10 times, your SIM will need to be replaced.

  • Make sure the device is asking for a PUK. If it’s asking for a PIN, try the default SIM PINs of ‘1234’ or ‘5678’.
  • If you get a prompt about a PUK code or your SIM is locked, Contact Us to request your PUK code.
  • If you’re prompted to enter the PUK code, enter it. You may need to attempt a phone call before you are prompted to enter the code.
    • Enter your PUK code in the PUK field.
    • Enter your SIM New PIN code in the [New PIN] field. You must enter it twice.
  • If you’re not prompted to enter a PUK code, open the phone dialer and enter SIM 1 **05PUK[New PIN] *[New PIN]# or SIM 2 **052[PUK2][New PIN2]*[New PIN2]#.
    • USSD short codes must be enabled on your device for the PUK unlock code to work.

Recovery mode

If your device is having issues, you can use recovery mode to wipe the cache partition or delete all the information.

On this page:

  • Delete all information / reset
  • Wipe cache partition

Delete all information / reset

Alcatel / Coolpad
  • Back up data on the internal memory.
  • Turn off the device.
  • Press and hold the Power button and the Volume up button.
  • When the phone turns on, release the Power button but continue to hold the Volume up button until you see the Recovery screen.
  • Use the Volume buttons to scroll to Wipe data/factory reset, then press the Power button.
  • Use the Volume buttons to scroll to Factory data reset, then press the Power button.
  • Wait until the device finishes formatting and brings you back to the menu.
  • Use the Volume buttons to scroll to Reboot system now, then press the Power button.
CAT
  • Back up data on the internal memory.
  • Turn off the device.
  • Press and hold the Power button.
  • When the Android logo displays, immediately release the Power button, and simultaneously press and hold the Volume down button.
  • An ‘Installing system update’ message may show briefly before the Android Recovery menu options appear.
  • Press the Volume down button several times to highlight Wipe data / factory reset, then press the Power button.
  • Press the Volume down button several times to highlight YES, then press the Power button.
  • When the process is complete, Reboot system now is highlighted.
  • Press the Power button to restart the device.
Google
  • Back up data on the internal memory.
  • Turn off the device.
  • Press and hold the Volume down button and Power button at the same time.
  • When you get the triangle with an exclamation point and Fastboot, release both buttons.
  • Use the Volume buttons to choose Recovery Mode, then press the Power button.
  • Use the Volume buttons to highlight Wipe data/factory reset, then press the Power button.
  • Use the Volume buttons to highlight Yes, then press the Power button. Wait while your information is deleted.
  • Use the Volume buttons to highlight Reboot system now, then press the Power button.
LG
  • Back up data on the internal memory.
  • Turn off the device.
  • Press and hold the Power/Lock button and the Volume Down button at the same time.
  • When the LG logo appears, quickly release and then re-hold the Power/Lock button while continuing to hold the Volume Down button.
  • When ‘Factory data reset’ appears, use the Volume Down button to highlight Yes.
  • Press the Power/Lock button to select.
  • When prompted to “Erase all user data and restore default settings,” use the Volume Down button to highlight Yes.
  • Press the Power/Lock button to select and reset the device.
Motorola / moto
  • Back up data on the internal memory.
  • Turn off the device.
  • Press and hold the Volume down button and the Power button at the same time until the phone turns on.
  • Release the Power button but continue to hold the Volume down button until the Recovery screen appears.
  • Use the Volume buttons to highlight Recovery Mode.
  • Press and hold the Power button. While holding it down, press the Volume Up button, then release both buttons.
  • Use the Volume buttons to highlight Wipe data/factory reset, then press the Power button.
  • Use the Volume buttons to highlight Factory data reset, then press the Power button.
  • Use the Volume buttons to highlight Reboot system now, then press the Power button.
Nokia
  • Back up data on the internal memory.
  • Turn off the device.
  • Press and hold the Volume up button and the Power button at the same time until the phone turns on.
  • Use the Volume buttons to highlight Wipe data/factory reset, then press the Power button.
  • Use the Volume buttons to highlight Factory data reset, then press the Power button.
OnePlus
  • Press and hold the Volume down button and Power button at the same time.
  • When the OnePlus logo appears, release the Power button, but continue holding the Volume down button.
  • At the Password screen, enter the Password or PIN number that you use to unlock your device. When done, select Ok.
  • Choose English, Wipe data and cache, Reset everything (Music, pics, etc).
  • Select This cannot be undone, continue?, then choose Reboot to restart your phone.
Samsung
  • Back up data on the internal memory.
  • If you have signed into a Samsung account on the device, you have activated Anti-theft and will need your Samsung credentials to finish the factory reset.
  • Turn off the device.
  • Press and hold the Volume Up button first, then the Side button. Continue holding while the device powers on.
  • Press Volume down to highlight Wipe data / factory reset, then press Side button to select it.
  • Use the Volume buttons to highlight Factory data reset, then press the Side button.
  • Use the Volume buttons to highlight Reboot system now, then press the Side button.
  • When complete, highlight Reboot system now with the Volume down button and select it with the Side button.
T-Mobile
  • Back up data on the internal memory.
  • Turn the device off.
  • Press and hold the Volume up button, then press and hold the Power button at the same time until the phone turns on.
  • When the device powers on, release the Power button but continue holding Volume up until the recovery screen appears.
  • Use the Volume buttons to highlight Wipe data/factory reset, then press the Power button.
  • Use the Volume buttons to highlight Factory data reset, then press the Power button.
  • Use the Volume buttons to highlight Reboot system now, then press the Power button.
TCL
  • Back up data on the internal memory.
  • Turn the device off.
  • Press and hold the Power button and the Volume up button.
  • When the phone turns on, release the Power button but continue to hold the Volume up button until you get the Recovery screen.
  • Use the Volume buttons to scroll to Wipe data/factory reset, then press the Power button.
  • Use the Volume buttons to scroll to Factory data reset, then press the Power button.
  • Wait until the device finishes formatting and brings you back to the menu.
  • Use the Volume buttons to scroll to Reboot system now, then press the Power button.

Wipe cache partition

Wiping the cache partition may resolve device issues without deleting personal data. Not available on all devices.

Alcatel / Coolpad
  • Turn off the device.
  • Press and hold the Volume Up and Power buttons.
  • When the device turns on and logo displays, release both buttons.
  • Use the Volume buttons to highlight wipe cache partition, then press the Power button.
  • Continue using the Volume and Power buttons to confirm your choice if prompted.
  • Wait while the cache partition is wiped.
  • Use the Volume buttons to highlight Reboot system now and select it with the Power button.
  • Wait for the device to reset.
CAT
  • Turn off the device.
  • Press and hold the Power button.
  • When the Android logo displays, immediately release the Power button, and simultaneously press and hold the Volume down button.
  • An ‘Installing system update’ message may show briefly before the Android Recovery menu options appear.
  • Press the Volume down button several times to highlight Wipe cache partition, then press the Power button.
  • When the process is complete, Reboot system now is highlighted.
  • Press the Power button to restart the device.
Samsung
  • Turn off the device.
  • Press and hold the Volume Up button first, then the Side button. Continue holding while the device powers on.
  • Press Volume down to highlight Wipe cache partition, then press Side button to select it.
  • Continue using the Volume down and Side buttons to confirm your choice if prompted.
  • When complete, highlight Reboot system now with the Volume down button and select it with the Side button.
T-Mobile
  • Turn the device off..
  • Press and hold the Volume up button, then press and hold the Power button at the same time until the phone turns on.
  • When the device powers on, release the Power button but continue holding Volume up until the recovery screen appears.
  • Use the Volume buttons to highlight Wipe cache partition, then press the Power button.
  • Use the Volume and Power buttons to confirm your choices if prompted. Wait while the cache partition is wiped.
  • Use the Volume buttons to highlight Reboot system now, then press the Power button.

Roambee BeeAware administration (EOL)

The Roambee device is no longer available to order.

You can set up and manage your Roambee devices with the steps on this page. Check out the Asset Management & Tracking with NB IoT page for more information.

On this page:

  • Add, modify, or delete users

Log in and navigate the Roambee Portal

Login

To log in for the first time, make sure you’ve received an email from support@roambee.com with your password. If you haven’t received it, contact your system administrator.

  • In a web browser, visit portal.roambee.com.
  • Enter your user name (email address) and password.
  • Select Log in.
  • If you belong to multiple accounts, choose the account you want to log into.
Navigation

The portal is divided into three areas:

  • The Main Bar has the user name, role, Support button, and Modern View button.
  • The Module Menu allows you to choose from a variety of pages in the portal, like Manage Users, Shipments, Locations, and Bees.
  • The Screen Area changes depending on what you select in the Module Menu.

Add, modify, or delete users

Add a User
  • Choose the Manage Users module.
  • Select the + by to Add user.
  • Fill out the Add new user pop-up. You must fill out fields with an asterisk (*).
  • Select Save. An email is sent to the new users.
Modify a User
  • Choose the Manage Users module.
  • Select the Actions by to the user you want to modify.
  • Select Edit.
  • Update any information in the Edit user pop-up.
  • Select Save.
Delete a User
  • Choose the Manage Users module.
  • Select Actions by to the user you want to modify.
  • Select Delete.

Create and edit locations

Create a location
  • Choose the Locations module.
  • Select Add.
  • Fill out the Location Wizard pop-up. You must fill out fields with an asterisk (*).
  • Select Add Location.
Edit a location
  • Choose the Locations module.
  • Select Edit by to the location you want to edit.
  • Update any information in the Location Wizard pop-up.
  • Select Modify Location.

Create, edit, and use accounts

Create a sub-account
  • Choose the Accounts module.
  • Select Add.
  • Fill out the Create a new Account pop-up.
    • You must fill out fields with an asterisk (*).
    • You must fill out all four tabs. Select Continue once you’ve completed a tab.
  • Select Save.
Edit a sub-account
  • Choose the Accounts module.
  • Select Edit by the sub-account you want to edit.
  • Update any information as needed, then select Save.
Log in to a sub-account
  • Choose the Accounts module.
  • Select Login as by the sub-account you want to log in on.
  • You can also switch between accounts by choosing Select Account to log in as.

Create and fulfill orders

Create an order
  • Choose the Orders module.
  • Select New.
  • Choose the account you’re creating the order for, then select OK.
  • Fill out the order information, including the shipment destination, SKU, and quantity, then select Place Order.
Fulfill an order
  • Choose the Orders module.
  • Select the Actions menu by the order you want to fulfill, then select Fulfill.
  • Make sure the order summary is correct, then select Continue.
  • Assign the devices that will be used on the sub-account, then select Continue.
  • Enter the shipping information, then select Fulfill. Make sure the device was assigned to the correct sub-account.

Manage your bees

Find out where your Bees will work

Check our narrowband coverage map to check where Roambee BeeAware will work. International and domestic roaming are not supported.

Roambee BeeAware buttons & LEDs
  • The Network LED blinks green fast when searching for coverage, blinks green slowly when connected, and is off when in sleep mode or off.
  • The Battery LED is solid red when charged, blinks red fast when charging or powering on/off, blinks red slowly when the battery is low, and is off when device is on and working fine.
  • The GPS LED is Solid yellow when it has a GPS fix, blinking yellow when searching for GPS, and is off when in sleep mode or off.
  • Press and hold the Power button for 3 seconds to turn on or off.
  • Use the USB charging port to plug in your charging cable.
  • Press and hold the Multi-function button to report the current location and restart GPS fix.
  • The Hanging hole is used to hang the device when affixing is not an option.
Bee Pickup
  • Choose the Bee Pickup Page module.
  • Enter the device name and all related information regarding the pickup purpose. You must fill out fields with an asterisk (*).
  • Select Save. You’ll receive a confirmation the device was checked-in, select Ok.
  • You can confirm the device was checked in by choosing the Bees module.
Change reporting interval
  • Choose the Bees module.
  • Select Actions by to the desired device, then select interval.
  • Set the desired reporting interval between 5 minutes and 24 hours, then select Send Change.
View device history
  • Choose the Bees module.
  • Select Actions by the desired device, then select history.
  • Adjust the desired date range and select Go!.
  • You’ll be taken to a screen that displays a map and the sensor history.
View device messages
  • Choose the Bees module.
  • Select Actions by the desired device, then select messages.
  • Choose the time zone and adjust the desired date range, then select Go!.
  • View the device messages. Choose the + to get more details for a specific message.
Manage and download data
  • Choose the Bees module.
  • Use the following options to filter devices as needed:
    • Search lets you search for specific devices
    • Show/hide columns lets you restrict what information appears on the screen
    • Reset tables resets the device list back to default view
  • Choose how you want to download your data:
    • Download lets you download a file with the data
    • Copy places the information to your clipboard so you can paste it
    • Excel exports the information to Excel
    • PDF converts the data into a PDF file

Software Updates & Backup

Device resets

Steps for

Master reset from settings menu

A master reset removes all user accounts and resets your Samsung Galaxy Chromebook Go to factory settings and may delete your personal data on the internal storage, such as downloads, images, and apps. It doesn’t delete data stored on the SIM card or SD card.

  • Back up data on the internal memory.
  • Select the Time > Settings in the bottom right-hand corner of your screen.
  • Select Advanced > Reset settings.
  • In the Powerwash section, select Reset.
  • Read and check the Powerwash disclaimer, select Continue > Restart.
  • Wait for the device to reset. Soft reset with hardware keys

A soft reset is a simulated battery removal. Use a soft reset to power a device off when the screen is frozen or unresponsive and the device has an internal battery that can’t be removed. It doesn’t cause loss of personal data on the device.

  • Press and hold the Power button for at least 8 seconds.
  • Wait 3 -5 seconds, next press the Power button on the device keyboard to turn your device back on.
Software updates
  • Select the Time > All Settings (cog wheel) in the bottom right-hand corner of your screen.
  • Select Windows Update.
  • Wait for the device to check for updates, and download if a new software version is available.

First time use

When you first turn on your new device, you may get a setup wizard to help you get started. Use these steps to walk through the setup process if needed.

This Google Account will be set as the owner and is the only account that will be able to change certain Chrome settings.

Software Updates & Device Resets

Master reset from settings menu

A master reset removes all user accounts and resets your Samsung Galaxy Chromebook Go to factory settings and may delete your personal data on the internal storage, such as downloads, images, and apps. It doesn’t delete data stored on the SIM card or SD card.

  • Back up data on the internal memory.
  • Select the Time > Settings.
  • Select Advanced > Reset settings.
  • In the Powerwash section, select Reset.
  • Read and check the Powerwash disclaimer, select Continue > Restart.
  • Wait for the device to reset.
Soft reset

This is a uni-body device with an internal battery that cannot be removed. If you need to soft reset the device, follow these steps:

  • Select the Time > Settings.
  • Select the Shut down icon.
  • Wait 3 -5 seconds, next press the Power button on the device keyboard to turn your device back on.
Soft reset with hardware keys

A soft reset is a simulated battery removal. Use a soft reset to power a device off when the screen is frozen or unresponsive and the device has an internal battery that can’t be removed. It doesn’t cause loss of personal data on the device.

  • Press and hold the Power button for at least 8 seconds.
  • Wait 3 -5 seconds, then press the Power button on the device keyboard to turn your device back on.
Software updates
  • Select the Time > Settings.
  • Select About Chrome OS
  • Select Check for updates.
  • Wait for the device to check for updates, and download if a new software version is available.

Samsung Galaxy Wearable app

Galaxy Wearable and Samsung Galaxy Watch are third-party applications for Android and Apple iOS devices. The Galaxy Wearable app connects your wearable device to your phone.

On this page:

  • About the app
  • Samsung wearable and phone compatibility
  • How to use the app
  • Helpful tips

About the app

While some Samsung watches can be set up and used without a phone, all of them can be used with the Galaxy Wearable app on a compatible phone. It also manages and monitors wearable device features and apps installed through Galaxy Gear Apps.

Samsung wearable and phone compatibility

Samsung wearables are only compatible with certain phones and operating systems. Make sure your phone is compatible before trying to set up your watch.

  • A Samsung phone will have the most compatibility options.
  • A non-Samsung phone running Android may have limited support on some features, and some features are only available on Samsung phones.
  • Apple iOS
  • Newer Samsung watches with Wear OS are not compatible with iOS.
  • Some older Samsung watches are compatible with certain versions of iOS.
  • Review the complete list of compatible devices, OS versions, and features on Samsung.com.
  • Samsung Galaxy rings are supported on Samsung phones running Android 11.0 or newer. They are not compatible with iOS.

How to use the app

Activate or connect a watch on your smartphone
  • Turn on your watch.
  • On your phone, install and open the Galaxy Wearable app.
  • Update the app to the latest version if needed.
  • Start the setup:
    • If your phone isn’t paired with the watch, select Get started in the app.
    • If your phone is paired with the watch already, select Watch settings > Mobile plans in the app.
  • Follow the on-screen prompts to continue the activation process.
Remote connection

Use your Samsung account to connect your phone to your watch remotely over Wi-Fi or mobile network. This is useful when the devices are not connected by Bluetooth. Your watch can still receive notifications from your phone.

  • You must connect your watch to Wi-Fi and sign in to your Samsung account on your phone to enable this feature.
  • Open the Galaxy Wearable app.
  • Select Watch settings > Advanced features > Remote connection.
  • Select the switch to turn on or off.
Back up, switch phones, and restore

When you connect your watch to another phone, the watch resets. Make sure you back up important data and settings on your watch, so you can restore them.

  • Back up your watch settings and data:
    • Open the Galaxy Wearable app.
    • Select Watch settings > Accounts and backup.
    • Select Backup, if prompted, select Open Smart Switch.
    • Review the required permissions, select Allow.
    • View the date and time of Last backed up, if Backup files are listed. Backups can also be saved to Samsung account storage when signed into your Samsung account.
  • Switch to a new phone:
    • On your watch, swipe down and select Settings > General > Transfer watch to new phone > Transfer watch to new phone?.
    • This removes the watch connection on your current phone and resets your watch.
    • Next, follow steps to activate or connect to your new phone.
  • Restore your watch settings and data:
    • Open the Galaxy Wearable app.
    • Select Watch settings > Accounts and backup.
    • Select Back up and restore > Restore.
    • The phone searches for backups to restore.
    • Review the backup data you want to restore.
    • Select Restore now.
    • Confirm Remote connection is turned on.
Software updates
  • Open the Galaxy Wearable app.
  • Select Watch settings > Software update > Check for updates.
  • Wait as your device updates and restarts, if an update is available.
Find My Watch
  • Open the Galaxy Wearable app.
  • Select Watch settings > Find my watch > Continue.
  • Review Samsung Find permissions, select Continue.
  • Review Find your Galaxy devices, select Turn on or Skip.
  • Select how often you receive a Notification when someone views your location.
  • Select Next.
  • Select Ring.
  • Your watch will vibrate and ring to help you find it.
  • When you’ve found your watch, select Stop.

Helpful tips

  • To make the most out of your watch or even navigate its settings on a bigger screen, it is recommended that you pair your watch to a compatible phone.
  • Settings and features provided by the Galaxy Wearable app are only available when your Galaxy Watch is connected to your mobile device.
  • Continued use of GPS running in the background can dramatically decrease battery life.
  • For any further help with the app, please visit Samsung’s help for Galaxy Wearable or contact Samsung. T-Mobile can only provide limited support for other developers’ applications. If you’re running into problems, check out our troubleshooting tips.

Settings & Tech Specs

Get to know your Samsung LTE Mobile Hotspot Pro
  • Notification bar: Shows information about the connection status, signal strength, battery level, and time, and displays notifications about incoming messages, and other action.
  • Display: Shows all the information needed to operate your device, such as the number of wireless connected devices, number of received messages (along with date, time and phone number), and data usage.
  • USB Connector: Provides a direct connection for USB-capable devices using this connector type.
  • Power key: Switches the phone off and on.
  • WPS key: Allows you to pair with devices currently using a WPS connection. The WPS (Wi-Fi Protected Setup) feature allows you to pair your Wi-Fi-capable device without the need for entering a passcode. This process is similar to Wi-Fi Direct pairing.
  • Charging Port: Allows you to connect a compatible power cable.
  • Mini USB Connector: Provides a mini USB for connection to devices using this type of connector.
  • microSD Card Slot (internal): Allows you use a microSD card to expand the memory of your device.
  • USB Connector: Provides a USB plug for connection to devices using this type of connector. This provides your target device with wired Internet access.

Format SD card

Formatting the SD card deletes all data on it. You may wish to format the SD card if you want to delete the files, if files or apps on the SD card are not working, or if the SD card is not working.

Open or delete files using the computer

You must use the USB cable that comes with your phone.

  • Connect the USB cord to the phone, then to a computer.
  • On your computer, select Open folder to view files > OK.
  • Another Removable Disk window will appear (one folder contains files saved in your phone memory and one folder contains files saved on your SD card). Select Open folder to view files > OK.
  • Locate the folder that contains files you want to delete.
  • Once you have located the files, right-select and select Delete.
  • When done, disconnect the USB cable.
Transfer files between computer & SD card

You must use the USB cable that comes with your phone to transfer files.

  • Connect the USB cord to the phone, then to a computer.
  • On your computer, select Open folder to view files > OK.
  • Another Removable Disk window will appear (one folder contains files saved in your phone memory and one folder contains files saved on your SD card). Select Open folder to view files > OK..
  • Locate the folder that contains files saved on your SD card.
  • Locate the file(s) you want to move on your computer.
  • Cut or copy and paste the desired file(s) from your computer to your SD card.
  • When done, disconnect the USB cable.
SIM card

  • Insert the battery, making sure to align the gold contacts.
  • Press down gently to secure the battery.
  • Position the battery cover over the battery compartment and press down firmly along the edges to snap it back into place.

Software Updates & Device Resets

Master reset from settings menu

A master reset restores the original factory settings and may delete your personal data on the internal storage, such as downloaded content, ringtones, images, apps, and contacts. It does not delete data stored on the SIM card or SD card.

  • The device will reboot automatically.
Master reset with hardware keys

A master reset restores the original factory settings and may delete your personal data on the internal storage, such as downloaded content, ringtones, images, apps, and contacts. It does not delete data stored on the SIM card or SD card. If the device menus are frozen or unresponsive, you can master reset using hardware keys.

  • Turn on the device.
  • Press and hold the Power and WPS keys for 5 seconds to display an on-screen Factory Reset message.
  • Press the Power key to reset the device. Otherwise, press the WPS key to cancel the reset operation.
  • Once completed, the device should reboot and the main screen will re-appear.
Software updates

Your device automatically updates to the latest software version. No additional action is required.

Set up a new T-Mobile device

Congratulations on your new purchase! Get steps to set up your new device and transfer data from the old one.

Set up without switching

First phone? Forgot to backup? We can still get you started!

  • If your device has an eSIM, check out Set up your eSIM for additional details on activating your device.
  • To get step-by-step instructions, choose your device and select Update & Backup > Out of box setup.

Switch to an Android

Android to Android

We recommend you transfer your data when directed during your device’s initial out-of-box setup process, that’s usually the easiest way. You might also check for a manufacturer’s app, like Samsung Smart Switch.

You can also use your Google account to switch from one Android device to another:

  • On your existing device from the Home screen, open the Settings app.
  • Navigate to the Google Backup section:
    • Samsung: Select Google Services > Manage Backup.
    • Other Android: Select System > Backup.
  • Make sure Photos, videos, and other device data is backed up.
    • If backup is off turn it on and wait for the device to back up the data.
    • If backup is on confirm the device recently backed up the data. If their data was not recently backed up, back up the device before proceeding.
  • Select Confirm.
  • On the new device from the Home screen, swipe up to view your Apps.
  • Transfer you data by choosing Settings > Accounts > Add Account > Google.
  • Sign in to your Google account where the data is backed up.
  • When asked if you would like to download the synced information, select Yes.
  • Depending on the amount of data backed up it may take a while to download. You must wait for the download to be complete.
Apple to Android
  • Apple iOS apps cannot be transferred to Android but you may be able to find similar apps in the Play Store.
  • For data transfer steps, review Switch to Android.
  • Activate the SIM card or eSIM for your new device. Check SIM card & eSIM for details.
  • Once complete, follow the setup wizard on the new device.

Switch to Apple iOS

Let’s set up your new Apple device.

Android to Apple
  • Use the Move to iOS app to move your data.
  • Android apps cannot be transferred to Apple devices but you may be able to find similar apps in the App Store.
  • You can install Google Photos (iPhone) and Google Photos (Android) on both devices for easy photo transfer.
  • Activate the SIM card or eSIM for your new device. Check SIM card & eSIM for details.
  • Once complete, follow the setup wizard on your new device.
Apple to Apple

Check out Apple.com for additional details.

  • Backup your data on the current device using iCloud. Temporary iCloud storage is available.
  • Make sure you know your Apple ID and Apple ID password. You’ll need them when setting up your new device.
  • Make sure your current device is connected to Wi-Fi and has Bluetooth on.
  • Turn on your new device and place it near your current device, then swipe up on the Hello screen.
  • On your current device, make sure the right Apple ID is showing on the pop-up and choose Continue.
  • Use your current device to scan the animation on your new device. Wait for a message that says Finish on New [Device].
  • On your new device, enter your current device password. If prompted, enter your Apple ID password.
  • Follow the instructions to set up Face ID or Touch ID on your new device.
  • If your old device used an eSIM, Transfer Cellular Plan will appear on your new device. Select the phone number to transfer and choose Continue.
  • Choose how you want to transfer your data and follow the on-screen steps:
    • Download from iCloud: Apps & data download in the background and you can use your device immediately. Temporary iCloud storage is available.
    • Transfer directly from previous device: You’ll need to wait for the transfer to complete before using your new device.
  • Follow the on-screen prompts to set up the following services:
    • Apple Pay
    • Cloud Drive
    • Siri
    • App Analytics
  • If you have an Apple Watch and you’re setting up a new iPhone, you’ll be asked if you’d like to transfer your Apple Watch.
  • Keep your devices near each other and plugged in to power until the iPhone data migration process is complete.
  • Once complete, select Continue on both devices.
  • If you’re using a physical SIM, either move your SIM card or transfer it to an eSIM.

Still need help?

To learn about additional features for your device, head to Tutorials, locate your device, and find the steps you need.

SIM card & eSIM

The SIM card or eSIM is your device’s ticket to the T-Mobile network!

On this page:

  • What’s a SIM card / eSIM?
  • Set up your SIM card
  • Buy a SIM card
  • Set up your eSIM
  • Get help with your eSIM
  • Watch our video on installing SIM cards

What’s a SIM card / eSIM?

SIM card
  • A SIM card is a small chip that contains information your device needs to connect to the T-Mobile network.
  • T-Mobile SIM cards come with adapters to allow for use with Nano, Micro, or Standard SIM sized devices.
eSIM
  • Embedded SIM (eSIM) is just a SIM card gone digital, so you don’t have to wait for a physical SIM.
  • Just download your eSIM over Wi-Fi and connect to the T-Mobile network in minutes!

Set up your SIM card

I’m a T-Mobile customer

If you’re an existing T-Mobile customer upgrading to a new device you’ll need to activate your new SIM first. New customers will have their SIMs shipped activated.

  • Make sure SIM Protection is disabled.

  • Open the T-Life app while you’re connected to the T-Mobile network.

  • Select the Manage tab and choose the line you want to change the SIM on.

  • Choose SIM transfer or activation > Get Started.

  • Enter the IMEI number for the device you’re transferring your SIM to, then select Continue.

  • Choose to activate a SIM card, then select Continue.

  • Enter the ICCID, then select Continue.

  • Review the requested change and select Activate.

  • If prompted, respond to the interactive SMS (iSMS) to confirm the change. Once you have your active SIM, follow these steps:

  • With the device off, open the SIM card tray and insert the SIM card.

    • For orders with multiple devices, use the order confirmation email to verify which SIM card goes in which device.
    • Here’s a short video to guide you through the process.

  • Turn the device on. Your service should be working.

    • If you’re bringing your own device from a different carrier or company and data isn’t working, add T-Mobile’s APN settings.
    • If you don’t have bars of signal, check out No Service Troubleshooting.

  • To transfer data from your old device, review Set up a new T-Mobile phone.

I’m a T-Mobile Home Internet customer

If you just signed up for T-Mobile Home Internet, the SIM card is already in your device and active! Check out T-Mobile Home Internet Support for information on device placement and setup.

If you’ve just replaced your Home Internet Gateway, you’ll need to remove the SIM card from your old gateway and insert it into the replacement. Check out Set up your T-Mobile Gateway & Network for information on replacement gateway set up.

Buy a SIM card

  • Postpaid: Review our SIM card page to order online. You can also find one in a T-Mobile store.
  • Prepaid: Review the Prepaid SIM Card page to order online. You can also stop by a store.

Set up your eSIM

  • If you’re upgrading or transferring service to a new device, make sure to turn off SIM Protection before following these steps. If you don’t, you’ll receive an error.
  • If you’re switching between Apple & Android or don’t have your old device, follow the steps for Other devices.
  • To activate a new Prepaid account, check out the T-Mobile Prepaid eSIM app.
Apple iPhone

There are a few ways to setup your eSIM:

  • During the initial setup, you’ll be prompted to activate an eSIM or transfer one from an existing iPhone.

  • If you’ve already set up your iPhone and are connected to Wi-Fi, your iPhone will prompt you when the T-Mobile Cellular Plan is ready to be installed.

  • Didn’t get a prompt or chose to activate later? You can activate your eSIM from the device Settings > Cellular.

  • Our Universal Tutorials have steps to activate your eSIM on supported devices. Transfer existing SIM from Google phone to Apple iPhone after initial setup

  • Confirm devices meet these requirements.

    • Current device: Google Pixel 10 series
    • New device: Apple iPhone 11 or newer running iOS 26 or higher
    • PIN / Password enabled
    • Bluetooth enabled
    • Not available for Government accounts

  • Place your new iPhone close to your current Google device.

  • On your new iPhone, select Settings > Cellular > Set Up Cellular. If you already have another SIM set up on your iPhone, select Add eSIM.

  • On ‘Transfer Your Phone Numbers screen’ select Other Options > Transfer from Android.

  • Scan the QR code with your current Google device.

  • On your Google device, select the line to transfer and confirm transfer.

  • After the transfer is complete, select Done on both devices.

Before you start

Make sure:

  • Your device is powered on and near your phone

  • Your device is connected to Bluetooth Initiate the eSIM download

If the download is successful, the screen will display a checkmark, and your Watch App Cellular Plan will show T-Mobile (Activating will disappear once download is complete). Your device will now connect to the T-Mobile network when it moves out of Bluetooth range.

Connections & network

Bluetooth

Turn on/off

  • From the home screen, press down on the Rotary Channel Knob to open the menu.

  • Scroll to Network, then select it.

  • Scroll to Bluetooth, then select it.

    • If it says ‘Click to ON’, press down on the Rotary Channel Knob to turn it on.
    • If it says ‘Click to OFF’, press down on the Rotary Channel Knob to turn it off. Pair device

  • From the home screen, press down on the Rotary Channel Knob to open the menu.

  • Scroll to Network, then select it.

  • Scroll to Bluetooth, then select it.

  • Make sure it says ‘Click to turn OFF’, then scroll to Pair Device and select it.

  • Scroll through the list of devices and select the one you want to pair.

  • Press down on the Rotary Channel Knob to start pairing.

  • Follow the on-screen instructions to complete pairing, including entering any requested PINs. Delete pairing

  • From the home screen, press down on the Rotary Channel Knob to open the menu.

  • Scroll to Network, then select it.

  • Scroll to Bluetooth, then select it.

  • Scroll to Paired Device, then select it.

  • Scroll through until you find the desired paired device, then select it.

  • Rotate the Rotary Channel Knob to the left to being unpairing.

  • Press down on the Rotary Channel Knob to confirm the unpairing.
