  • Scroll to VK7 Settings, then select it.
  • Adjust the following options:
    • Auto Shut Down (on/off)
    • Delay (30-90 minutes)
Date & Time
  • From the home screen, press down on the Rotary Channel Knob to open the menu.
  • Scroll to System, then select it.
  • Scroll to Date & Time, then select it.
  • Adjust the following options:
    • Format (12hr or 24hr)
    • Network Time (on/off)
Settings lock

Settings lock prevents a user from changing anything under Network, Location and System settings. It also prevents access to Developer mode.

  • From the home screen, press down on the Rotary Channel Knob to open the menu.
  • Scroll to System, then select it.
  • Scroll to Settings Lock, then select it.
  • Select Click to ON to turn it on and set the password.
  • Select Click to OFF to enter the password and turn it off.
Language
  • From the home screen, press down on the Rotary Channel Knob to open the menu.
  • Scroll to System, then select it.
  • Scroll to Language, then select it.
  • Choose your language:
    • English
    • Française
    • Español
Restart
  • From the home screen, press down on the Rotary Channel Knob to open the menu.
  • Scroll to About, then select it.
  • Scroll to Reboot, then select it.
Network reset
  • From the home screen, press down on the Rotary Channel Knob to open the menu.
  • Scroll to System, then select it.
  • Scroll to Reset Options, then select it.
  • Scroll to Network reset, then select it.
Factory Data Reset (Delete all)

Resetting all data removes the PTT app. Only perform this when directed by Siyata or Customer Support.

  • From the home screen, press down on the Rotary Channel Knob to open the menu.
  • Scroll to System, then select it.
  • Scroll to Reset Options, then select it.
  • Scroll to All Data then select it.
  • Click to confirm the reset.
Mobile Device Unlock

Twist the Rotary Channel Knob to scroll through options. Press it to select.

  • Contact us to request your Mobile Device Unlock PIN.
  • Insert a non-T-Mobile SIM card into the device and turn it on.
  • On the Network Locked screen, press the Rotary Channel Knob.
  • Enter the 8-digit unlock PIN, then select the check mark.

Software how-tos: TVision HUB

Use these steps to set up and manage settings for the TVision HUB. For issues and requests not listed on this page, check out AndroidTV Help​, as the HUB is an Android TV device.

On this page:

  • HUB / Android TV account
  • Google Assistant
  • Apps & games
  • Connections & network
  • Casting
  • Settings
  • Accessibility settings
  • Update & reset

HUB / AndroidTV account

  • Sync your media and activity across devices when you sign into a Google account on your HUB (which is an AndroidTV device).
  • Use multiple accounts in YouTube, the Play Store, and other Google services to keep separate watch histories.
  • These settings are specific to the TVision HUB on AndroidTV. These steps will not work with other AndroidTV manufacturer (such as Phillips).
  • This account is for your HUB device, not TVision service.
Sign in or add an account

On your HUB remote, press the Assistant button.

  • On your HUB, open Settings.
  • Select Accounts & Sign In > Add account.
  • Use the remote to enter your Google username and password. If you don’ t have a Google account, learn how to create one.
Change accounts

In certain apps, suggestions are based on viewing history. To get personalized results in Google apps, make sure you’re signed into the appropriate Google account. To switch accounts:

  • Open an app that uses your Google account, like YouTube or Play Store.
  • When the app opens, select your account. If the app does ask you to choose an account:
    • Open the app’s settings
    • Sign out of the current account.
    • Sign into the desired account. The next time you use the app, you can choose which account you want to use.
Sync account

‘Sync now’ will update the HUB device with any changes to the associated Google Account since the last sync.

  • Synced Google apps may include Calendar, Contacts, Google Play Movies and TV, Google Play Music, and People.
  • Syncing apps will improve recommendations and functionality of Google Assistant.
  • The User may disable use of this data for recommendations / Google Assistant by toggling the app to ‘disabled.’
  • To sync your account:
    • From the HUB Home screen, select Settings.
    • Under ‘Accounts & Sign In,’ select your account.
    • Select Sync now.
Remove / manage account
  • On your HUB, go to the Home screen.
  • Select the Settings icon.
  • Select Accounts & Sign In.
  • Select the account you want to manage, and choose from the following:
    • Sync now
    • Remove account
    • Choose apps to sync
      • Calendar
      • Contacts
      • Google Play Movies & TV
      • Google Play Music
      • People details

Google Assistant

  • You can ask questions and complete tasks on your TVision HUB.
  • The Google Assistant comes installed on your TVision HUB. You can turn it on during the initial setup, or later.
  • On the HUB, Google Assistant is available in English, French, German, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese (Brazilian), and Spanish. More languages coming soon!
  • Google Assistant only controls the settings for the device. It does not control settings for the TVision Mobile app. To control settings for the app, review Smart TVs and TV-Connected devices: TVision app.
  • Before you begin, check for updates, review Update & reset.
Talk to your Assistant
  • On your HUB remote, press the Assistant button, then ask your question.
  • To make sure the Assistant can hear you, speak into the microphone on your remote.
  • To do more with the Assistant on your HUB:
    • Ask the Assistant “What can you do?”
    • On your phone, download the Assistant app.
Manage Google Assistant settings
  • From the HUB Home screen, select Settings.
  • Select Device Preferences > Google Assistant to manage the following:
    • Accounts
    • View permissions
    • Searchable apps
    • SafeSearch filter (on / off)
    • Block offensive words (on / off)
SafeSearch and Block Offensive Words
  • SafeSearch and Block Offensive Words can help you block inappropriate or explicit images from your Google Search results when using Google Assistant to search.
  • These filters aren’t 100% accurate, but they help you avoid most adult content. Learn more about how SafeSearch works.
  • To turn on SafeSearch / Block Offensive Words:
    • From the HUB Home screen, select Settings.
    • Select Device Preferences > Google Assistant.
    • Toggle the SafeSearch or Block Offensive Words filter on or off.
Enable Carrier Billing
  • T-Mobile Android phone users can set up T-Mobile billing as their default billing on their device.
  • Sign into the TVision HUB using the same Google username and password.
  • Google recognizes the user’s preferences and sets T-Mobile carrier billing as the default billing on the user’s Android TV.
  • Google password authentication is required for purchases.

Apps & games

You can get apps and games for your HUB through the Play Store app.

Get apps & games
  • From the HUB Home screen, select Apps.
  • Select the Play Games app.
  • Select an app or game.
    • To purchase a free app or game, select Install.
    • To purchase a paid app or game, select the game’s price and follow the instructions to complete your purchase.
    • Paid games require adding a payment method. Review Google Play Help: Add, remove, or edit your payment method or contact Google support for questions and steps on setting up Google Play payment methods.
Manage apps
  • From the HUB Home screen, select Settings.
  • Select Apps > See all apps.
  • Select the desired app, then select from the list of actions:
    • Force stop
    • Uninstall
    • Clear data
    • Clear cache
    • Clear defaults
    • Notifications (on / off)
    • Permissions
      • Contacts (on / off)
      • Location (on / off)
      • Microphone (on / off)
      • Phone (on / off)
      • SMS (on / off)
Play a game
  • From the HUB Home screen, go to the “Games” row.
  • Find and select the game you want to play.
Find a previously downloaded app or game in your TV settings
  • From the HUB Home screen, select Settings.
  • Select Apps.
Find a previously downloaded app or game in the Google Play Store
  • On your HUB, select the Play Store.
  • Select My Apps.
  • Under “Apps installed,” select the app, then select Open.
Delete an app or game in your TV settings
  • From the HUB Home screen, select Settings.
  • Select Apps.
  • Select the app you want to delete (select See all apps for a complete list).
  • Select Uninstall > OK.
Delete an app or game from the Google Play Store
  • On your HUB, select the Play Store.
  • Find the app or game you want to delete.
  • Select Uninstall. If you don’t want an app to show in the top row of the HUB Home screen, turn off notification for that app.
    • Go to Settings > Apps.
    • Select the app.
    • Select Notifications > Off.
Update an app or game
  • On your HUB, open the Play Store.
  • Choose My Apps.
  • Under “Updates available,” you’ll find apps that can be updated. Select the app you wish to update, or select Update all.
Enable auto-update
  • On your HUB, open the Play Store.
  • Choose My Apps.
  • Select Open settings > Auto-update apps.
HUB app management (force stop, clear data, clear cache, clear defaults, notifications)
  • From the HUB Home screen, go to Settings.
  • Select Apps > See all apps.
  • Select the desired app, then select from the list of actions:
    • Force stop
    • Uninstall
    • Clear data
    • Clear Cache
    • Clear defaults
    • Notifications (on / off)
    • Permissions
      • Contacts (on / off)
      • Location (on / off)
      • Microphone (on / off)
      • Phone (on / off)
      • SMS (on / off)
Authentication settings

Authentication is required for all digital content purchases through Google Play (including within apps) by default.

  • Every time you authenticate for a purchase, you can continue to buy all forms of digital content through Google Play (including apps) for the next 30 minutes without authenticating again.
  • Disabling authentication may result in unauthorized purchases. You assume responsibility for all charges, including unintended or unauthorized purchases.
  • Authentication is always required for every purchase under the Family section for an app or game, even if you have your settings set differently.
  • Authentication settings apply only to the active account on the device where you add them. If you use your Google Account on more than one device, repeat the steps for each device. If you use multiple accounts on your device, repeat the steps for each account on the device.
  • To turn authentication on / off:
    • Hold the Home button on the HUB remote.
    • Select Settings.
    • Select Purchase authorization.
    • Choose a setting and follow the on-screen instructions.

Connections & network

Pair a Bluetooth Device

You can connect wireless keyboards, game controllers, and other devices to your HUB. To pair Bluetooth devices:

  • Hold the Home button on the HUB remote.
  • Select Settings.
  • Under “Remote and accessories,” select Add accessory.
  • On your TV or monitor, select your device from the list.
    • Your TV will display a list of nearby devices available for pairing.
    • If your device isn’t listed, put your device in pairing mode and it will be added to the on-screen list.
Manage network connection

“Network & Internet” settings allow the user to enable / disable Wi-Fi for the TVision HUB, scan and select the preferred Wi-Fi network, and view the settings and signal strength for the connected network.

  • On your remote, press the Home button.
  • Select the Settings icon.
  • Select Network & Internet.
  • Toggle Wi-Fi on.
  • Under “Available networks,” select the network you wish to connect to.
  • Enter the password and select the enter icon.
Forget a network
  • On your remote, press the Home button.
  • Select the Settings icon.
  • Select Network & Internet.
  • Select the desired network.
  • Select Forget Network.
Check network connection

Use the TVision Network & Diagnosis tool to monitor network speeds.

  • On your remote, press the Home button.
  • Select TVision Network & Diagnosis (select See all Apps if TVision Network & Diagnosis does not appear on the Home page).
  • Select Network Speed to check the current network speeds or select Network Detection to check current network status.

Casting

  • If you have a HUB, you can cast content from phones, tablets or laptops to your TV. If you don’t have a HUB, learn how to cast content to other TVs.
  • You can only cast from the latest version of a Chromecast-enabled app or a Chrome browser on a device connected to the same Wi-Fi network as the HUB.
To cast content from your device to your TV…
  • Connect your device to the same Wi-Fi network as your HUB.
  • Open the app that has the content you want to cast.
  • In the app, find and select the Cast icon.
  • On your device, select the name of your TV.
  • When the Cast icon changes color, you’re successfully connected. To stop casting, on your device select the Cast icon, then Disconnect.

Settings

Display

Display settings control the display format of the signal sent to the HUB. The display format is also dependent on the capabilities of the TV and the content being displayed. To view and manage Display settings:

  • From the HUB Home screen, select Settings.
  • Select Device Preferences > ​More > Display to view and manage the following:
    • Screen resolution
      • Auto switch to best resolution (on / off)
      • Display Mode (setting for the resolution and refresh rate of the signal sent to the TV)
      • Color Depth Settings (determines the number of colors on a screen. Increasing color depth increases the colors rendered)
      • Color Space Settings (determines color model encoding format for rendering color on the display)
    • Screen position (controls the scaling of display screen)
      • Zoom in screen
      • Zoom out screen
Home screen
  • The Home screen is the main HUB interface, and is accessed from the Home button on the remote.
  • The Customize channels setting allows the user to control the channels displayed on the Home screen.
  • Channels are the rows of content displayed on the Home screen, such as:
    • Apps (can’t be removed)
    • Netflix (can’t be removed)
    • Google Play Music
    • YouTube
Screen saver

Use these settings to put the TVision HUB into screen saver and sleep (power-saving) modes when the HUB is inactive.

  • From the HUB Home screen, select Settings.
  • Select Device Preferences > Screen Saver to view and manage the following:
    • Screen Saver
      • Turn screen off
      • Backdrop
      • Colors
    • When to start
      • 5 minutes
      • 15 minutes
      • 30 minutes
      • 1 hour
      • 2 hours
    • Put device to sleep
      • 30 minutes
      • 1 hour
      • 3 hours
      • 6 hours
      • 12 hours
      • Never
    • Start now
Keyboard

Keyboard settings control the keyboard layout and functionality for Apps that require keyboard entry. To adjust keyboard settings:

  • From the HUB Home screen, select Settings.
  • Select Device Preferences > Keyboard.
  • Select from the available options to update settings:
    • Current keyboard
    • Gboard Settings
      • Current version
      • Languages (defaults to system language)
      • Terms of service
      • Privacy policy
      • Open source licenses
      • Share usage statistics
    • Manage keyboards
      • Gboard (requires a connected Gboard)
      • Google voice typing (on / off)
      • Virtual Remote Keyboard
Surround Sound Audio Output

Audio Output settings control the audio format of the signal sent to the TV / display. The audio format is also dependent upon the capabilities of the TV and the content being viewed. To view and manage Audio Output:

  • From the HUB Home screen, select Settings.
  • Select Device Preferences > More > Audio Output to view and manage the following:
    • Dolby sounds
      • Off
      • Line
      • RF
    • Audio Mixing (on / off)
    • Digital Audio Format
      • PCM
      • SPDIF
      • AUTO
      • Manual (for definition of audio modes, review theSound section on this page)
        • Dolby Atmos in Dolby Digital Plus (Pass through)
        • Dolby Digital
        • Dobly Digital Plus
        • DTS (Pass through)
        • DTS-HD (Pass through)
        • AAC
        • Dobly TrueHD (Pass through)
Sound
  • Sound settings control the system sounds (selections and alerts) that occur as the user navigates through the screens and menus.
  • The output sound formats require support of the TVision HUB and the connected TV or sound system. Auto is the recommended setting.
  • To update Sound settings:
    • From the HUB Home screen, select Settings.
    • Select Device Preferences > Sound.
    • Select from the available options to update settings:
      • System sounds (on / off)
      • Select formats
        • Auto: Use the formats that your device supports (recommended)
        • None
        • Manual
          • Dolby Atmos in Dolby Digital Plus (Pass through)
            • 9.1 surround sound via Dolby Digital Plus stream (lower bitrate)
            • 9.1 => 9 speakers, 1 sub-woofer
          • Dolby Digital
            • 5.1 surround sound
            • 5.1 => 5 speakers, 1 sub-woofer
          • Dolby Digital Plus
            • 7.1 surround sound
            • 7.1 => 7 speakers, 1 sub-woofer
          • DTS (Pass through)
            • 5.1 surround sound (this is an alternate 5.1 surround sound standard, different than Dolby’s)
            • 5.1 => 5 speakers, 1 sub-woofer
          • DTS-HD (Pass through)
            • 7.1 surround sound (this is an alternate 7.1 surround sound standard, different than Dolby’s)
            • 7.1 => 7 speakers, 1 sub-woofer
          • AAC
            • 5.1 surround sound
            • 5.1 => 5 speakers, 1 sub-woofer
          • Dolby TrueHD (Pass through)
            • Supports up to 7.1 surround sound, as well as Dolby Atmos (9.1) immersive audio. Support for Dolby Atmos requires Dolby Atmos data embedded in the content being streamed.
            • 7.1 => 7 speakers, 1 sub-woofer
HDMI CEC

HDMI CEC settings allow the HUB device to control the TV input and power. This feature may not be supported by all TV models. To view and manage HDMI CEC settings:

  • From the HUB Home screen, select Settings.
  • Select Device Preferences > More > HDMI-CEC to view and manage the following:
    • CEC Switch (on / off)
      • When enabled in this setting and supported by the TV, this feature allows the TV remote to control the TVision HUB power on / off, volume, and D-pad.
      • Some, but not all of these functions may work on some TVs (e.g., you can control power, but not volume).
      • May not work for all TV models.
    • One key play (on / off)
      • When enabled and supported by the TV, powering on the TVision HUB or pressing the Home button will automatically switch the TV input to the TVision HUB and the TVision Home screen.
      • Example: If a TV is set for an Xbox on TV Input 2, pressing the TVision Home or Power button will automatically switch the TV Input to TVision on Input 1.
      • May not work for all TV models.
    • One key power off (on / off)
      • Powering off the TVision HUB will power off the TV when this feature is enabled.
      • May not work for all TV models.
Date & time

Date & time settings control date and time source, time zone, and formatting. To edit Date & time settings:

  • From the HUB Home screen, select Settings.
  • Select Device Preferences > Date & time.
  • Select the desired setting to update:
    • Automatic date & time
    • Set date (available if Automatic date & time is off)
    • Set time (available if Automatic date & time is off)
    • Set time zone
    • Use 24-hour format
Language

Language settings control the displayed language for the TVision HUB’s Settings menu. Use of this setting will vary by apps outside of the TVision HUB’s Settings menu. To update Language settings:

  • From the HUB Home screen, select Settings.
  • Select Device Preferences > Language.
  • Select from the list of available languages.
Location

Location enables / disables periodic reporting of HUB device location data to Google. Google may collect location data periodically and use this data in an anonymous way to improve accuracy and location-based services. To manage Location settings:

  • From the HUB Home screen, select Settings.
  • Select Device Preferences > Location > Location status to view and manage the following:
    • Use Wi-Fi to estimate locattion
    • Off
About Device

The About Device section allows users to check for system updates and factory reset the HUB device. About Device also provides information including model, versions, serial number, and interface addresses (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, IP). To view and manage About Device information:

  • From the HUB Home screen, select Settings.
  • Select Device Preferences > Storage to view and manage the following:
    • System Update
    • Device name
    • Restart
    • Status
      • IP Address
      • WiFi Mac address
      • Bluetooth address
      • Serial number
      • Up time
    • Legal information (legal documentation and license information provided by Google. Includes OPT-OUT setting for personalized advertising in Legal information > Ads > Opt out of Ads Personalization)
    • Model
    • Version
    • Android security path level
    • Kernal version
    • Build
    • SELinux status
    • Netflix ESN
    • TVision SW Version
Storage

Use Storage settings to view usage for apps, photos, videos, audio, downloads, and cached data. You can can remove apps and clear cache as needed (the TVision app can’t be deleted).

  • From the HUB Home screen, select Settings.
  • Select Device Preferences > Storage.
  • Select Internal shared storage to view storage information for the following:
    • Apps
    • Photos & videos
    • Audio
    • Downloads
    • Cached data (clears all cached data)
    • Misc.
    • Available

Accessibility settings

You can use the built-in screen reader, closed captions, and your phone to make your HUB experience more accessible.

Enable screen reader

When you use a screen reader, you can hear what’s happening on your TV or monitor (you may need sighted assistance to turn on the screen reader). To turn on the screen reader:

  • From the HUB Home screen, select Settings.
  • Select Device Preferences.
  • Select > Accessibility > Talkback > Enable.
Change screen reader volume & pitch
  • From the HUB Home screen, select Settings.
  • Select Device Preferences.
  • Select Accessibility > Talkback > Configuration.
  • Choose one of the following options:
    • Speech volume
    • Verbosity
    • Speak passwords
    • Sound feedback
    • Sound feedback volume
    • Audio ducking
Closed captions

The following steps will enable closed captions for the TVision app and some other apps. Some apps (like YouTube) may require you to update the settings within that app as well.

  • From the HUB Home screen, select Settings.
  • Select Device Preferences.
  • Select Accessibility > Captions.
  • Choose one of the following options:
    • Display (on / off)
    • Select Language
    • Text size
    • Caption style
Enable Accessibility shortcut

When the shortcut is on, you can press both the back and down buttons on the remote control for 3 seconds to start an accessibility feature. To enable the Accessibility shortcut:

  • From the HUB Home screen, select Settings.
  • Select Device Preferences.
  • Select Accessibility > Accessibility shortcut > Enable accessibility shortcut.
  • Select the shortcut service (either Talkback or Switch Access).
Switch Access

Switch Access scans the items on your screen, highlighting each item in turn, until you make a selection. To use Switch Access, you’ll first need one or more switches. There are several kinds of switches:

  • Use an external switch: A switch is a device that sends a keystroke signal to your Android device. Several companies sell these devices, such as AbleNet, Enabling Devices, RJ Cooper, and Tecla. These devices connect to your Android device via USB or Bluetooth (Google does not endorse these companies or their products).
  • Use an external keyboard: You can configure a standard USB or Bluetooth keyboard to work as a switch device by assigning one or more of its keys to actions.
  • To turn on Switch Access:
    • From the HUB Home screen, select Settings.
    • Select Device Preferences.
    • Select Accessibility > Switch Access > Enable.

Update & reset

  • A factory data reset will erase all data from the TVision HUB’s internal storage, including:
    • Associated Google accounts
    • System and app data and settings
    • User downloaded apps
  • After the factory reset, the user will need to complete the install process, including pairing the remote and signing into Google and TVision accounts.
Factory data reset the TVision HUB in settings
  • Select the Settings icon.
  • Select Device Preferences > Reset.
  • Confirm you want to reset your device.
Factory data reset the TVision HUB with the power button
  • Press and hold the button on the side of the TVision HUB device for 15 seconds, then release the button.
  • Using the remote, select Reset > Erase everything. If the remote is not working;
    • Navigate to Reset by short-pressing the power button on the side of the TVision HUB.
    • Select Reset > Erase everything by long-pressing the power button on the side of the TVision HUB.
Restart device
  • On your HUB, open Settings.
  • Select Device Preferences > About > Restart.
  • Once the system restarts, play your video, music, or game again.
Update firmware
  • On your HUB, open Settings.
  • Select Device Preferences > About > Build. If the build is PI.4795, your device is using the most current software.
  • Select System update > Software update.
    • If your system needs an update, select Download.
    • If you don’t need an update, a “Your system is up to date” message displays.
Enter Safe mode
  • Hold the OK button for 2 seconds.
  • Select Restart.
Exit Safe mode
  • On your HUB, open Settings.
  • Select Device Preferences > About > Restart.

  • Authentication is always required for every purchase in the Family section for an app or game, even if you have your settings set differently.
  • Authentication settings apply only to the active account on the device where you add them. If you use your Google Account on more than one device, repeat the steps to turn authentication on/off for each device. If you use multiple accounts on your device, repeat the steps for each account on the device.
  • To turn authentication on/off:
    • Hold the Home button on the HUB remote.
    • Select Settings from the on-screen menu.
    • Select Accounts & Sign In.
    • Select your active or desired account.
    • Select Payment & Purchases.
    • Choose your desired purchase authentication preference.

Connections & network

Pair a Bluetooth Device

You can connect wireless keyboards, game controllers, and other devices to your HUB. To pair Bluetooth devices:

  • Hold the Home button on the HUB remote.
  • Select Settings from the on-screen menu.
  • Int the Remote and accessories section, select Add accessory.
  • On your TV or monitor, select your device from the list.
    • Your TV will display a list of nearby devices available for pairing.
    • If your device isn’t listed, put your device in pairing mode and it will be added to the on-screen list.
Manage network connection

“Network & Internet” settings allow the user to enable/disable Wi-Fi for the TVision HUB, scan and select the preferred Wi-Fi network, and review the settings and signal strength for the connected network.

  • Hold the Home button on the HUB remote.
  • Select Settings from the on-screen menu.
  • Select Network & Internet.
  • Toggle Wi-Fi on.
  • In the Available networks section, select the network you wish to connect to.
  • Enter the password and select the enter icon.
Forget a network
  • Hold the Home button on the HUB remote.
  • Select Settings from the on-screen menu.
  • Select Network & Internet.
  • Select the desired network.
  • Select Forget Network.
Check network connection

Use the TVision Network & Diagnosis tool to monitor network speeds.

  • On your remote, press the Home button.
  • Select TVision Network & Diagnosis (select See all Apps if TVision Network & Diagnosis does not appear on the Home page).
  • Select Network Speed to check the current network speeds or select Network Detection to check current network status.

Casting

  • If you have a HUB, you can cast content from phones, tablets or laptops to your TV. If you don’t have a HUB, learn how to cast content to other TVs.
  • You can only cast from the latest version of a Chromecast-enabled app or a Chrome browser on a device connected to the same Wi-Fi network as the HUB.
To cast content from your device to your TV…
  • Connect your device to the same Wi-Fi network as your HUB.
  • Open the app that has the content you want to cast.
  • In the app, find and select the Cast icon.
  • On your device, select the name of your TV.
  • When the Cast icon changes color, you’re successfully connected. To stop casting, on your device select the Cast icon, then Disconnect.

Settings

Display

Display settings control the display format of the signal sent to the HUB. The display format is also dependent on the capabilities of the TV and the content being displayed. To access and manage Display settings:

  • Hold the Home button on the HUB remote.
  • Select Settings from the on-screen menu.
  • Select Display & Sound > ​Advanced display settings for the following options:
    • Allow game mode: on/off
    • Dynamic range & Color format
    • Screen resolution
      • Auto switch to best resolution (on / off)
    • Zoom in screen
      • Screen position (controls the scaling of display screen)
      • Zoom out screen
Home screen
  • The Home screen is divided into 7 tabs: Search, For You, Live, Movies, Shows, Apps, and Library.
  • Using the Home button on the HUB remote will take you to the For You tab where you can find your apps and recommended content from all services.
  • The Live, Movies, and Shows tabs will isolate content from that specific type of media and will feature personalized recommendations.
  • The Apps tab is where users can search for new apps to download and receive additional app recommendations from the Google Play Store.
  • The Library tab will source all content that you have added to your watchlist (on HUB or the Google TV mobile app) as well as owned content connected to your Google account, movies anywhere, and your YouTube TV DVR.
  • Selecting the profile picture will open a panel for settings and other notifications. To quickly access this panel, hole the Home button on the HUB remote.
Screen saver

Use these settings to put the TVision HUB into screen saver and sleep (power-saving) modes when the HUB is inactive.

  • Hold the Home button on the HUB remote.
  • Select Settings from the on-screen menu.
  • Select System > Ambient Mode to access and manage screensaver settings
Keyboard

Keyboard settings control the keyboard layout and functionality for Apps that require keyboard entry. To adjust keyboard settings:

  • Hold the Home button on the HUB remote.
  • Select Settings from the on-screen menu.
  • Select System > Keyboard.
  • Select from the available options to update settings:
    • Current keyboard
    • Gboard Settings
      • Current version
      • Languages (defaults to system language)
      • Terms of service
      • Privacy policy
      • Open source licenses
      • Share usage statistics
    • Manage keyboards
      • Gboard (requires a connected Gboard)
      • Google voice typing (on / off)
      • Virtual Remote Keyboard
Surround Sound Audio Output

Audio Output settings control the audio format of the signal sent to the TV / display. The audio format is also dependent upon the capabilities of the TV and the content being viewed. To access and manage Audio Output settings:

  • Hold the Home button on the HUB remote.
  • Select Settings from the on-screen menu.
  • Select Display & Sound > Advanced sound settings to review and manage the surround sound format with either automatic detection, or a manual option
System Sounds

System sound settings control the system sounds that occur as the user navigates through the screens and menus.

  • Hold the Home button on the HUB remote.
  • Select Settings from the on-screen menu.
  • Select Display & Sound.
  • Navigate to System Sounds and select OK on the remote to toggle on/off.
HDMI CEC

HDMI CEC settings allow the HUB device to control the TV input and power. This feature may not be supported by all TV models. To access and manage HDMI CEC settings:

  • Hold the Home button on the HUB remote.
  • Select Settings from the on-screen menu.
  • Select Display & Sound.
  • Select HDMI-CEC to review and manage the following:
    • CEC Switch (on / off)
      • When enabled in this setting and supported by the TV, this feature allows the TV remote to control the TVision HUB power on / off, volume, and D-pad.
      • Some, but not all of these functions may work on some TVs (e.g., you can control power, but not volume).
      • May not work for all TV models.
    • One key play (on / off)
      • When enabled and supported by the TV, powering on the TVision HUB or pressing the Home button will automatically switch the TV input to the TVision HUB and the TVision Home screen.
      • Example: If a TV is set for an Xbox on TV Input 2, pressing the TVision Home or Power button will automatically switch the TV Input to TVision on Input 1.
      • May not work for all TV models.
    • One key power off (on / off)
      • Powering off the TVision HUB will power off the TV when this feature is enabled.
      • May not work for all TV models.
Date & time

Date & time settings control date and time source, time zone, and formatting. To edit Date & time settings:

  • Hold the Home button on the HUB remote.
  • Select Settings from the on-screen menu.
  • Select System > Date & time.
  • Select the desired setting to update:
    • Automatic date & time
    • Set date (available if Automatic date & time is off)
    • Set time (available if Automatic date & time is off)
    • Set time zone
    • Use 24-hour format
Language

Language settings control the displayed language for the TVision HUB’s Settings menu. Use of this setting will vary by apps outside of the TVision HUB’s Settings menu. To update Language settings:

  • Hold the Home button on the HUB remote.
  • Select Settings from the on-screen menu.
  • Select System > Language.
  • Select from the list of available languages.
Location

Location enables / disables periodic reporting of HUB device location data to Google. Google may collect location data periodically and use this data in an anonymous way to improve accuracy and location-based services. To manage Location settings:

  • Hold the Home button on the HUB remote.
  • Select Settings from the on-screen menu.
  • Select Privacy > Location to access and manage the following:
    • Location status: Use Wi-Fi to estimate location
    • Scanning always available: on/off
About Device

The About Device section allows users to check for system updates and factory reset the HUB device. About Device also provides information including model, versions, serial number, and interface addresses (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, IP). To access and manage About Device information:

  • Hold the Home button on the HUB remote.
  • Select Settings from the on-screen menu.
  • Select System > About to review and manage the following:
    • System Update
    • Device name
    • Reset
    • Status
      • IP Address
      • WiFi Mac address
      • Bluetooth address
      • Serial number
      • Up time
    • Legal information (legal documentation and license information provided by Google. Includes OPT-OUT setting for personalized advertising in Legal information > Ads > Opt out of Ads Personalization)
    • Model
    • Version
    • Android security path level
    • Kernal version
    • Build
    • SELinux status
    • Netflix ESN
    • TVision SW Version
Storage

Use Storage settings to get usage for apps, photos, videos, audio, downloads, and cached data. You can ve apps and clear cache as needed (the TVision app can’t be deleted).

  • Hold the Home button on the HUB remote.
  • Select Settings from the on-screen menu.
  • Select System > Storage.
  • Select Internal shared storage to access storage information for the following:
    • Apps
    • Photos & videos
    • Audio
    • Downloads
    • Cached data (clears all cached data)
    • Misc.
    • Available

Accessibility settings

You can use the built-in screen reader, closed captions, and your phone to make your HUB experience more accessible.

Enable screen reader

When you use a screen reader, you can hear what’s happening on your TV or monitor (you may need sighted assistance to turn on the screen reader). To turn on the screen reader:

  • Hold the Home button on the HUB remote.
  • Select Settings from the on-screen menu.
  • Select System > Accessibility > Talkback > Enable.
Change screen reader volume & pitch
  • Hold the Home button on the HUB remote.
  • Select Settings from the on-screen menu.
  • Select System.
  • Select Accessibility > Talkback > Configuration.
  • Choose one of the following options:
    • Speech volume
    • Verbosity
    • Speak passwords
    • Sound feedback
    • Sound feedback volume
    • Audio ducking
Closed captions

The following steps will enable closed captions for the TVision app and some other apps. Some apps (like YouTube) may require you to update the settings within that app as well.

  • Hold the Home button on the HUB remote.
  • Select Settings from the on-screen menu.
  • Select System.
  • Select Accessibility > Captions.
  • Choose one of the following options:
    • Display (on / off)
    • Select Language
    • Text size
    • Caption style
Enable Accessibility shortcut

When the shortcut is on, you can press both the back and down buttons on the remote control for 3 seconds to start an accessibility feature. To enable the Accessibility shortcut:

  • Hold the Home button on the HUB remote.
  • Select Settings from the on-screen menu.
  • Select System.
  • Select Accessibility > Accessibility shortcut > Enable accessibility shortcut.
  • Select the shortcut service (either Talkback or Switch Access).
Switch Access

Switch Access scans the items on your screen, highlighting each item in turn, until you make a selection. To use Switch Access, you’ll first need one or more switches. There are several kinds of switches:

  • Use an external switch: A switch is a device that sends a keystroke signal to your Android device. Several companies sell these devices, such as AbleNet, Enabling Devices, RJ Cooper, and Tecla. These devices connect to your Android device via USB or Bluetooth (Google does not endorse these companies or their products).
  • Use an external keyboard: You can configure a standard USB or Bluetooth keyboard to work as a switch device by assigning one or more of its keys to actions.
  • To turn on Switch Access:
    • Hold the Home button on the HUB remote.
    • Select Settings from the on-screen menu.
    • Select System.
    • Select Accessibility > Switch Access > Enable.

Update & reset

  • A factory data reset will erase all data from the TVision HUB’s internal storage, including:
    • Associated Google accounts
    • System and app data and settings
    • User downloaded apps
  • After the factory reset, the user will need to complete the install process, including pairing the remote and signing into Google and TVision accounts.
Factory data reset the TVision HUB in settings
  • Press and hold the home button on the HUB remote
  • Select settings from the on-screen menu
  • Select System >About > Reset.
  • Confirm you want to reset your device.
Factory data reset the TVision HUB with the power button
  • Press and hold the button on the side of the TVision HUB device for 15 seconds, then release the button.
  • Using the remote, select Reset > Erase everything. If the remote is not working;
    • Navigate to Reset by short-pressing the power button on the side of the TVision HUB.
    • Select Reset > Erase everything by long-pressing the power button on the side of the TVision HUB.
Restart device
  • Hold the Home button on the HUB remote.
  • Select Settings from the on-screen menu.
  • Select System > Restart.
  • Once the system restarts, play your video, music, or game again.
Update firmware
  • Hold the Home button on the HUB remote.
  • Select Settings from the on-screen menu.
  • Select System > About > System update.
    • If your system needs an update, select Download.
    • If you don’t need an update, a “Your system is up to date” message displays.

Set up your SyncUP DRIVE device

Insert/remove SIM card

Depending on your model, you may not be able to remove your SIM card.

Embedded SIM

If your device has an embedded SIM card, it cannot be removed. You can find the SIM card number on the device label, next to ICCID.

Physical SIM card (SyncUP DRIVE 6200 and 6500 only)
  • Insert the tip of the tray eject tool to eject the SIM card tray.
  • Place the micro-SIM card on the tray with the gold-colored contacts facing down and slide the tray back into place.
Install the SyncUP DRIVE (OBD2) device

While the device can be used in multiple cars, it can only be connected to one account at a time.

  • Check that the car is compatible with the vehicle compatibility tool.
  • Download and install T-Life on your phone on the Apple App Store or Google Play Store.
  • Add your SyncUP DRIVE to T-Life.
  • Make sure your vehicle is parked outside in a safe location and the engine is turned off. Do not insert or remove the SyncUP DRIVE unless the vehicle is off.
  • Connect your OBD2 device to the OBD connector port.
    • The OBD (On-Board Diagnostics) connector is usually located on or under the dashboard, on the driver’s side.
    • Do not force your OBD2 device into the port as this can damage the device.
  • Start the engine and go for a drive.
  • Wait as your OBD2 device searches for and connects to the T-Mobile network. It may take 5-10 minutes to connect on the first use.
  • Connect your phone or other devices to your network.
    • Use your normal Wi-Fi application to connect to the wireless network.
    • Select the Wi-Fi network name.
    • Enter the Wi-Fi network password. (The default is the last 8 digits of the IMEI.)
Cellular network settings (SyncUP DRIVE 6200 and 6500 only)
Manual network selection
  • Connect to the SyncUP DRIVE hotspot over Wi-Fi.
  • Open your browser and go to http://192.168.0.1 .
  • Log in as Administrator. (The default Admin login is admin.)
  • Select Settings > Network Settings.
  • In ‘Network Selection,’ choose Automatic or Manual.
  • Select Apply.
Data roaming
  • Connect to the SyncUP DRIVE hotspot over Wi-Fi.
  • Open your browser and go to http://192.168.0.1 .
  • Log in as Administrator. (The default Admin login is admin.)
  • Select Settings > Network Settings.
  • In ‘WAN Connection Mode Settings,’ select Check here to connect to internet in the roaming status to enable/disable.
  • Select Apply.
APN settings
  • Connect to the SyncUP DRIVE hotspot over Wi-Fi.
  • Open your browser and go to http://192.168.0.1 .
  • Log in as Administrator. (The default Admin login is admin.)
  • Select Settings > Network Settings.
  • Select Manual in the APN section.
  • Select Add New.
  • Enter the following details:
    • Name
    • Authentication mode
    • Username & Password
Mobile Device Unlock

SyncUP DRIVE is locked to the T-Mobile network and cannot be unlocked to use on other networks.

Add SyncUP DRIVE to T-Life
  • Log in to the T-Life app.

    • QR Code: Use the camera on your phone to scan the QR code on the back of the Tracker.

If you select a real time vehicle notification, you’ll be taken to the T-Life app. You may need to log in before selecting Locate to view the event.

Customize notification settings

Vehicle health

Roadside Assistance with AAA

T-Mobile and AAA provide on-demand access to a 24/7 toll-free hotline and roadside assistance.

Reset (SyncUP DRIVE 6200 and 6500 only)

Reset the SyncUP DRIVE (OBD2) device when you’re transferring it to a new owner to delete any information and reset the settings to default.

On the device
  • Insert a pin into the Reset hole.
  • Hold for three seconds or until the LED1 indicator turns red.
On the Hotspot Administrator page
  • Connect to the SyncUP DRIVE hotspot over Wi-Fi.
  • Open your browser and enter the URL: http://192.168.0.1.
  • Log in as Administrator (the default Admin login is admin.)
  • Select Settings > Device Settings.
  • Select Reset.

Troubleshoot issues with SyncUP DRIVE

For your SyncUP DRIVE device to work, make sure:

The vehicle is compatible​ with SyncUP.

The SyncUP DRIVE device has a SIM card and is set up.

You’ve waited at least 15 minutes after setup, and taken your car on a drive.

If all of that checks out, then:

  • Turn off the vehicle, and unplug the device from the OBD port.
  • Plug the device back into the OBD port, and restart the vehicle.
  • Check the LED light shows a connection. Make sure the care is outside in an area it can get a signal.
    • Solid red: The device has power, but no cellular connection.
    • Solid green: The device is connected to cellular data and GPS.
    • Blinking green: The device is not yet connected to the cellular network or GPS network.
  • If you still have a problem, contact us to look into things on your account.

About SyncUP TRACKER

Getting started

For help setting up your SyncUP TRACKER, check out our video:

&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;nbsp;

Key features
  • Location Tracking: Check the last known location on a map and get near real-time location tracking, even when you’re miles away.
  • Virtual Boundaries: Set virtual geofenced boundaries to get notified when it leaves the selected area so you can quickly react.
  • Ring When Lost: Easily locate an item that’s nearby, but not in plain sight.
  • Location History: Check where your tracker has been for up to 2 weeks. Includes stationary trip history.
  • Directions to Tracker: Get directions to the Tracker’s current location from your location.
  • Motion Alert: Be notified when the Tracker moves.
  • Water and Dust Resistant: IP67 rated stands up to dust, water and drops.
  • Rechargeable battery: The 890 mAh rechargeable battery lasts up to 7 days depending on usage.
How is SyncUP TRACKER different from other tracking technologies like Bluetooth?

SyncUP TRACKER uses a combination of GPS technology, Wi-Fi, and T-Mobile’s LTE nationwide network to locate your device at any time from anywhere – even from thousands of miles away. Bluetooth-based location devices must be within a limited range of a smartphone to provide its location. SyncUP TRACKER is also available for both iOS and Android.

Front
  • Power button: Hold for 5 seconds to turn the TRACKER on/off.
  • LED indicator: Displays TRACKER status.
  • Temperature sensor: Detects ambient temperature.
  • Speaker: Audible feedback from the device.
  • Light sensor: Detects changes in light.
Back
  • IMEI number: Refer to this number for set up if needed.
  • Personal ID: ID label space.
  • Magnetic charging strip: Charger attaches here during charging.
  • QR code: Scan to pair the TRACKER during set up in the app.
Charging
  • Align the charging pins of the USB cable with the charging strip on the back of the TRACKER.
  • Connect the USB end to the power adapter.
  • Plug the adapter into an outlet to charge the TRACKER.
  • The LED indicator will be yellow when charging and green when fully charged.
Care and Cleaning

Use a soft, clean cloth and warm water to wipe off the TRACKER. While most household cleaners should not stain or damage the device, check on a small area first. The USB charging cable and adapter should only be cleared with a dry, clean cloth.

How is SyncUP TRACKER 2 different from other tracking technologies like Bluetooth?

SyncUP TRACKER 2 offers several advantages over other trackers:

  • Extended battery life: With up to 30% longer battery, SyncUP TRACKER ensures it lasts through extended tracking periods.
  • Rechargeable: Unlike many competing trackers that require battery replacements, SyncUP TRACKER is rechargeable, making it more eco-friendly and cost-efficient.
  • Lost Mode: This proactive feature helps guide anyone who finds your tracker through the process of returning it, increasing the likelihood of recovering lost items quickly and efficiently.

  • LED indicator: Displays TRACKER 2 status.
  • Light sensor: Detects changes in light.
  • Speaker: Audible feedback from the device.
Back
  • Lanyard loop: Attach lanyard or key ring here.
  • IMEI number: Refer to the number for setup if needed.
  • QR code: Scan to pair the TRACKER 2 during set up in the app, or return a lost device.
  • USB-C port: Insert USB cable here to charge.
Charging
  • Insert the USB charging cable into your TRACKER 2, attach it to the USB-C power adapter (not included), and connect it to a power outlet.
  • The LED indicator will be red when charging and solid green when fully charged.
Care and Cleaning

Use a soft, clean cloth and warm water to wipe off the TRACKER 2. While most household cleaners should not stain or damage the device, check on a small area first. The USB-C charging cable and charging block should only be cleared with a dry, clean cloth.

Status Lights

Youre Syncup TRACKER will inform you of status changes with different light colors.

Color

Flash / Solid

Meaning

Green

Solid for 5 seconds, then turns off

Battery charged 50-100%

Yellow

Solid for 5 seconds, then turns off

Battery charged 15-50%

Red

Solid for 5 seconds, then turns off

Battery charge level under 15%

Red

Flash for 1 second every 6 seconds continuously

Battery level approaching 0%. If not charged, flashing turns off at 0% battery

Green

Solid when connecte to charger

Battery charge has reached 100%

None

No light

Standby/ normal operation

Magenta

Flashes up to 10 times over 20 seconds followed by 3 times in 1 second, then turns off

TRACKER has successfully sent to SOS to T-Life on all phones to which TRACKER has been previously shared

Magenta

Flashes up to 10 times over 20 seconds, then turns off

TRACKER attempt to send SOS was not successfully delivered

White

Flash for one second every 2 seconds

Flashing in sync with TRACKER ringtone

White

Fades in over 1 second, statys solid for 5 more seconds

TRACKER went from OFF to ON

White

Flashes 3 times in 1 second, then turns off

TRACKER went from ON to OFF

White

Flashes 5 times in 1.5 seconds then turns off

User performed Factory Reset

SyncUP TRACKER in T-Life

Use T-Life to get the most out of your T-Mobile SyncUP TRACKER.

On this page:

  • App requirements
  • Download and login
  • Get started
  • Use the app

App requirements

  • Wi-Fi: 802.11 at 2.4 GHz
  • Android 11 or later (tablets not supported)
  • iOS 16 or later (iPad not supported)

Download and login

T-Life is required. It allows you to access your items’ location, notifications and more.

  • The app is available for free on the Apple App Store, Google Play Store, or t-mobile.com/syncuptracker.
  • Make sure your smartphone is up-to-date with the latest operating system and that it meets the requirements.

Get started

  • Ensure that the ICCID printed on back of SyncUP Tracker is updated your SyncUP Tracker line of service.
  • Hold the SyncUP Tracker power button until the device beeps to power on.
  • Log into the T-Life app.
  • Select the Locate tab and choose either People or Things.
  • Select + Add and choose Add SyncUP TRACKER > I have a Tracker device.
  • If prompted, select to agree to push notifications.
  • Choose how to add your SyncUP Tracker:
    • Scan QR Code: Use the camera on your phone to scan the QR code on the back of the Tracker.
    • Enter code manually: Enter the IMEI number found on the back of the Tracker, then select Next.
  • If prompted, check the box to agree to the terms & conditions, then choose I accept.
  • If prompted, allow Location in App Permissions.
  • If prompted, choose Battery Optimization preference.
  • Place the TRACKER on the charger and follow the on-screen steps to finish setting up your Tracker profile and adding the device until onboarding completes. (Note: the TRACKER device needs to remain on the charger during this onboarding step).

Use the app

View Tracker location
  • Open T-Life and choose the Locate tab.
  • Select the SyncUP Tracker in the Things section.
  • The location will appear on the map.
View and create a virtual Boundary
  • Open T-Life and choose the Locate tab.
  • Select the SyncUP Tracker in the Things section.
  • Select Virtual Boundaries and choose to add a new one.
  • Use the map or enter the address to your desired location.
  • Enter the rest of the information, like a boundary name and included devices, then choose Save.
Get Directions to your TRACKER
  • Open T-Life and choose the Locate tab.
  • Select the SyncUP Tracker in the Things section.
  • Choose Get Directions.
View Location History
  • Open T-Life and choose the Locate tab.
  • Select the SyncUP Tracker in the Things section.
  • Choose Location History.
Change the device Tracking Mode
  • Open T-Life and choose the Locate tab.
  • Select the SyncUP Tracker in the Things section.
  • Choose the desired tracking mode.
Use the Light Sensor
  • Open T-Life and choose the Locate tab.
  • Select the SyncUP Tracker in the Things section.
  • Choose the Gear icon and select Tracker Notifications > Light Sensor.
  • Choose if you want the light sensors to detect Dark to Light, Light to Dark, or both light event types.
Use Motion Alert
  • Open T-Life and choose the Locate tab.
  • Select the SyncUP Tracker in the Things section.
  • Choose the Gear icon and select Tracker Notifications > Motion Alert.
View Notifications
  • Open T-Life and choose the Locate tab.
  • Select the SyncUP Tracker in the Things section.
  • Choose the Bell icon.
Refresh Location
  • Open T-Life and choose the Locate tab.
  • Select the SyncUP Tracker in the Things section.
  • Choose the Gear icon and select Location Refresh.
Change notification settings
  • Open T-Life and choose the Manage tab.
  • Tap on Settings.
  • Tap on Notifications.
  • Tap on SyncUP Tracker.
Edit your device profile
  • Open T-Life and choose the Locate tab.
  • Select the SyncUP Tracker in the Things section.
  • Choose the Gear icon and select Cusomize to change the following:
    • Tracker Type
    • Image Type
    • Avatar
    • Device Name
View Device information
  • Open T-Life and choose the Locate tab.
  • Select the SyncUP Tracker in the Things section.
  • Choose the Gear icon and select Device Information.
Report an issue
  • Open T-Life.
  • From anywhere in the app, shake your phone and select Report a bug.
  • Choose Locate> SyncUP TRACKER to report an issue with your SyncUP TRACKER device or app.
Help Center
  • Open T-Life and choose the Locate tab.

Admin page

Access the Admin Page using Wi-Fi
  • Connect to the Mobile HotSpot via Wi-Fi.
  • Launch an available web browser on your connected device and go to mobile.hotspot You may also enter 192.168.0.1 in the browser address bar to access the admin page.
  • Enter the Admin Page administrator password. The default administrator password is admin.
  • Select the Save Password checkbox if you want to skip the login screen in the future.
  • Select Login.
Access the Admin Page using USB
  • With the device turned off, connect the hotspot device to a PC with the included USB cable.
  • Turn on the device.
  • The OS detects and recognizes new hardware and finishes the installation automatically. After successful installation, the icon will appear on your desktop. If the system does not launch installation automatically, you can run the installation program in path of (My) Computer > Mobile Hotspot > choose folder based on your OS > Run set-up.exe.
  • Select the icon to open the Admin Page login screen. If you ran the set-up.exe file, the web page interface will automatically pop up.
  • Enter the Admin Page administrator password. The default administrator password is admin.
  • Select the Save Password checkbox if you want to skip the login screen in the future.
  • Select Login.
Change the admin password
  • Access the mobile hotspot Admin Page.
  • Select the Settings tab.
  • Select Device Settings.
  • Under the Account Management heading, enter a new password into the New Password and Confirm New Password fields.
  • Select Apply.
Change the network name (SSID)
  • Access the mobile hotspot Admin Page.
  • Select the Settings tab.
  • Select Wi-Fi Settings.
  • Under the SSID heading, change the name that appears in the Network Name (SSID) field.
  • For Broadcast Network Name you may select enable or disable for broadcasting the hotspot’s Network Name (SSID).
  • Select Apply to save your changes.
Change the network password
  • Access the mobile hotspot Admin Page.
  • Select the Settings tab.
  • Select Wi-Fi Settings.
  • Enter a new password in the Password field.
  • Select Apply to save your changes.
Locate the mobile number
  • Access the mobile hotspot Admin Page.
  • Select the Information tab.

Battery saving mode
  • Access the mobile hotspot Admin Page.

  • Under the Wi-Fi Performance Settings heading, select one of the following for Wi-Fi Performance:
    • High performance (Longer Wi-Fi range but shorter battery life)
    • Economy mode (Shorter Wi-Fi range but longer battery life)
  • Select Apply.
Tips to save battery life
  • Access the mobile hotspot Admin Page.
  • Select the Settings tab.
  • Select Device Settings.
  • Under the Wi-Fi Sleep Settings heading, choose one of the following for Sleep Time (shorter durations will increase battery life while Wi-Fi is not in use).
    • After 10 minutes idle
    • After 15 minutes idle
    • After 20 minutes idle
    • After 30 minutes idle
    • After 60 minutes idle
    • Never go to Standby

APN & data settings
  • Access the mobile hotspot Admin Page.

  • Select Network Settings.
  • Under the ‘APN’ heading, confirm the information entered is correct.

  • Select Add New.
  • Enter the following information:
    • Profile Name: T-Mobile
    • APN: fast.t-mobile.com
  • Select Apply.
Manual network selection

The device detects and registers on wireless networks inside T-Mobile’s calling area, but roaming networks are usually restricted to T-Mobile SIM cards. You can manually select a network only in areas where T-Mobile does not own GSM spectrum.

  • Access the mobile hotspot Admin Page.
  • Select Disconnect.
  • Select the Settings tab.
  • Select Network Settings.
  • Under the ‘Network Selection’ heading, select Manual.
  • Select Search.
  • Choose the network to connect.
  • Select Apply.
Turn on / off data roaming
  • Access the mobile hotspot Admin Page.
  • Select Disconnect.
  • Select the Settings tab.
  • Select Network Settings.
  • Under the ‘WAN Connection Mode Settings’ heading, check or uncheck Check here, to connect to the internet in roaming status to turn data roaming on/off.
  • Select Apply.
Tethering
  • With the device turned off, connect the hotspot device to a PC with the included USB cable.
  • Turn on the device.
  • The OS detects and recognizes new hardware and finishes the installation automatically. After successful installation, the icon will appear on your desktop. If the system does not launch installation automatically, you can run the installation program in path of (My) Computer > Mobile Hotspot > choose folder based on your OS > Data (if needed) > Run set-up.exe.
  • Tethering is automatically active while connected.
Default Wi-Fi SSID and password
  • If the screen on the mobile hotspot is blank, use the WPS button to wake it up.
  • Double-press the WPS button on the device.
  • Read the SSID and Password displayed on the screen. The SSID and Password displayed on the screen will always be correct, even if they have been changed from the defaults.
Scan & connect to Wi-Fi
  • Turn on the mobile hotspot.
  • On your computer or other Wi-Fi enabled device, search for available Wi-Fi Networks and select the Network Name (SSID) for your Mobile HotSpot.
  • Enter the network password. It may take up to a minute to establish a connection.
Turn Wi-Fi on / off
  • Hold the WPS button it for less than 3 seconds then release.
  • The device will show Connecting/Disconnecting. It will then show Connected (no X over transfer arrows), or Disconnected (X over transfer arrows).

Software Updates & Device Resets

Master reset from settings menu

A master reset restores the original factory settings and may delete your personal data. It does not delete data stored on the SIM card.

  • Access the mobile hotspot Admin Page.
  • Select the Settings tab.
  • To confirm the master reset is complete, the SSID name and Password will be reset to default settings.
Master reset with hardware keys

A master reset restores the original factory settings and may delete your personal data. It does not delete data stored on the SIM card. If the device menus are frozen or unresponsive, you can master reset using hardware keys.

  • Open the SIM card door.
  • Insert a small object like a pin into the reset hole and hold it for three seconds to reset the device.
  • To confirm the master reset is complete, the SSID name and Password will be reset to default settings.
Software updates

Your device automatically updates to the latest version. No additional action is required.

T-Mobile device unlock

Learn how to use your device on another carrier or wireless provider’s network. This may also be known as SIM unlock, network unlock, or carrier unlock.

On this page:

  • What’s a Device Unlock?
  • Check unlock status & eligibility
  • Unlock your device
  • Get help

What’s a Device Unlock

  • Device Unlock lets you use your device with another carrier, for things like international travel or selling your device.
  • This is different from Domestic or International roaming, where you use a T-Mobile SIM/eSIM to access a different wireless provider’s network.

Check unlock status & eligibility

Once your device is eligible, T-Mobile will automatically unlock the device within two business days if it supports remote unlock.

T-Mobile.com account
  • Log into your T-Mobile Account and choose the Accounts page.
  • Select the line you wish to unlock, then choose Check device unlock status.
  • Under the device image, check if your device is eligible to be unlocked. Review Device Unlock Policy for a list of eligibility requirements.
T-Life / T-Mobile app
  • Open the T-Life / T-Mobile app and choose the Manage tab.
  • Select the line you wish to unlock. You may need to choose Manage all first.
  • View the ‘Device lock status’ field. Select Device lock status for additional details.
    • Under the device image, view your progress toward device unlock eligibility.
    • Review Device Unlock Policy for a list of eligibility requirements.

Unlock your device

Make sure you are connected to the T-Mobile network or Wi-Fi, then select your device type and follow the steps. If your device isn’t listed or the steps don’t work, choose your device on the Devices page for unlock steps or Contact us for assistance

Apple iPhone
  • To view unlock status, select Settings > General > About. If Carrier Lock says No SIM restrictions, your iPhone is unlocked.
  • If you have a locked iPhone that’s eligible, Contact us so we can submit the unlock.
Samsung
  • From your list of apps, choose Settings > Connections > More Connection Settings.
  • Select Network Unlock > Permanent Unlock, then wait for the unlock to complete.
  • Restart your device.
Google
  • Make sure you have a T-Mobile SIM inserted or T-Mobile eSIM setup on the device.
  • Access the Play Store and download the T-Mobile Device Unlock (Pixel) app.
  • Open the app and choose Check eligibility.
  • Select Permanent Unlock, then wait for the unlock to complete.
  • Restart your device.
Motorola
  • From your list of apps, choose Settings > About Phone > Device Unlock.
  • Select Permanent Unlock, then wait for the unlock to complete.
  • Restart your device.
Motorola devices purchased through USCellular

Motorola device is saying it is SIM unlocked

If your Motorola device is eligible for a SIM unlock but the unlock doesn’t complete, you may be able to refresh the unlock request.

Before you start

  • Make sure:
    • Your device is connected to Wi-Fi or the T-Mobile network.
    • Your device remains powered on during the refresh. Refresh the unlock request
  • When the SIM Unlock message appears, tap the More options menu (⋮) in the upper-right corner.
  • Select Refresh.
  • Wait while your device checks for and downloads the latest SIM unlock information.
  • Follow any additional on-screen prompts. What to expect

If the refresh is successful, your device downloads the SIM unlock automatically. Once complete, you can use your device with another compatible wireless provider’s SIM card.

If the issue continues

  • Try the following:
    • Restart your device.
    • Verify you’re connected to Wi-Fi or the T-Mobile network.
    • Wait a few minutes, then try Refresh again. If your device still doesn’t receive the SIM unlock, contact T-Mobile Customer Care for additional assistance.
LG
  • From your list of apps, choose Settings > Network & Internet > Mobile Networks.
  • Select Network Unlock > Continue > Permanent Unlock, then wait for the unlock to complete.
  • Restart your device.
OnePlus
  • From your list of apps, choose Settings > Wi-Fi & Internet > SIM & network.
  • Select either Advanced or Network Unlock.
  • Choose Permanent Unlock, then wait for the unlock to complete.
  • Restart your device.
Device Unlock App

Some older Android devices have a Device Unlock app preinstalled.

  • From your list of apps, choose Device Unlock.
  • Select Device Unlock > Continue and wait for the device to communicate with the server.
  • Choose Permanent Unlock, then wait for the unlock to complete.
  • Restart your device.
Other devices
  • Apple iPads, Apple Watches and Samsung Galaxy Watches are sold unlocked.
  • Hotspots and some tablets require unlock code. Contact us to request an unlock code

Get help

  • Contact us if you can’t find the app or settings to unlock your T-Mobile device, or if you get an error message when attempting to complete the unlock.
  • Not all devices are compatible with every wireless provider.
  • If you’ve unlocked a T-Mobile device but can’t get signal with another carrier, contact the other wireless provider for assistance.
  • If you’re bringing an unlocked device to T-Mobile, check out our compatibility checker and signal troubleshooting.

Settings & Tech Specs

First time use

Review these steps if you need help with the setup process.

  • Remove the back cover and battery to find the Wi-Fi Name (SSID) and password inside the back panel of your mobile hotspot.
  • Verify the SIM card is inserted and replace the battery and back cover.
  • Hold the Power button for 3 seconds until all LED indicators illuminate.
  • Connect your Wi-Fi device to your Mobile Hotspot.
  • On your computer or other Wi-Fi enabled device, search for available Wi-Fi networks and select network name (SSID).
    • From a Windows PC:
      • Left-select Wireless Network Connection on the taskbar to view available networks.
      • Choose the SSID from the list of available networks.
    • From a Mac computer:
      • Select System Preferences > Network > Airport.
      • Select Advanced to choose SSID from the list of available networks.
      • Choose the SSID from the list of available networks and enter your hotspot password.
    • From an iOS device:
      • Go to Settings > Wi-Fi.
      • Choose the SSID from the list of available networks and enter your hotspot password.
    • From an Android device:
      • Go to Settings > Wi‑Fi settings.
      • Choose the SSID from the list of available networks and enter your hotspot password.

Apps & Accessories

Access hotspot WebUI Manager

The hotspot WebUI Manager is a virtual dashboard to manage your mobile hotspot’s settings, features, and security controls.

  • After connecting the hotspot to your Wi-Fi enabled device, open a web browser and enter http://192.168.0.1 in the address bar.
  • Enter the WebUI password and select Login. The password is Admin + last 4 digits of the IMEI. The IMEI is printed on the device label under the battery.
  • On your first login, you will be asked to create a new password. Create your new password and log in again.
Change hotspot admin password
  • Select Settings > Device Settings.
  • Enter the current password, new password, and re-confirm the new password.
  • Select Save.
Change hotspot Network Name (SSID) and Wi-Fi password
  • Select Settings > Wi-Fi Basic Settings.
  • Select radio button 2.4 or 5 GHz.
  • Change the name and password in the field and select Save.
  • This will disconnect your current connection and you will need to reconnect to the hotspot and log back into the WebUI manager.
View device information

Go to the Device information page for basic information about your hotspot, including:

  • Phone Number (shows the phone number of the SIM card)
  • IMEI
  • Signal Strength.
  • 2.4GHz Network Name (SSID) (displays 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi Channel name).
  • 5GHz Network Name (SSID) (displays 5 GHz Wi-Fi Channel name).
  • Maximum Connections (the maximum number of connected devices allowable is 10).
  • LAN Domain
  • MAC Address
  • IP Address
  • WAN IP Address
  • Software Version
  • Model name
View plan details

Go to the Plan details page to review your data plan details and set up a monthly billing plan.

  • Set the billing day: Choose from 1 through 31.
  • Set the billing month: Choose from 1 through 12.
View connection details

Go to the Statistics page to review information about your connection, including:

  • Upload speed
  • Download speed
  • Current Connection
  • Current Year

Battery, Memory, & Storage

Battery
  • Remove the back cover.
  • Install or remove the battery.
  • Replace the back cover.
Insert/Remove SIM card

This device supports a Nano size SIM card.

  • Remove the back cover and battery.
  • Insert/Remove the SIM card from the SIM slot.
  • Replace the battery and back cover.
Turn SIM PIN on/off

The SIM PIN code can protect your SIM from being used in other devices. When you turn on the SIM PIN lock, the device prompts you to enter the code after turning it on.

  • Access the hotspot WebUI Manager.
  • Select Settings > Pin Code Management.
  • Toggle the Pin Code Management switch on or off.

Connections & Network

Hotspot network name (SSID) & password
  • The hotspot network name (SSID) is the name of the Wi-Fi network you’ll need to connect to.
  • The default hotspot network name (SSID) and password can be found inside the back panel of your mobile hotspot by removing the back cover and battery.
  • You can change the SSID and password using the WebUI Manager
Turn Hotspot on
  • Hold the Power button for 3 seconds until all LED indicators illuminate.
  • Wait for the Network and Wi-Fi Indicators to come on, one at a time.
  • When the Network and Wi-Fi icons light up, the Wi-Fi connection is enabled.
Turn Hotspot off
  • Hold the Power button for 3 seconds until all LED indicators turn off.
  • The Network and Wi-Fi connections have been disabled.
Connect to the hotspot

To connect your Wi-Fi enabled device to your hotspot for internet access, follow these steps.

  • Make sure your hotspot is turned on.
  • Select the Wi-Fi Network Name (SSID).
  • Enter the Wi-Fi Password.
  • Refer to the Hotspot WebUI Manager or the Quick Start Guide if you need to change your hotspot Wi-Fi Network Name (SSID) or Wi-Fi Password.
USB tethering

To connect your Wi-Fi enabled device to the mobile hotspot using a USB-C cable instead of using the Wi-Fi network follow these steps.

  • Make sure your mobile hotspot is on and has an active data connection.
  • Connect one end of the USB C cable to the hotspot and the other end to your device.
  • Your device will detect a network connection via USB automatically.
  • Check your connection by visiting a website.
Turn on / off cellular data
  • Access the hotspot WebUI Manager.
  • Select Settings > Network Settings.
  • Toggle the Cellular Data switch on or off.
Turn on / off data roaming
  • Access the hotspot WebUI Manager.
  • Select Settings > Network Settings.
  • Toggle the Data Roaming switch on or off.
Create a new APN (Access Point Name)

Your mobile hotspot comes pre-configured with the access point name (APN) for your network service provider. The mobile hotspot checks the APN to determine the type of network connection to establish.

  • Access the hotspot WebUI Manager.
  • Select Settings > Network Settings.
  • Select Add under the APN list. A pop-up box will appear to create new APN.
  • Enter the Profile Name of APN.
  • Enter the APN.
  • Enter the Username and Password.
  • Select Authentication Mode: PAP or CHAP.
  • Select IPType: IPv4 or IPv4v6.
Push WPS button
  • Access the hotspot WebUI Manager.
  • Select Settings > WPS.
  • Activate the WPS connection on the device you want to connect to the hotspot.
  • Select Push WPS Button.
  • Wait a moment for a successful Wi-Fi connection.
Enter Device PIN
  • Access the hotspot WebUI Manager.
  • Select Settings > WPS.
  • Activate the WPS connection on the Wi-Fi device you want to connect to the hotspot.
  • Enter the device’s 8-digit PIN code in the hotspot WebUI Manager.
  • Wait a moment for a successful Wi-Fi connection.
Connecting with WPS button

To connect your Wi-Fi device securely using the WPS button on your hotspot follow these steps.

  • Keep the T-Mobile Hotspot in range of the device you want to connect with.
  • Turn on your mobile hotspot by pressing and holding the Power button for 3 seconds.
  • Open your Wi-Fi network manager on your computer, smartphone, tablet, or other Wi-Fi enabled device.
  • Connect your Wi-Fi enabled device to your hotspot by selecting your mobile hotspot’s network name (SSID).
  • Press and hold the WPS button located on the bottom of the mobile hotspot for 5 seconds.
  • Your Wi-Fi enabled device will start connecting.

Email & Messaging

View a text messaging

This device can only receive messages and not send them. To view a text message, follow these steps.

  • The message LED indicator will flash on the hotspot when a new message is received and will show a solid light when the inbox is full.
  • Access the hotspot WebUI Manager.
  • Select the SMS tab. A list of messages will be displayed.
  • Choose the message to open it.
Delete a text message

A maximum of 50 new messages can be stored. Older messages will be deleted automatically. To delete a text message, follow these steps.

  • Access the hotspot WebUI Manager.
  • Select the SMS tab. A list of messages will be displayed.
  • Select the checkbox next to the message you want to delete.
  • Select Delete.

Software Updates & Backup

Master reset from the admin page

A master reset restores the original factory settings. It does not delete data stored on the SIM card.

  • Access the hotspot WebUI Manager.
  • Select Settings > Device Settings.
  • Select Device > Backup and Restore > Restore Factory Defaults.
  • Select Reset under Factory Reset.
  • Select Confirm.
  • Wait a moment as the device is restored to the default settings.
  • You will need to re-connect to the device with the default Wi-Fi login credentials.
Master reset with hardware keys

A master reset restores the original factory settings. It does not delete data stored on the SIM card. If the device menus are frozen or unresponsive, you can master reset using hardware keys.

  • Turn the device on.
  • Insert a paperclip into the Factory Reset Pinhole.
  • Press the Factory Reset Pinhole for 6 seconds and release. The device will reset and restart.
Software Update

The device automatically updates to the latest software version when it’s available. There is no option to manually check for a software update.
