Admin page

Access Admin Page for the First time

The first time you access the Mobile Hotspot Admin page, you will be taken through a required set up wizard and given the opportunity to change your Admin password, Wi-Fi network SSID, and W-Fi network password.

  • Connect your Wi-Fi enabled computer to your Mobile Hotspot via Wi-Fi. Use the default SSID and Wi-Fi password located on the white sticker next to the battery.
  • Select the Mobile HotSpot icon on your desktop or open a browser window and enter mobile.hotspot.
  • Enter the default password ‘admin’ and then select Log in.
  • When the page opens, review the tips and select Next.
  • Review the next set of tips and select Next.
  • In the text field, enter your new, unique, Admin page password and select Next.
  • Enter a new name for your Mobile HotSpot (the SSID) that you’ll use to identify your connection from the list of available networks. When finished, select Next. If you need to find the SSID later, use the arrow keys to navigate to the Device info screen, use the Enter key to review the Network Name.
  • If desired, select Change Wi-Fi security password to change your default Wi-Fi password. Otherwise, your Wi-Fi password will remain the default password. When finished, select Finish.
  • Your Mobile HotSpot will automatically disconnect from your computer to enable you new settings. Reconnect your Wi-Fi enabled computer to your Mobile HotSpot using your new settings. When you have connected, select Refresh Page. If too much time elapses, you may have to log back in to the Admin page using your new Admin password that you just created.
Access Admin Page
  • Connect your computer to your Mobile Hotspot via Wi-Fi.
  • Select T-Mobile Hotspot Admin icon on your desktop or open a browser window and enter mobile.hotspot or 192.168.0.1 into the address bar.
  • In the Password field, enter the Admin Page password that you created. The default administrator password is admin.
  • Select Log in.
Add additional access point names

It is recommended that you accept default settings and do not change them unless you are an advanced user. If you have problems using your Mobile Hotspot after you change a setting, it is recommended that you reset the device to factory default settings.

  • Connect your computer to your Mobile Hotspot via Wi-Fi.
  • Select the T-Mobile Hotspot Admin icon on your desktop or open a browser window and enter mobile.hotspot.
  • Enter your administrator password that you created and select Login.
  • Select Configuration.
  • If necessary, select General.
  • Select Add.
  • Adjust the following settings (further explanation available in the table on this page):
    • Profile Name
    • APN
    • Authentication
      • None
      • PAP
      • CHAP
    • User Name
    • Password
  • Select Save. > Save to confirm.
  • Select Refresh page. If necessary, re-connect to your Mobile Hotspot to update the settings. To reconnect, if necessary, ‘Forget’ your network on your Wi-Fi enabled computer to remove the previous settings associated with your Wi-Fi enabled computer. Next, scan again for available Wi-Fi networks, and then reconnect to your Mobile Hotspot. Access point settings

Option

Description

Profile Name

Enter the profile name.

APN

Enter the APN string.

Authentication

PAP: Password Authentication Protocol (PAP) provides a simple method, without encryption, for the peer to establish its identity by using a two-way handshake.

CHAP: Challenge-Handshake Authentication Protocol is used to periodically verify the identity of the peer by using a three-way handshake.

User Name

The user name is used to obtain authentication from the ISP when the connection is established.

Password

The password is used to obtain authentication from the ISP when the connection is established.

Change basic wireless network settings
  • Connect your computer to your Mobile Hotspot via Wi-Fi.
  • Select the T-Mobile Hotspot Admin icon on your desktop or open a browser window and enter mobile.hotspot.
  • Enter your administrator password that you created and select Login.
  • Select Configuration.
  • Select Hotspot Settings.
  • Adjust the following settings:
    • Change password (Admin password)
    • Network mode
    • Network Name (SSID)
    • Broadcast network name (on/off)
    • Wi-Fi Security
    • Encryption
    • Password (Wi-Fi password)
    • Channel
    • Enable default data limits
    • Enable default time limits
    • Subnet mask
    • Enable DHCP server (on/off)
    • DHCP Address Range
    • DHCP Lease time (in hours)
  • Select Save. If necessary, reconnect to your Mobile Hotspot to update the settings.
Change administrator password

Your administrator password is the password you use to access your T-Mobile Hotspot Admin page on your computer. Changing the administrator password does not change the password you use to connect other devices to your Mobile Hotspot.

  • Connect your computer to your Mobile Hotspot via Wi-Fi.
  • Select the T-Mobile Hotspot Admin icon on your desktop or open a browser window and enter mobile.hotspot.
  • Enter your administrator password that you created and select Login.
  • Select Configuration.
  • Select Hotspot Settings.
  • Under ‘Admin Password,’ select Change Password.
  • In the Password field, enter your current password.
  • In the New field, enter your new password.
  • In the Verify field, enter the new password to confirm.
  • Select Change > OK.
Change the SSID
  • Connect your computer to your Mobile Hotspot via Wi-Fi.
  • Select the T-Mobile Hotspot Admin icon on your desktop or open a browser window and enter mobile.hotspot.
  • Enter the administrator password that you created and select Login.
  • Select Configuration > Hotspot Settings.
  • Select the Network Name (SSID) field and enter the desired SSID.
  • Select Save.
Change the Wi-Fi password

The Wi-Fi password is the password used to connect other devices to your Mobile Hotspot. Changing the Wi-Fi password does not change the password you use to access your T-Mobile Hotspot Admin page from your computer.

  • Connect your computer to your Mobile Hotspot via Wi-Fi.
  • Select the T-Mobile Hotspot Admin icon on your desktop or open a browser window and enter mobile.hotspot.
  • Enter the administrator password that you created and select Login.
  • Select Configuration > Hotspot Settings.
  • Under ‘Wi-Fi Security,’ select the Password field and delete the existing password.
  • Enter your new Wi-Fi Security Password.
  • Select Save > Save to confirm. You will need to reconnect to your Mobile Hotspot using the new settings.
Change connection mode (Automatic or Manual)
  • Connect your computer to your Mobile Hotspot via Wi-Fi.
  • Select the T-Mobile Hotspot Admin icon on your desktop or open a browser window and enter mobile.hotspot.
  • Enter your administrator password that you created and select Login.
  • Select Configuration.
  • Select General.
    • To connect manually:
      • Under Auto Connect, select the Automatically connect to T-Mobile when device is powered on check box to clear the check box and disable auto-connect.
    • To connect automatically:
      • Under Auto Connect, select the Automatically connect to T-Mobile when device is powered on check box to select the check box and enable auto-connect.
      • If you choose to connect manually, then you must also disconnect from the internet manually.
  • Select Save > Save to confirm.
  • After you are automatically disconnected, reconnect to your Mobile Hotspot to update the settings. If necessary, to reconnect, ‘Forget’ your network to remove the previous settings on your Wi-Fi enabled computer, scan again for available Wi-Fi networks, and then reconnect to your Mobile Hotspot.
Firewall settings

You can set up firewall rules to protect your network from virus, worm, and malicious activity on the Internet.

  • Connect your computer to your Mobile Hotspot via Wi-Fi.
  • Select the T-Mobile Hotspot Admin icon on your desktop or open a browser window and enter mobile.hotspot.
  • In the Password field, enter the Admin Page password that you created.
  • Select Log in > Configuration.
  • Select the Firewall settings tab.
Local area network (LAN) status

To get the status of your local area network (LAN) and change advanced Mobile Hotspot settings:

  • Connect your computer to your Mobile Hotspot via Wi-Fi.
  • Select the T-Mobile Hotspot Admin icon on your desktop or open a browser window and enter mobile.hotspot.
  • Enter your administrator password that you created and select Login.
  • Select Configuration > Hotspot Settings.
  • Review the ‘Network Settings’ and change as desired.
  • Select Save. If necessary, reconnect to your Mobile Hotspot to update the changes.
Enable or disable MAC / IP / Port Filtering
  • Connect your computer to your Mobile Hotspot via Wi-Fi.
  • Select the T-Mobile Hotspot Admin icon on your desktop or open a browser window and enter mobile.hotspot.
  • Enter your administrator password that you created and select Login.
  • Select Configuration > Firewall Settings.
  • Select Enable filtering to select or clear the Check box and enable or disable.
  • If Enable filtering is enabled, select the Default policy field and then select one of the following options:
    • Accepted
    • Dropped
  • Select Save.
Delete a rule
  • Connect your computer to your Mobile Hotspot via Wi-Fi.
  • Select the T-Mobile Hotspot Admin icon on your desktop or open a browser window and enter mobile.hotspot.
  • Enter your administrator password that you created and select Login.
  • Select Configuration > Firewall Settings.
  • Select View [x] rule[s] and select the check box for each rule you want to delete.
  • Select Delete > Close > Save.
Add a new rule
  • Connect your computer to your Mobile Hotspot via Wi-Fi.
  • Select the T-Mobile Hotspot Admin icon on your desktop or open a browser window and enter mobile.hotspot.
  • Enter your administrator password that you created and select Login.
  • Select Configuration > Firewall Settings.
  • If necessary, select Enable filtering to select the Check box and enable.
  • Enter the follow settings as necessary:
    • MAC Address
    • Destination IP Address
    • Source IP Address
    • Protocol
    • Destination Port Range
    • Source Port Range
    • Action
    • Comment
  • When finished, select Add Port Filter Rule.
  • If successful, View [x] rule(s) will now increase by one.
  • Select Save.

Battery, Memory, & Storage

Insert Battery
  • Gently push the back cover down and then remove it.
  • Insert the battery by aligning the contacts on the battery with the metal springs in the battery compartment.
  • Slide the back cover on and snap it back into place.
Remove Battery
  • Gently push the back cover down and then remove it.
  • Lift and remove the battery.
  • Slide the back cover on and snap it into place.
SIM Card

To insert or remove the SIM card…

  • Gently push the back cover down and then remove it.
  • Lift and remove the battery.
  • Place the SIM card into the SIM card slot with the gold contacts facing down, or slide out the SIM card to remove it.
  • Replace the battery while ensuring the gold contacts are aligned.
  • Slide the back cover on and snap it into place.
Insert / remove SD card
  • Pull the cover of the memory card slot to the side.
  • Insert the microSD card into the card slot with the gold contacts facing up until it locks into place, or to remove, press the microSD card gently inward until it locks, and then release. The card will pop out slightly and can be removed.
  • Replace the cover over the card slot to close it.
Open / delete files

You must use the USB cable that comes with your phone.

  • Connect the USB cord to the phone, then to a computer.
  • On your computer, select Open folder to view files > OK.
  • You will get another Removable Disk window, select Open folder to view files > OK again. One folder shows files saved in your phone memory and one folder shows files saved on your SD card.
  • Locate the folder that contains files you want to delete.
  • Once you have located the files, right-select and choose Delete.
  • When done, disconnect the USB cable.
Transfer files

You must use the USB cable that comes with your phone.

  • Connect the USB cord to the phone, then to a computer.
  • On your computer, select Open folder to view files > OK.
  • You will get another Removable Disk window, select Open folder to view files > OK again. One folder shows files saved in your phone memory and one folder shows files saved on your SD card.
  • Locate the folder that contains files saved on your SD card.
  • Locate the file(s) you want to move on your computer.
  • Cut or copy and paste the desired file(s) from your computer to your SD card.
  • When done, disconnect the USB cable.

    • Profile Name: Enter the profile name.

      • None
      • PAP: Password Authentication Protocol (PAP) provides a simple method, without encryption, for the peer to establish its identity by using a two-way handshake.
      • CHAP: Challenge-Handshake Authentication Protocol is used to periodically verify the identity of the peer by using a three-way handshake.
    • User name: The user name is used to obtain authentication from the ISP when the connection is established.

Delete APN Broadband Profile

  • Select Configuration > General.
  • From under ‘WWAN APN Settings,’ select the Profile field and then select the profile you want to delete.
  • Select Delete > Delete to confirm.
Mobile Hotspot setup & icons
  • If necessary, remove the battery cover for your Mobile Hotspot and note the default Network Name / SSID and Password printed on the white label located next to the battery (If the sticker is missing or unreadable, the default SSID is T-Mobile Broadband##, where ## is the last 2 digits of the device IMEI and the default password is the last 8 digits of the device IMEI).
  • Replace the battery cover and then power on your Mobile Hotspot.
  • On your computer, open the application you use to connect via Wi-Fi.
  • Select the default SSID for your Mobile Hotspot. If you do not get your SSID, your Mobile Hotspot may have gone into sleep mode. Use the Power key to wake the display.
  • Enter the default password.
  • Select OK.
  • Your Mobile Hotspot’s Internet connection is now available to your connected computer. If your service is not already set up, open a web page on your computer and follow the on-screen prompts to set up your service. Otherwise, open a web page and browse.
Switch 3G / 4G / LTE
  • Connect your computer to your Mobile HotSpot via Wi-Fi.
  • Select the T-Mobile HotSpot Admin icon on your desktop or open a browser window and enter mobile.hotspot.
  • Enter the Admin password that you created and select Login.
  • Select Configuration > General.
  • In ‘Network Radios,’ select one of the following options:
    • Best available
    • LTE only
    • 3G only
    • 2G only
Turn on / off data roaming
  • Connect your computer to your Mobile HotSpot via Wi-Fi.
  • Select the T-Mobile HotSpot Admin icon on your desktop or open a browser window and enter mobile.hotspot.
  • Enter the Admin password that you created and select Login.
  • Select Configuration > General.
  • In ‘Data Roaming,’ select the box to check or un-check Allow connections when roaming.
Tethering on a PC

To connect your PC computer to your Mobile Hotspot using tethering…

  • Power on your Mobile Hotspot.
  • Connect the large end of your USB cord to your USB port on your computer.
  • Connect the small end of your USB cord to your Mobile Hotspot.
  • If you haven’t already installed the Webconnect software, complete the Mobile Hotspot Install Wizard by following the next six steps. Otherwise, skip to step 5.
    • From the pop-up window, select Next. If the pop-up window fails to appear, select Start > My Computer, then hover over Mobile HotSpot and right-select. Choose Open, open the Windows folder, and then select the autorun.exe icon.
    • Select Next> Next > Next > Install.
    • Select Finish. When installation has finished, the Admin Shortcut icon will appear on your desktop.
  • Tethering is now active. Open your web browser and navigate to the desired web page.
  • To end the session, remove the USB cable.
Tethering on a Mac

To connect your Mac computer to your Mobile Hotspot using tethering…

  • Charge and turn on your Mobile Hotspot.
  • Plug the small end of the USB cable into the bottom of the Mobile Hotspot.
  • Plug the large end of the USB cable into a USB port on your Wi-Fi enabled computer.
  • If you haven’t already installed the Webconnect software, complete the Mobile Hotspot Install Wizard by following the next five steps. Otherwise, skip to step 5.
    • From the pop-up window, select Mac. If your computer fails to automatically launch installation of the Mobile Hotspot shortcut:
      • From the desktop screen, if necessary, close any pop-up windows to reveal the ‘Go’ menu link.
      • Select Go > Computer.
      • Select Mobile Hotspot.
      • Select Mac.
    • Select Mobile Hotspot.mpkg.
    • Select Continue.
    • If necessary, select Change Install location or Customize to adjust these settings. When finished, select Install
    • When the installation finishes, select Close. The Admin shortcut will appear on your desktop when the software has finished installing.
  • Tethering is now active. Open your web browser and navigate to the desired web page.
  • To end the session, remove the USB cable.
Linux

To connect your Linux computer to your Mobile Hotspot using tethering…

  • Charge and turn on your Mobile Hotspot.
  • Plug the small end of the USB cable into the bottom of the Mobile Hotspot.
  • Plug the large end of the USB cable into a USB port on your Wi-Fi enabled computer.If you haven’t already installed the Webconnect software, you must complete the next 3 steps to install.
  • Select the CD ROM icon or manually navigate to and open your USB drive.
  • Select the Install icon.
  • Select Run. Tethering is active when the download finishes.
  • Open the web browser and navigate to the desired web page.
  • To end the session, remove the USB cable.

Email & Messaging

Send messages
  • Connect your computer to your Mobile Hotspot via Wi-Fi.

  • Select SMS > New.
  • In the SMS Number field, enter the recipient’s 10-digit phone number.
  • In the Text Entry field, enter a message that is up to 140 characters long.
  • Use the Enter key to send the text message.
View & text messages
  • Connect your computer to your Mobile Hotspot via Wi-Fi.
  • Select the T-Mobile Hotspot Admin icon on your desktop or open a browser window and enter mobile.hotspot.
  • Enter the administrator password that you created and select Login.
  • Select SMS to review the following categories:
    • Next to ‘SMS,’ the number of new, unread messages is indicated inside parenthesis.
    • Select Messages to open messages from T-Mobile.
  • From the ‘Conversations’ section, select the desired Conversation thread.
  • Review the text message in the Conversation thread.
Delete text messages (SMS)
  • Connect your computer to your Mobile Hotspot via Wi-Fi.
  • Select the T-Mobile Hotspot Admin icon on your desktop or open a browser window and enter mobile.hotspot.
  • Enter your administrator password that you created and select Log in.
  • Select SMS.
  • Choose one of the following options:
    • To delete an entire Conversation thread, select the trash can icon next to the desired Conversation thread.

Security

PUK

If you enter a PIN code incorrectly several times in a row, the device blocks you from attempting again. You must contact us for the PUK code. Entering the wrong code can permanently damage your SIM card.

  • Contact us to request your PUK code.
  • Access the Web Portal
  • Select Unlock SIM.
  • Enter the PUK code.
  • Select OK.
  • Enter your new PIN.
  • Select OK.
  • Re-enter your new PIN.
  • Select OK.
Change SIM PIN
  • Connect your computer to your Mobile Hotspot via Wi-Fi.
  • Select the T-Mobile Hotspot Admin icon on your desktop or open a browser window and enter mobile.hotspot.
  • Enter your administrator password that you created and select Login.
  • Select Configuration > General > Change PIN.
  • Enter your current SIM PIN code into the PIN Code field.
  • Enter your new SIM PIN code into the New PIN field.
  • Enter your new SIM PIN code again into the Verify PIN field.
  • Select Change PIN > OK.
Turn on / off SIM PIN

The SIM PIN code can protect your SIM from being used in other devices. When you turn on the SIM PIN lock, the device prompts you to enter the code after turning it on. To lock and unlock the SIM card:

  • Connect your computer to your Mobile Hotspot via Wi-Fi.
  • Select the T-Mobile Hotspot Admin icon on your desktop or open a browser window and enter mobile.hotspot.
  • Enter your administrator password that you created and select Login.
  • Select Configuration > General.
  • Select Enable PIN Lock to select the check box and enable.
  • In the PIN Code field, enter your default SIM PIN code (‘1234’) and select Enable PIN. If you enter the incorrect SIM PIN code three times, your SIM Card will become locked and you will need your PUK Code. If this happens, contact us to obtain your PUK Code.
  • Read the message and select OK., or select Power Off Now to immediately enable SIM PIN lock.

Settings & Tech Specs

First use wizard

The first time you access the Mobile Hotspot Admin page, you will be taken through a required setup wizard and given the opportunity to change your Admin password, Wi-Fi network SSID, and W-Fi network password. To access the Mobile HotSpot Admin page for the first time…

  • Connect your Wi-Fi-enabled computer to your Mobile Hotspot via Wi-Fi. Use your default SSID and Wi-Fi password to connect which are located on the white sticker next to the battery. Remove the back panel to access them.
  • Select the Mobile HotSpot icon on your desktop or open a browser window and enter mobile.hotspot.com.
  • Enter your default password ‘admin’ and select Log in
  • When the page opens, review the tips and select Next.
  • Review the next set of tips and select Next.
  • In the text field, enter your new, unique, Admin page password and select Next.
  • Enter a new name for your Mobile HotSpot (the SSID) that you’ll use to identify your connection from the list of available networks. When finished, select Next.
  • If desired, select Change Wi-Fi security password to change your default Wi-Fi password. Otherwise, your Wi-Fi password will remain the default password. When finished, select Finish.
  • Now, your Mobile HotSpot will automatically disconnect from your computer to enable your new settings. Reconnect your Wi-Fi-enabled computer to your Mobile HotSpot using your new settings. When you have connected, select Refresh Page.

Software Updates & Device Resets

Master reset from Settings menu

A master reset restores the original factory settings and may delete your personal data on the internal storage. It does not delete data stored on the SIM card or SD card. To perform a master reset…

  • Connect your computer to your Mobile Hotspot via Wi-Fi.
  • Select the T-Mobile Hotspot Admin icon on your desktop or open a browser window and enter mobile.hotspot.
  • Enter your administrator password that you created and select Login.
  • Select Configuration.
  • Select Reset to factory defaults.
  • Select Reset Settings.
  • You will be automatically disconnected from your Mobile Hotspot as the default settings are restored. Reconnect using the default SSID and password located on the white sticker next to the battery.
Master reset with hardware keys

A master reset restores the original factory settings and may delete your personal data on the internal storage. It does not delete data stored on the SIM card or SD card.

Resetting your device restores all factory defaults. You may need to reset your device if you cannot connect device(s) to your Wi-Fi HotSpot or can not regain access to the Web portal. If the device is frozen or unresponsive, you can master reset using hardware keys. To perform a master reset:

  • Power on your Mobile Hotspot.
  • Gently push the back cover down and then remove it.
  • Locate the Reset point.
  • When ready to perform the reset, if necessary, use the Power button to wake up the screen.
  • Gently insert a paper clip into the Reset point for the three seconds.
  • Watch the activated screen. When it begins to shut down, remove the paper clip.
  • Your device will shut down and automatically restart.
  • To confirm a successful factory reset, when the device restarts and displays the ‘Device info’ screen, use the Enter key.
  • Get the Network Name and confirm that it has changed to your default network name. You can check by comparing the name to the Network Name / SSID that appears on the white sticker next to the battery.
Software update
  • On your Mobile Hotspot, use the arrow buttons to navigate to the Settings screen.
  • Select Enter.
  • With Software Update highlighted, choose Enter.
  • Follow any additional prompts.

T-Mobile Warranty program

If you’re having issues with your device and troubleshooting isn’t helping, we can help!

On this page:

  • What does my device warranty include?
  • In-warranty solutions
  • Protection 360 or Device Protection solutions
  • Out-of-warranty solutions
  • Complete an exchange in-store

What does my device warranty include?

Electrical and mechanical issues due to defects
  • Device network issues, such as no service or no internet
  • Device cannot turn on
  • Crashing or freezing
  • Issues reading memory card or SIM card
  • Unresponsive button
  • Flip phone hinge is stuck
  • Antenna does not extend
Does not include

All physical damage is excluded from warranty coverage

  • Cracks in the back or case, dents, chipped glass, etc.
  • Missing or damaged buttons
  • Scuffs or scratches on the device case
  • Screen damage
  • Camera lens scratch or damage
  • Charging port damaged, loose, or not charging
  • Battery issues Warranty programs are available directly through T-Mobile, Equipment Manufacturers (OEM), or other insurers.

In-warranty solutions

Devices are covered by the OEM warranty period (typically 12 months). REVVL devices are covered by T-Mobile’s 24-month limited warranty. Exclusions and restrictions apply.

  • First, check out our easy-to-follow troubleshooting steps that fix most device issues.
  • Contact us:
    • Visit a T-Mobile store
    • Contact Us

Protection 360 or Device Protection solutions

If you have Protection 360 or Basic Device Protection, you get:

  • Extended warranty for upgrade or repair for as long as you have protection services active on your account.
  • Devices with issues not covered by warranty, file a claim, or upgrade. For devices covered by Apple Care services or Apple, contact Apple support.

Out-of-warranty solutions

Common reasons a device is out of warranty:
  • The original manufacturer warranty period is expired.
  • The device was purchased through a third party, like a friend or re-seller.
  • Device has third-party parts from an unauthorized repair.
  • Liquid or physical damage is present. Always check for damage! If we receive a damaged device your account will be charged a fee.
Device is damaged
  • If you have Protection 360 or Basic Device Protection, file a claim. For devices covered by Apple Care services or Apple, contact Apple support.
  • Explore eligibility options to upgrade your device.
Not purchased from T-Mobile or is outside of warranty
  • Contact the manufacturer directly if you do not want to, or cannot, participate in T-Mobile’s device replacement program.
  • If you have Protection 360, contact Assurant
  • Explore eligibility options to upgrade your device.

Complete an exchange in-store

After diagnostics and troubleshooting have been completed, we will order a replacement device that will be sent to the T-Mobile store of your choice. We will notify you when the device arrives at the store.

Prepare for your replacement
  • Back up your device and reset it to remove personal information, which we can help you with at the store.
  • Device color is not guaranteed. The replacement device may be refurbished and will carry a 90-day warranty, or the original warranty, whichever is longer.
  • Keep SIM cards & accessories, including case, charger, back cover, SIM card, memory card, removable battery, stylus, and watchband or other accessories. (T-Mobile cannot retrieve them after devices are sent to the Return Center.)
Replacement pick up & payment process
  • Pay the warranty exchange fee including tax if applicable.
  • Pick up your replacement device within 8 days from the order date, otherwise the order will be canceled.
  • You must be listed as the Billing Responsible Party or authorized user, have a photo ID and bring the defective device to the store.
  • The device will be inspected in the store for damage to help prevent unexpected fees.
  • Once we collects your device, you cannot be charged an out-of-warranty or non-return fee.
  • If the device is found to be damaged, we will cancel the exchange instead of charging you for the device and help you explore alternate replacement options.
  • If you require an exception to this process, Contact Us to speak with us for an alternate solution.

About TIMEX FamilyConnect Watch

Stay active and connected to your loved ones with 4G LTE 2-way calling and messaging, heart rate monitoring, activity tracking, a dedicated SOS button, and fall detection. This watch works with the intuitive TIMEX FamilyConnect app to customize your preferences and contacts and get daily reminders to keep you on track.

Check out the TIMEX FamilyConnect Watch user manual and Quick Start Guide for detailed instructions on how to set up and use your device.

What’s in the box?

  • Watch

  • Charging dock

  • SIM tool

  • USB type A to C charging cable

  • Quick start guide Key Features

  • SOS Alert and Fall Detection: Dedicated SOS button and fall detection will call a designated contact to get help fast and send alerts to loved ones.

  • Two-way Calling and Messaging: Stay connected with family and friends with two-way calling and messaging.

  • Real-time Location Sharing: Use the FamilyConnect app to get location updates on map views, set up safe zones and track activity.

  • Fitness Tracking: Stay healthy with a heart rate monitor and fitness tracker that counts steps, calories burned, distance walked and more.

  • Premium design for an active lifestyle: The lightweight and splash-resistant watch with interchangeable bands can fit wrist sizes from 5 - 3/4” to 8 - 1/2”. Plus, the 2.5D glass provides a beautiful, seamless edge on the 1.41” full-color AMOLED touch display.

  • Convenient and fast charging: The 600 mAh battery can provide up to 3 full days of mixed usage, and up to 7 days of standby time. The convenient charging dock lets you charge up easily and quickly so you can get back to your activities. Tech Specs

Technical specifications for the TIMEX FamilyConnect watch

    • Operating System: Proprietary

    • Fall Detection: Yes
    • PAI Scoring: Yes

  • App Features

    • Geo Location: Yes
    • Tracking: Automatic / On-demand
    • Activity monitoring: Run, walk, distance, history, calories, goals
    • Notifications: Watch status, in-app messages, scheduled reminders, alarms, medication reminders, sedentary reminders, safezone alerts, SOS alerts, fall detection alerts Display / Dimensions

Setting up the Watch & App

Download the TIMEX FamilyConnect App

  • Search for TIMEX FamilyConnect in the Apple App Store or Google Play store.

  • Be sure your smartphone is up-to-date with the latest operating system and meets the minimum technical requirements. Set up your watch

  • Press and hold the Power button on the side of the watch. The T-Mobile SIM comes in the watch

  • Press the power button and follow the remaining steps on the screen.

  • Choose your language.

  • The watch will ask you to contact T-Mobile Care to activate. Sign in or create an account in the TIMEX FamilyConnect App

  • Select the app on your device.

  • If you already have an account, choose SIGN IN.

  • If you don’t have an account, choose CREATE ACCOUNT.

  • Set up your account information, including your password.

  • Add your phone number.

  • Add a profile picture.

  • Select NEXT.

  • You will receive a confirmation email. Follow the instructions to verify your email address.

  • After you Confirm Email & Grant consent on the email you received, you’ll be taken back to the TIMEX app.

  • Read the Privacy Policy and select Accept.

  • Choose ADD WATCH. Add an account for yourself (with emergency contacts)

  • Register to the app as a new user. Select ADD WATCH.

  • Select Watch to continue, then select NEXT.

  • If you’re setting up a watch for yourself, select FOR ME.

  • You may add emergency contacts. Select the blue plus icon to add.

  • Enter a new emergency contact or choose one from Your Contacts.

  • Once you’ve entered your emergency contact information select SAVE.

  • The app will ask for any missing information. Choose Add Now or Add Later.

  • Once an emergency contact has been added, select CONTINUE to complete this step. Add an account for a loved one

  • Register to the app as a new user. Select ADD WATCH.

  • Select Watch to continue, then select NEXT.

  • If you’re setting up a watch for a family member, select FOR FAMILY MEMBER.

  • You’ll be automatically added as the main emergency contact. Select the blue plus icon to add a new or additional emergency contact.

Using the TIMEX FamilyConnect Watch App

Initial Setup (HeartFIT profile)

  • You’ll be prompted to set up a HeartFIT profile once the watch is paired during the onboarding process. Select CONTINUE.
  • You’ll be prompted to enter your user information such as height and weight. You can also add a profile picture. Select NEXT to continue.
  • You’ll select your activity goals, or enter them manually. Select NEXT to continue.
  • You’ll be asked a series of questions for PAI before setup is completed. Once you’ve completed, select OK to save your HeartFIT profile. PAI (Personal Activity Intelligence)

PAI is a science-backed health score that measures the impact of your physical activity on your heart and guides you to a longer, healthier life.

Add an Approved Contact

  • In the app, select the MENU icon. Select All Contacts.

  • Once in Contacts, select the blue plus button to add an additional contact.

  • You may add new contact as Contact or Guardian, then name, phone number, and email before you APPLY TO a designated watch.

  • Once the new contact is added, you may send an SMS message notification to a new contact. Add a New Preset Message

  • From the main app screen, select the desired watch you’d like to add a new preset message for and select the SETTINGS icon.

  • While in the WATCH DATA & SETTINGS menu, select PRESET MESSAGES.

  • You will be able to view all preset messages and add new ones with the blue + icon. Select the blue + icon.

  • Add your new, customer preset message. Select the blue checkmark to add. Location Tracking (create a safe-zone)

  • In the app, select the MENU icon. Choose Safe Zones.

  • Once in Safe Zones, select the blue + icon to add a new Safe Zone.

  • You may add an address, name the Safe Zone and customize the radius of the Safe Zone from 650ft to 1960ft. Then select APPLY TO designated watch.

  • In addition to Safe Zones. Guardians may customize Automatic Location Updates and Set Monitoring Times under DEVICE SETTINGS. Location Tracking (using the map view to find the watch)

  • In the app, select the MENU icon. Select Map View.

  • Once in the Map View, select the watch you would like to zoom in on by selecting the profile image. Choose the desired watch name.

  • From this view, you may access device settings or choose from available actions like SEND MESSAGE, CALL WATCH, REFRESH LOCATION, or ACTIVE TRACKING.

  • Refreshing location will manually refresh the location of the watch. You may also enable ACTIVE TRACKING to get up to the moment location activity. Track Medication

  • Medication tracker can be found in the Daily Planner on the app. Select Track Medication and select NEXT.

  • Add the medication name, dosage, detailed frequency information, and customize a notification. Select SAVE.

  • Once you’ve saved the tracked medication, you may view or edit in the Medication Manager.

  • Guardians will now be notified with push medication notifications via the TIMEX app.

Device how-tos

Power up (fast charging)

The 600 mAh battery can provide up to 3 full days of mixed usage, and up to 7 days of standby time. Fully charge the battery in less than 2.5 hours and quickly get back to your activities.

2-Way Calling (How to make a call)

  • Select the Phone in the watch menu.

  • Select from several options to complete calls like Contacts, Dialer, Recent Calls, and Voice Mail.

  • Select the green call icon once a valid phone number has been entered to initiate the call.

  • Once the call is connected, you can adjust the volume or dialer for post-connected prompts. 2-Way Messaging (how to send a text or app message)

  • Select Messages in the watch menu.

  • Choose from Recent Messages to view a recent conversation or Send Message to create a new message. Select Send Message.

  • Choose the contact you want to send a message to.

  • Choose from App or Text. 2-Way Messaging (using an SMS text message)

  • When choosing to use the SMS text message feature, select the Text icon.

  • You may view a recent SMS message conversation or select the message bubble icon to create a new one. Select the message bubble icon.

  • You may select from designated preset messages such as “Hello!” or choose on-screen keyboard icon. Select the keyboard icon.

  • From the on-screen keyboard, you may enter a custom message and send it as an SMS text. 2-Way Messaging (using an App message)

  • When choosing app message, select from more robust options. Select voice message, text message, or emoji message.

  • When selecting voice message, you may send a voice recorded message, up to 30 seconds long, to TIMEX app contact.

  • When selecting app text message, you may send a preset message or customize using the on-screen keyboard.

  • When selecting emoji message, you may choose from over 20 popular emojis to customize their emoji app message. Location Tracking

  • Select MORE in the watch menu.

  • Select Check-in.

  • Select SEND to send your location to TIMEX App.

  • Verify location is sent, then select OK. SOS Button

How to initiate an SOS alert to your emergency contact.

  • From any menu, long-press the SOS side button for at least 3 seconds to initiate an SOS alert.

  • A long vibration feedback will alert you that an SOS has been initiated and a HELP! animation will appear on the watch screen. Continue to hold down the SOS button to complete an SOS alert.

  • Once the animation is finished after the long press of 5 seconds, the designated Emergency Contact will be called. If you let go of the SOS button before the animation is completed, the SOS alert will be canceled. Voice Commands

  • From any menu, double-press the SOS side button to launch the Voice Command interface.

  • Voice command UI will appear on the screen to prompt a command. Select the microphone icon to show available commands, or state their command clearly to complete a task. Available voice commands include:

    • “Help”
    • “Call…(name)”
    • “Send Message to..(name)”
    • “Show Weather” or “Weather”
    • “Show Steps”
    • “Show PAI”
    • “Show heartrate”
    • “Show Medications”
    • “Show Alarms”
    • “Show Reminders”
    • “Open Brightness”
    • “Show Sleep”
    • “Show Calculator”
    • “Show Sedentary Reminder”

New to T-Mobile

Carrier Freedom

We’ve made it easier than ever to switch to T-Mobile. When you switch from an eligible carrier to T-Mobile, we’ll reimburse your previous carrier’s remaining device payment balance and/or early termination fee (ETF). Carrier Freedom is now Family Freedom.

On this page:

  • Requirements for Carrier Freedom
  • Redemption process for Carrier Freedom
  • Getting your reimbursements
  • Legal Terms

Requirements

To participate in Carrier Freedom, you need to meet the following requirements:

  • Port in your number and activate a new voice line
  • You’ll need to port in (transfer) your number from an eligible postpaid carrier to a T-Mobile account.
    • You’ll need to port in your number and activate a new voice line of service.
    • This offer is not available to port-ins from, prepaid carriers, including T-Mobile Prepaid and Metro by T-Mobile, free Google Voice services, and all MVNOs using T-Mobile’s network.
    • This offer is also not available to port-ins of numbers that have been used with T-Mobile service within the past 90 days.
  • Trade-in your phone
  • You’ll need to trade-in a phone, and make sure of the following:
    • If you’re submitting for device plan reimbursement, the device you’re trading in must be the one on the device financing agreement from your previous carrier.
    • The device must be able to power on.
    • The LCD and display must be acceptable and there can be no liquid damage.
    • Turn off any of your device’s security features, such as activation lock, anti-theft, and Find My iPhone features.
    • The device has been on a payment plan for at least 90 days, and you’ve made at least three successful minimum payments.
    • You’ll need to accept the trade-in quote during your new phone purchase.
  • Buy a new phone
  • You’ll need to purchase a new phone via our Equipment Installment Plan.
  • Submit your device financing details and/or final bill
  • The information you need to show depends on the type of reimbursements you’re submitting for:
    • For a device financing reimbursement:
      • You’ll need to submit an image of the financing details, including carrier, device make & model, financing tenure, mobile number, and payoff amount.
      • You’ll need to have had a device payment plan with your current carrier for at least 90 days and you’ve made at least three successful minimum payments.
    • For early termination fee (ETF) reimbursement, you’ll need to submit a copy of your final bill showing the ETF.

Redemption process

You’ll need to complete the activation and port-in, as well as initiate the trade-in with your new phone order prior to submitting for reimbursement.

  • Your trade-in must be processed at the time of ordering your new phone.
    • In-store: You have the option of doing an instant trade-in where you give it to the associate at the time of purchase or you can defer your trade-in and return it to T-Mobile within 30 days.
    • Online or over the phone: Return the trade-in to T-Mobile within 30 days.
  • You will receive text message confirmation from T-Mobile when your trade-in device has been received and processed.
Ready to redeem

If you’ve completed the activation and port-in, initiated the trade-in, and have images of your device financing details and/or final bill information captured, you’re ready to follow these steps to perform the online reimbursement submission.

  • Scan the QR code or go to promotions.t-mobile.com within 30 days of the qualifying transaction.
  • Log in with your T-Mobile ID and account credentials.
  • Select the number you want to submit Carrier Freedom for.
  • Enter all the required information including:
    • Transaction date
    • The channel where the transaction took place
    • Transaction type
    • If you ported your number to T-Mobile
    • Transaction category
  • Under FINDING THE RIGHT SWITCHING OFFER:
    • In the drop-down, select Voice.
    • In the next drop-down, select Reimbursement Type: Device Financing Reimbursement or Early Termination Fee Reimbursement.
    • In the drop-down, select Previous Carrier, then select CONTINUE.
  • Read the “Terms & Conditions” including trade-in eligibility requirements and then select the check box next to “I have read and agree to the Terms & Conditions of this promotion”. select CONTINUE.
  • On the next page, you’ll need to “Select which numbers (max of 4 redemptions per account) you’d like to submit for Carrier Freedom”. Select the drop-down next to each line you want to submit for the selected reimbursement offer.
    • T-Mobile For Business, you will get an input box to manually type in each number you are submitting redemption for.
  • Under Contact Phone Number, “Select Number” in the drop-down. Select CONTINUE.
  • On the next page, you’ll find 3 Steps To Submit For Pay Off:
    • How to submit your payoff information: Customer gathers screenshots for each device being submitted.
    • Upload an image of each phone number:
      • Upload screenshots of final bill and/or device financing details page for each selected phone number.
      • Accepted image formats: .pdf, .jpg, or .png
      • Image limits: up to 5 MB per image and a max of 15 images
      • The name and address on the final bill does NOT need to match the info on your My T-Mobile account.
    • Select SUBMIT for processing. Please allow up to 3 days for a status update.
  • After the submission is finished processing, the page will display a message letting you know if your reimbursement was approved. (If it wasn’t approved, it means an error was found during the submission process, and a T-Mobile rep will contact you shortly to help you with the process.)
Submission status

You can check the status of a submission by logging in to the T-Mobile Redemption Center and selecting Check Status.

Getting your reimbursements

Device financing reimbursements

Here are some important things to know about device financing reimbursements:

  • After submitting for reimbursement, you should know within 3 days if your submission was successful. Allow 15 days after meeting all requirements to receive your reimbursement.
  • The device you’re trading in must be the one on the device financing agreement from your previous carrier.
  • The trade-in device must be received and pass inspection before the device financing reimbursement will be issued.
  • Max reimbursement per line is a combined total of $800 for both carrier device financing balance and ETF.
  • To be eligible for device financing reimbursement under this promotion:
    • You must have had an eligible locked phone on installment plans with your previous carrier for at least 90 days, and
    • You must have made at least three payments toward that installment plan.
  • Not included in reimbursements: taxes on device financing and any current or past due monthly service charges.
Early Termination Fee (ETF) reimbursements

Here are some important things to know about ETF reimbursements:

  • After submitting for reimbursement, you should know within 3 days if your submission was successful. Allow 15 days after meeting all requirements to receive your reimbursement.
  • Reimbursement is for a maximum of 4 voice lines per account.
  • Your trade-in device must be received and pass inspection before the ETF reimbursement will be issued.
  • The amount paid will be equal to the ETF amount your previous carrier charges for the type of device.
  • Max reimbursement per line is a combined total of $800 for both ETF and device financing.
  • Not included in reimbursements: taxes on ETF and any current or past due monthly service charges.
When you should expect to receive your reimbursement
  • Reimbursement generally takes place 15 days after the submission is approved and trade-in per line is received.
  • Prepaid virtual cards are sent via a text message typically within 24-48 hours after the Day 15 date. If you don’t get the message, you can access your prepaid virtual card information by checking your submission status page.
Didn’t receive or lost your virtual card SMS?

If you never received the SMS, or if you did but accidentally deleted it, you can still get your virtual card info by following these steps:

  • Go to T-Mobile’s Redemption Center.
  • Select GET STARTED.
  • Sign in to My T-Mobile with your T-Mobile ID.
  • On the ‘Submission Status’ page, select the one that states PAID. This will expand it to review more information for that submission.
  • Select REDEEM VIRTUAL CARD. You can also use the step-by-step walk through of this process found on our Switchers overview.
  • Confirm the mobile number.
  • Accept the terms and conditions.
  • Once registered, a page displays your virtual card information.

We’ve made it easier than ever to make the switch to T-Mobile. When you switch to T-Mobile from an eligible carrier, we’ll reimburse your previous carrier’s remaining device payment balance and/or early termination fee (ETF), up to $800 per line via virtual prepaid card (max of 4 per account), when you activate a new voice line, bring (port) your number to the new line, trade-in an eligible phone, purchase a new phone on an Equipment Installment Plan, and submit proof of your eligible device financing or early termination fees.

    • This offer is not available to port-ins from prepaid carriers, including T-Mobile Prepaid and Metro by T-Mobile, free Google Voice services, and all MVNOs using T-Mobile’s network.

T-Mobile Tuesdays

T-Mobile Tuesdays is a program that thanks T-Mobile customers with free stuff, great deals, and exclusive offers every Tuesday—just for being a customer. And every so often, you have a chance to win epic prizes like amazing vacations, the latest smartphones, gift cards, and more.

Get T-Mobile Tuesdays

On this page:

  • What is T-Mobile Tuesdays
  • Who’s eligible
  • Claiming and redeeming gifts and prizes
  • What’s up for grabs this week?

What is T-Mobile Tuesdays

We want to thank you for being a T-Mobile customer. What better way than hooking you up with free stuff?! Every week through the T-Life app, you can claim gift offers and you may have a chance to win prizes. New offers are available every week from Tuesday at 5 a.m. ET through Wednesday at 4:59:59 a.m. ET.

Who’s eligible

Any T-Mobile or Metro by T-Mobile customer on a qualifying branded monthly rate plan can participate. Qualifying rate plans include most consumer and business monthly plans that include voice and data. Every qualifying line can participate if considered to be in “active status.”

To be eligible, customers must be at least 18 years old, minors need to be at least 16 years of age with parental consent. and customers in Puerto Rico must be at least 21 years old.

To enter for a chance to win prizes, you must be a legal resident of any one of the fifty United States, Puerto Rico, United States Virgin Islands, or the District of Columbia and age of majority or at least sixteen (16) years of age and participating with parental supervision. The app and website(s) are not for use by people under the age of 16. Sometimes we run promotions on Twitter—check the rules for each contest to see any additional eligibility criteria

T-Mobile employees are only eligible to receive the weekly gift offers; they’re not eligible for the chance to win prizes.

*Excluded plan and account types:
  • DIGITS plans
  • Government
  • Mobile Internet
  • Pay as You Go
  • Prepaid without data
  • Partner and Wholesale Brands / MVNO
  • Suspended or Canceled accounts
  • T-Mobile Connect
  • Wearables
What if you’re not a T-Mobile customer?

Only T-Mobile and Metro by T-Mobile customers are eligible to receive THANKINGS every Tuesday. When available, non-customers can participate in sweepstakes for a chance to win prizes by visiting https://amoe.t-mobiletuesdays.com and following the registration instructions.

Claiming and redeeming gifts and prizes

To get your gifts and for your chance to win prizes, make sure you open the T-Life app to the Tuesdays tab every week at some point between Tuesday at 5 a.m. ET to Wednesday 4:59:59 a.m. ET. In the app, go through the list of gifts available and make sure you tap SAVE for the ones you want.

Once you save an offer, you can redeem it right away, or you can wait until later. If you decide to wait, just pay close attention to the date and time you have until to redeem the offer. Each gift or prize has its own expiration, sometimes ending within 24 hours. If you don’t redeem an offer right away, you can find it later in My Stuff.

My Stuff

In the Tuesdays section of T-Life, tap on My Stuff from the landing screen. In here, you can get details about your claimed gifts and prizes, including redemption method and specific terms and conditions.

What’s up for grabs this week?

Check out what we have in store for you this week by visiting one of these entry points. You’ll find all the offer details and requirements included with each gift and prize.

  • T-Mobile Tuesdays overview
  • Non-T-Mobile customers interested in contests or drawings, check out https://amoe.t-mobiletuesdays.com

Not Sold by T-Mobile

Bring your own device (BYOD) guide

As millions have already learned, it’s easy to bring your unlocked device to T-Mobile. Most phones can work on our network but we suggest you check out these details before you start using your unlocked Android or Windows device.

On this page:

  • BYOD compatibility
  • Check eligibility
  • Start using your device
  • Device compatibility

BYOD compatibility

T-Mobile is unable to guarantee devices from other carriers or those without T-Mobile software will work on our network. For additional details, check out the Non-T-Mobile phone & software disclaimer.

  • T-Mobile isn’t able to test Non-T-Mobile Devices’ call quality, performance, data speed, feature compatibility, or other functionalities. Experiences may vary depending on the original carrier settings.
  • Contact the manufacturer with any questions or problems regarding the device functionality, operation, or performance.
  • Check your warranty and contract with your current carrier to determine what conditions apply to unlocking the device.
  • Coverage and access to our high speed 4G LTE network is not guaranteed and isn’t available in some areas.
  • Your device must support the frequencies used by T-Mobile.

Check eligibility

  • A device must be unlocked to be compatible with the T-Mobile network. Check out Unlock your mobile wireless device if needed.
  • T-Mobile can’t provide an unlock code, contact the original carrier to request an unlock code.
  • If your device isn’t compatible after using these steps, you can trade in your current device and upgrade your device to a T-Mobile phone or tablet.
BYOD Check online
  • Go to T-Mobile’s IMEI Compatibility checker​ webpage.
  • Enter your IMEI and select Check phone to determine the BYOD eligibility.
    • If the checker shows “No match found,” verify the device supports T-Mobile frequencies​. Contact the manufacturer if your unsure of the device frequencies.
    • Determine if your device supports VoLTE and Extended Range LTE.

Start using your device

Need service?
  • Use the device’s user guide to determine which T-Mobile SIM card you need to purchase, check out Buy a SIM card.
  • If you are not a T-Mobile customer and need help activating your phone or tablet, find a plan that is right for you.
Already have an account?

Internet and picture messaging settings need to be updated to work on the T-Mobile network.

  • Insert the activate SIM card, turn on the device, and open a web page.
  • Some devices may update automatically but if not, change your settings using the BYOD T-Mobile data & APN settings.
  • Contact the device manufacturer for further instructions if data and picture messaging are still not working.

Device compatibility

If your device is only partially compatible with T-Mobile’s advanced network, we’ll send you a message to let you know after you activate your SIM. While you can still use the device, you may not experience the full benefits of our network. Here’s why that can happen:

Partial compatibility
  • Partially compatible devices may not support all the same network technologies and frequencies used on the T-Mobile network.
  • This can result in reduced coverage and slower data speeds compared to fully compatible devices.
  • We recommend setting up Wi-Fi calling to help improve your experience indoors.
Incompatible
  • Incompatible devices cannot access minimum network technologies and frequencies required to use the T-Mobile network.
  • This could lead to reduced access and limited coverage compared to fully compatible devices.
  • They also lack V-E911 capability, a crucial feature for accessing emergency services when connected to Wi-Fi Calling.
Software updates
  • If a manufacturer stops supporting a device, it will no longer receive software updates.
  • Certain apps, like our T Life app that offers free benefits every Tuesday, may not be compatible with older software versions.
How to improve compatibility

Network compatibility is built into device hardware; you must replace your device to take advantage of newer network technologies and frequencies.

Non-T-Mobile phone & software disclaimer

T-Mobile cannot and does not guarantee the functionality or performance of any handsets or devices that were not sold by T-Mobile or an authorized dealer of T-Mobile (“Non-T-Mobile Devices”) for use on the T-Mobile network or while roaming on any other network. Nor do we guarantee the functionality of any handsets or devices that do not have a software version that was sold or updated by T-Mobile (for example, rooted devices).

As a courtesy, we provide the T-Mobile Internet and picture messaging (MMS) settings for some Non-T-Mobile Devices. However, device troubleshooting that is not related to the T-Mobile network (T-Mobile Internet and picture messaging settings) is not provided for such Non-T-Mobile Devices. T-Mobile does not provide troubleshooting on Non-T-Mobile Devices for any issues not related to the T-Mobile network.

T-Mobile cannot guarantee the effectiveness of these settings, nor their placement in the device and therefore does not assume any liability for the lack of effectiveness of these settings for non-T-Mobile devices.

We strongly recommend that our customers contact the manufacturers of their Non-T-Mobile Devices with any questions or problems regarding the functionality, operation, or performance of their Non-T-Mobile Devices.

T-Mobile data & APN settings

Make sure you have the right data settings so services like the internet and picture messaging work.

On this page:

  • Automatic data settings & network reset
  • Manually input data settings

Automatic data settings & network reset

All devices sold by T-Mobile (and many that aren’t) support automatic configuration of your network and data settings. To reset your settings to default, choose your device manufacturer. These steps will reset all network settings and remove any saved Wi-Fi Networks or Bluetooth pairings, as well as reset any app-specific data restrictions.

Alcatel
  • From any home screen, swipe up.
  • Choose Settings > System > Reset options. If you don’t have Reset options, choose Advanced first.
  • Select Reset Wi-Fi, Cellular & Bluetooth > Reset settings.
  • If prompted, enter your PIN or Password.
  • Choose Reset settings.
Apple
  • From the Home screen, select Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone or iPad > Reset.
  • Choose Reset Network Settings.
  • If prompted, enter your PIN or Password.
  • Confirm selection.
CAT
  • From the Home screen, swipe up to display your apps.
  • Choose Settings > System > Advanced > Reset options > Reset Wi-Fi, mobile & Bluetooth > Reset settings.
  • If prompted, enter your PIN or Password.
  • Choose Reset settings.
Coolpad
  • From the Home screen, select App > Settings > General settings > Mobile network > Advanced.
  • Select Access Point Names to check the existing APNs.
  • Press the left soft key, then select Reset to default.
Google
  • From the Home screen, swipe up to display your apps.
  • Select Settings > System > Reset options > Reset Bluetooth & Wi-Fi.
  • Select Reset again to confirm.
LG
  • From the Home screen, swipe up to display your apps.
  • Choose Settings > System > Restart & reset > Network settings reset > Reset Settings > Reset Settings.
  • If prompted, enter your PIN or Password.
  • Choose Reset settings. A ‘Network settings have been reset’ message briefly flashes to indicate the reset is complete.
Motorola
  • From the Home screen, swipe up to display your apps.
  • Choose Settings > System > Reset options > Reset Wi-Fi, mobile & Bluetooth > Reset settings.
  • If prompted, enter your PIN or Password.
  • Choose Reset settings.
Nokia
  • From the Home screen, swipe up to display your apps.
  • Choose Settings > System > Advanced > Reset options > Reset Wi-Fi, mobile & Bluetooth > Reset Settings.
  • If prompted, enter your PIN or Password.
  • Choose Reset Settings. Once complete, a confirmation window will appear.
OnePlus
  • From the Home screen, swipe up to display your apps.
  • Choose Settings > System settings or Additional settings.
  • Select Back up and reset > Reset phone > Reset network settings.
  • If prompted, enter your PIN or Password.
  • Choose Reset settings again to confirm.
REVVL
  • From the Home screen, swipe up to display your apps.
  • Choose Settings > System > Reset options > Reset Wi-Fi, mobile & Bluetooth > Reset Settings.
  • If prompted, enter your PIN or Password.
  • Choose Reset Settings again to confirm.
Samsung
  • From the Home screen, swipe up to display your apps.
  • Choose Settings > General Management > Reset.
  • Select Reset network settings or Reset mobile network settings, then choose Reset settings.
  • If prompted, enter your PIN or Password.
  • Choose Reset. Once complete, a confirmation window will appear.
SCHOK
  • From the Home screen, select Menu (OK key) > Tools & Settings > Settings > Wireless & networks > Cellular networks.
  • Select Access Point Names > Options (right Soft key).
  • Select Reset to default > Yes (right Soft key).
TCL
  • From the Home screen, swipe up to display your apps.
  • Choose Settings > System > Reset Network settings reset > Reset settings.
  • If prompted, enter your PIN or Password.
  • Choose Reset settings.
Wiko Voix
  • From the Home screen, swipe up to display your apps.
  • Choose Settings > System > Reset options > Reset Wi-Fi, mobile, & Bluetooth > Reset settings > Reset settings.
  • If prompted, enter your PIN or Password.
  • Choose Reset. Wait for the device to reset.

Manually input data settings

This section will walk you through setting up internet and pictures messaging (MMS) on a non-T-Mobile phone if automatic configuration is not supported, but there are a few things to keep in mind before you get started:

  • We can’t guarantee these settings will make an unsupported device fully functional on the T-Mobile network.
  • Customer Care may not be able to help with unsupported device configuration, but you can always ask questions in the Community.
  • Check out the Non-T-Mobile phone & software disclaimer for more info.
Internet and Picture Messaging
  • Access Point Name (APN): fast.t-mobile.com

55+ plan verification

If you’re interested in signing up for or switching to a T-Mobile 55+ plan, check your eligibility and learn how to verify your status. Learn more about all of our plans.

How to get a T-Mobile 55+ plan

Call 1-800-TMOBILE or go to your nearest T-Mobile store to activate or change to a 55+ plan.

  • As the Billing Responsible Party, your age needs to be verified if you’ve already signed up for a 55+ plan or if you are interested in adding a plan.
  • Verify your age within 45 days from activation or plan change, otherwise, your plan will be switched to the standard plan version and risk a price increase.
  • Verify your eligibility by visiting a T-Mobile store with a valid government-issued ID and we will walk you through the process.

Requirements and eligibility

  • A valid government-issued ID must be provided at the time of activation or plan change to verify eligibility. Examples of acceptable government-issued IDs include:
    • Valid U.S. Driver’s License issued by the DMV with photo
    • Valid ID Card issued by the DMV
    • U.S. issued passport (passport cards are not accepted)
  • The Billing Responsible Party must be 55 years old or older to qualify.
  • If the Billing Responsible Party (BRP) on your plan is not 55 years old or older, you will need to complete a Change of Responsibility. Review Transfer account or line ownership for more information
Who’s eligible
  • U.S. and Puerto Rico residents, 55 years or older.
  • Proof of age is required.
  • Maximum of one Unlimited 55 account per Social Security Number. Multiple accounts with 1 - 4 line versions of this plan are not allowed.
Who’s not eligible?
  • Accounts that the Billing Responsible Party is not verified to be at least 55 years old
  • Business, Government, or Prepaid accounts.
  • Individuals who have or need more than four lines.

Activate HD video streaming

You can turn on HD video streaming on your device if you’re on a plan with optimized video streaming.

On this page:

  • Activation steps
  • HD video resolution details
  • Full terms

Activation steps

If you don’t have a plan that includes HD streaming, refer to Find the right plan for you​ to add a plan today.

From T Life
  • Access T Life on your device.
  • Select Manage then choose the Gear icon.
  • Select Device settings > Video quality.
  • If you have multiple lines on your account, tap the phone number to choose a line.
  • Next to HD Video Resolution, toggle it ON or OFF.
From T-Mobile.com
  • Log in to T-Mobile.com with your T-Mobile ID. If you don’t have one, register for a T-Mobile ID​.
  • Select PROFILE.
  • Go to MEDIA SETTINGS.
  • By HD Video Resolution, set the option to ON or OFF.

HD video resolution details

  • Activating HD video resolution only provides the ability to enable higher-resolution video streams by turning off video optimization. It doesn’t change the actual, available resolution of streaming video.
  • Video resolution isn’t determined by T-Mobile, but rather it’s determined by the video content provider like YouTube or Netflix.
  • Once you turn it on, HD video streaming availability should take effect immediately, but it may require closing and re-opening the app or browser window, or restarting your device.

Full terms

All on-network data used, including free streaming data, counts toward the heavy-user threshold of 50GB in a billing cycle, after which a T-Mobile-branded customer will no longer receive highest priority on the network. When an HD video is active, streaming high-definition video will use data much faster than optimized video, and brings up to the possibility of de-prioritization if you use enough data to reach that limit in a given month. (Learn more about T-Mobile’s Open Internet disclosures.)

411 directory assistance

411 directory assistance allows you to reach a live operator for directory assistance from your T-Mobile phone. To connect, dial 411, and send the call. Each 411 call costs up to $2.99, plus talk time for prepaid plans. Things to keep in mind when using 411 directory assistance:

  • Three directory listings are included per call.
  • Using toll-free area codes to call 411 won’t avoid the directory assistance charge.
  • International directory assistance isn’t available.

Call Forwarding

Call forwarding allows you to forward your incoming calls to another number. You can set it up to forward all your calls immediately. Or, you can set it up to forward if you don’t answer the call, if your phone is turned off, or if you’re out of signal range.

Be aware of the following when using call forwarding:

  • You can’t forward calls to international numbers.

  • You can only forward calls to 10- or 11-digit numbers.

  • Forwarding while roaming depends on the host country’s network capabilities. For steps on call forwarding:

  • Go to the Devices page.

  • Search, filter, or select your device.

  • Select Calling & Contacts in the How Tos section.

  • Select Block and/or manage calls.

  • Follow the instructions for setting up call forwarding for your device.

Call waiting

  • Call waiting and call hold are used together.
  • If you receive an incoming call while you’re on the phone, you hear a tone letting you know another call is coming in.
  • If you answer the incoming call, the first call is automatically placed on hold. You can then switch between the calls or join the calls using conference calling.
  • For prepaid plans, minutes are deducted for each incoming call when using call waiting.

To activate and manage your data account visit:

Consumer versus Non-Consumer Text Messaging

We want text messaging to remain a trusted form of communication. To support this goal, there are many systems in place to ensure a healthy text message ecosystem. This page will help you better understand how text messaging works.

On this page:

  • Types of messages
  • How healthy messaging works
  • Frequently asked questions

Types of messages

The wireless industry classifies text messages into two categories, consumer and non-consumer messaging. Each of these types of messages has its own route on the T-Mobile network.

Consumer messaging

These types of messages are sent by individuals directly to other people from their handsets. Consumer messages travel through SPAM filtering systems meant to block non-consumer messages our subscribers did not request, especially those messages with fraudulent or other harmful intent.

Non-consumer messaging

All other messages are non-consumer messages. Examples of non-consumer messages include:

  • Two-factor authentication codes
  • Account notifications
  • Billing related messages
  • Messages with transportation and delivery services
  • Political messages
  • High volume messaging For these messages to reach our customers they must be part of an approved campaign. They are subject to ongoing compliance and monitoring obligations. There is often a fee associated for those who want to deliver a non-consumer messaging campaign to our customers.

How healthy messaging works

Aggregators are the gateway for non-consumer messaging traffic, not just on our network but on the networks of all mobile carriers in the United States. We contract with messaging aggregators across the industry that review and approve non-consumer messaging campaigns on behalf of their clients. In addition to the various legal and regulatory obligations applicable to non-consumer messaging, these aggregators must adhere to T-Mobile’s Code of Conduct, as well as the wireless industry’s approved Messaging Principles and Best Practices so that they appropriately protect our customers and our network. These aggregators are responsible for reviewing the content of messaging campaigns as well as ensuring these campaigns remain compliant throughout the lifecycle. We refer to messaging campaigns submitted and approved in this manner as “sanctioned route” messaging. Approved messaging campaigns are not subject to SPAM filtering.

The most important step in running a non-consumer messaging campaign on sanctioned routes is to choose trusted aggregators. There are several options for non-consumer messaging traffic on sanctioned routes, including short codes, toll-free messaging, and as of Fall 2020, ten-digit long code or “10DLC” messaging.

Unfortunately, to avoid paying the business fees and following the compliance steps required for non-consumer messaging, some unscrupulous aggregators put non-consumer messaging into the consumer channel on “gray routes.” Businesses that unwittingly use grey-route for the delivery of their messages risk having their messages delayed or simply not delivered, as well as having their reputations and operations damaged.

We have long been an industry leader in fighting scammers and spammers. To protect our customers, we are taking steps to eliminate unsanctioned gray route traffic on our network. As the non-commercial messaging space continues to grow, we will continue to improve the messaging experience, while also maintaining the health of the messaging ecosystem

Frequently asked questions

I want to send non-consumer messages and have no idea where to start. Can you point me in the right direction?

There are a range of independent reputable companies offering messaging services on the sanctioned path that may suit your needs. We recommend you reach out to Kaleyra, Infobip, Sinch, Vibes Media, Twilio, or Cisco directly.

What is the difference between short code, toll free, and 10DLC messaging?

Short codes are 5 - 6 digit numbers that are used for texting only and are leased from the Short Code Registry. Toll-free is text enabling a toll-free number (8XX) that can be called or texted. All toll-free text messaging is administered through ZipWhip. Ten-digit Long Code, or 10DLC messaging, is enabling any phone number to be texted. Your aggregator can help walk you through specifics in more detail.

I was buying a service to send 10DLC messages prior to Fall 2020. Were those messages gray route? Will they move to the sanctioned route?

All non-consumer 10DLC messages sent prior to Fall 2020 were traveling the gray route, as the systems and sanctioned route to support 10DLC were not yet fully operational. Many aggregators have been working to transition their traffic to the newly established sanctioned route. The best way to learn your aggregator’s transition plans is to ask them directly.

I noticed there is some prohibited content in the T-Mobile Code of Conduct. What does that mean?

T-Mobile’s Code of Conduct has a list of prohibited content for non-consumer messaging campaigns. While illegal content will never be allowed, some campaigns do require additional review for evaluation of our exception process. If you want to run a campaign with content that you are concerned may be prohibited, work with your aggregator to determine if you are eligible for an approved exception. Please note that prohibitions are about content and not the nature of the organization running the message.

Can I just connect directly to T-Mobile to send non-consumer messages?

Only aggregators can connect directly to industry networks for non-consumer messaging. There are two reasons for this. First, non-consumer messaging campaigns often reach people across wireless providers and the aggregators maintain connections to all networks to have that reach for their clients. Second, non-consumer messaging campaigns have compliance obligations, and the aggregators help organizations navigate these requirements.

I’ve heard you can send a text by e-mail. What is that route for?

The e-mail to text gateway is a legacy system that may eventually be decommissioned in the future. It is designed for low volume consumer traffic only and cannot handle a significant volume of messages. For that reason, all non-consumer messaging is prohibited on the e-mail to text gateway, and even high volume consumer messaging may be blocked as it can impact the system’s ability to handle messages for all customers. If you need to send non-consumer or high-volume consumer messaging, work with an aggregator as their connections can handle these message volumes.

How can I know if the aggregator I’m working with is using a gray route or sanctioned route for my 10DLC campaign?

All entities that wish to send sanctioned 10DLC messaging traffic must be registered before their campaign messages will be approved for delivery on our network. If your aggregator is delivering traffic using sanctioned routes they will be aware of this registration process and will be able to provide you full registration details.

Are there certain key words that trigger filtering of non-consumer messaging?

Non-consumer messaging travelling on the sanctioned route is not subject to filtering. But gray route messaging is subject to T-Mobile SPAM filtering.

Why is non-consumer 10DLC sanctioned route just being launched now?

The demand to use 10-digit numbers for non-consumer messaging is a relatively new phenomenon, and there was a significant amount of technical work to create the systems to support it. During 2020, all major wireless providers completed that technical work and testing.

I’m a consumer who is receiving unwanted messages/messages that appear to be scams/messages I didn’t sign up for. Is there anything I can do?

Yes! First, reply to those messages with “STOP.” Legitimate platforms will honor this request and remove you from future messages. Second, please forward those messages to 7726 (SPAM). This allows us to locate and mitigate spam or scam messages more quickly.

Where can I go for more information?

You can find more information regarding non-consumer messaging on the wireless industry association’s website.

ctia.org

ctia.org

ctia.org

ctia.org

My messaging partner (aggregator) didn’t charge me previously, now they are charging me and telling me it’s T-Mobile’s charge, can you explain?

Please contact your aggregator. There may be fees associated with the sanctioned delivery of non-consumer messages charged by the messaging provider, but T-Mobile does not have visibility to what an aggregator partner may charge their customers for messaging services.

How does sending M2M SMS messages between two IoT devices work?

M2M SMS traffic is also routed by the same companies that handle non-consumer messaging. However, M2M and non-consumer traffic cannot be mixed together. M2M traffic must be isolated from all non-consumer intended to reach handsets and messaging service companies can help you set up these messaging connections.
