New T-Mobile customer

If you are new to T-Mobile, it is easy to sign up online. If you have any questions, Contact Us.

Existing T-Mobile Prepaid account

If you have an existing T-Mobile Prepaid account, you can change to a Connect by T-Mobile UNL Talk & Text plan.

Manage your plan

Need help?
  • If you don’t have Connect by T-Mobile as an available plan option or if you have a different account type, you will need to migrate your existing T-Mobile account to get Connect by T-Mobile.
  • If you do not want to migrate your current number, go back to Connect by T-Mobile to sign up. for a new line. You can cancel your existing account later if needed.

Migrate your account to Connect by T-Mobile Prepaid

Use this process to migrate an existing T-Mobile Prepaid line to a new Connect by T-Mobile Prepaid account, or for existing lines that do not have the option to change to Connect by T-Mobile online.

What you will need to get started

Before you can migrate your account to Connect by T-Mobile you will need these items:

  • A new SIM Card (applicable cost associated). Your current T-Mobile SIM card will not work with Connect by T-Mobile Prepaid but you can keep your existing number. If you have more than one T-Mobile number you want to migrate to Connect by T-Mobile, Contact Us.
  • The mobile number from your existing account you want to migrate.
  • Existing T-Mobile account number.
  • PIN/Passcode for your existing T-Mobile account which is different from your T-Mobile.com password - it’s the one you use when you call us.
  • Secondary email address (different from the one associated with your existing T-Mobile account).
What you need to know
  • Some services and benefits are unavailable for Connect by T-Mobile, such as Device Protection and Netflix On Us.
  • Any existing service promotions such as free lines or monthly discounts will be lost and may not be available if you decide to convert back in the future.
  • When you migrate your account any existing outstanding service or device payment balance on your consumer account will immediately become due.
  • Your voicemail account will be reset and you will lose any voicemails not saved to your device.
  • Your account tenure will reset, which may affect your ability to qualify for select programs in the near future.
  • Keep your account active until you activate your new SIM card.
  • Once your new SIM card is activated it will take 2 - 4 hours to transfer your existing number to your new SIM card.
Next, follow these steps

Some steps may direct you to say you don’t have a T-Mobile account or SIM card already. Continue to follow the step-by-step instructions outlined and your account will migrate successfully.

  • Go to https://prepaid.t-mobile.com/home.
  • Select Shop
  • Select Bring Your Own Device to use your existing phone. If you want to purchase a new device Contact Us.
  • Enter your ZIP code.
  • Select Continue.
  • In the Check IMEI section, check if your device will work with T-Mobile service or select Skip.
  • In the SIM card activation section, choose I need to buy a T-Mobile SIM card.
  • Select Continue. Your current SIM card will not work with Connect by T-Mobile Prepaid. Choose I have a T-Mobile SIM card if you have a T-Mobile branded SIM card that has never been used before.
  • Select New Customer when asked if you Are you an existing customer? We are creating a new Prepaid account your existing number will transfer to.
  • In the Product Selection, select Connect by T-Mobile plan. You can also select See More to learn about what each plan includes.
  • Select Go to Cart.
  • Verify your SIM card and plan selection.
  • Select Check Out on the Shopping Cart screen. Do not add on additional lines if you intend to migrate more than one mobile number to Connect by T-Mobile. Instead, Contact Us.
  • You will be prompted to Sign Up or Log in. Choose Sign Up and enter your new account information, then select Continue:
    • Email Address, which must be different from the one associated with your original T-Mobile account.
    • 4-digit PIN
    • Name
    • Address, select Original or Suggested address if a pop-up appears
    • Preferred language
  • Enter a Line nickname if you want For example, “My Line” or “Jennifer’s line” and select Use your existing number.
  • Next, enter details from your existing T-Mobile account:
    • Mobile Number
    • Account Number
    • PIN/Passcode
  • Complete the emergency address e911 information: Opt out or Opt in (default).
  • Add primary place of use address.
  • Select Continue.
  • Add an email address under Shipping notifications.
  • Select Continue.
  • Enter your payment method and address.
  • Review and agree to the payment terms and conditions.
  • Select Continue.
  • Review the order and Terms & Conditions.
  • Select Accept & Place Order to finish.
  • An on-screen message will confirm your order has been placed.
Still have questions?

Check out our Connect by T-Mobile FAQs for more information on these plans. You can also engage our Community for help with general questions about this process.

SiriusXM subscription & billing

Smartphone Mobile Hotspot (Wi-Fi sharing and tethering)

Smartphone Mobile Hotspot (SMHS) - also referred to as Mobile Hotspot, Wi-Fi Sharing, or tethering - lets you securely share your device’s Internet connection with up to 10 Wi-Fi-enabled devices on T-Mobile’s high-speed nationwide network. If you want a plan with Mobile Hotspot, check out our latest plans!

On this page:

  • About Mobile Hotspot
  • Use Mobile Hotspot
  • Check Mobile Hotspot amount & usage
  • Mobile Hotspot Data Passes
  • Troubleshooting

About Mobile Hotspot

What is Mobile Hotspot
  • Mobile Hotspot is included with many plans, such as Experience More, Experience Beyond, Go5G plans, and more.
  • Mobile Hotspot lets you share the high-speed data of your phone, tablet, or Wi-Fi Hotspot with up to 10 other Wi-Fi-enabled or tethered devices.
  • Price and high-speed Mobile Hotspot data allotment varies depending on your plan.
How Mobile Hotspot works
  • Mobile Hotspot on your device is different from location hotspots, like the Wi-Fi you connect to at a coffee shop or airport, and hotspot devices, like the devices sold by T-Mobile.
  • While you have Mobile Hotspot turned on, you can still make and receive calls and texts on your phone.
  • If you use your high-speed Mobile Hotspot allotment (such as 15GB), your Mobile Hotspot speed will be reduced until the end of your billing cycle.
  • To add more Mobile Hotspot to your current plan, use T-Life or log into T-Mobile.com to view available options.

Use Mobile Hotspot

You’ll need the following to use Mobile Hotspot on your device
  • A Wi-Fi-enabled or Bluetooth-enabled device (such as your phone).
  • A plan that includes Mobile Hotspot. Most plans include it - check out About Mobile Hotspot for details.
  • Coverage as Mobile Hotspot only works in 5G and 4G LTE coverage: View our coverage map.
Turn on and start using
  • On your Mobile Hotspot device (such as your phone), turn on Personal Hotspot or Wi-Fi Sharing (typically from the Settings app).
    • Go to T-Mobile Support > Device Assistance for device-specific steps.
    • Select your device, then open the Connections & Network menu for steps.
  • On the device you want to share data with, connect to the Mobile Hotspot network you just turned on. If you don’t want to use Wi-Fi, you can use a USB cable to connect to other devices (additional software and setup may be required on your device - check the Devices page for steps).

Check Mobile Hotspot amount & usage

  • Log in to T-Mobile.com from a browser and select Usage > Data.
  • View how much Mobile Hotspot data you’ve used. Select a line for additional details.

Mobile Hotspot Data Passes

Mobile Hotspot Data Passes provide you with additional high-speed on-network mobile hotspot data (10GB) to supplement your monthly data bucket on a Go5G or Experience plan.

  • Can be added to your voice line multiple times per month.
  • Eligible to Experience and Go5G plans.
  • Only one hotspot pass is active at a time. The next pass starts when the current pass is depleted or expires after 30 days - whichever comes first.
  • Once you use all your high-speed mobile hotspot data, you will continue to have unlimited mobile hotspot data based on your voice plan.
  • Hotspot passes will only work on network (domestic) and are not intended for international use.
  • You receive automatic SMS notifications when 80% and 100% of the Data Pass is used.
Add a pass from My T-Mobile
  • Go to My T-Mobile and log in to your account.
  • Click the Account tab at the top of the page or click Manage Add Ons and Benefits in the “I want to”…box.
  • Select the line you wish to add the data pass to.
  • Under One-Time Data Pass, select the desired data pass from the list and select Continue.
  • Select a date for the data pass to start.
    • If you don’t select a date, it will start immediately.
    • If you future date a pass, the effective date can be changed on My T-Mobile.
  • Click Agree & Submit.
Add a pass from the T-Life app
  • Open the T-Life app on your device.
  • Click the Manage tab on the bottom right of the app and select the line you wish to add the data pass to.
  • Under Benefits, select Manage add-ons and data.
  • Under One-time Data Pass, select the desired data pass from the list and select Continue.
  • Select a date for the data pass to start.
    • If you don’t select a date, it will start immediately.
    • If you future data a pass, the effective date can be changed in the T-Life app.
  • Click Agree & Submit.

Troubleshooting

Refer to the following resources:

  • Mobile Hotspot troubleshooting
  • Internet and data issues
  • Issues connecting game systems, TVs, or other devices to your Mobile Hotspot: Contact your device manufacturer for support as we can’t guarantee Mobile Hotspot will be compatible with all devices.

About the app

T-Life is the all-in-one app designed to simplify your T-Mobile experience. Whether you’re managing your account, shopping the latest devices, or unlocking exclusive T-Mobile perks, T-Life puts everything you need in one place so you can stay connected, stay informed, and get the most out of being a T-Mobile customer. Find out more.

T-Life is designed for devices running Android 11 / Apple iOS 17 or higher.

Getting started

  • Download and install the T-Life app.
  • Open the T-Life app. If prompted, sign in with your T-Mobile ID.
  • Review and agree to the terms & conditions.
  • Agree to the Notification and Location permissions for the app.

Use the app

Choose one of the features below for steps!

  • Account Management to manage your plan, features, and services
  • T-Mobile Tuesdays to see and redeem your offers
  • SyncUP KIDS Watch to keep your family safe
  • SyncUP DRIVE to find your vehicle
  • SyncUP TRACKER to track your belongings
  • Scam Shield to protect yourself
  • T-Mobile MONEY to manage your finances
  • T-Satellite to get the best connection in remote areas

Settings & support

Notification Permissions
  • From the Home tab, select the Manage or Account tab.
  • Choose the settings (gear) icon.
  • Select Push Notifications.
  • Select Tuesdays and Magenta Status.
  • Switch the toggle on to “Allow Notifications.”
Location Permissions
  • From the Home tab, select the Manage or Account tab.
  • Choose the settings (gear) icon.
  • Select Settings on Android or Update on iOS devices next to Location access.
  • Choose OK to open the phone’s location settings.
  • Select the desired location permissions. Always allowed is preferred.
Change Language

The T-Life app automatically switches between English and Spanish based on the device’s language. Some Android devices have settings to customize the language of specific apps that overrides this behavior.

Edit Profile
  • From the Home tab, select the Manage or Account tab.
  • Choose the settings (gear) icon.
  • Select Profile.
  • Choose a field to edit it, like your name or addresses.
Quick Tour
  • From the Home tab, select the Manage or Account tab.
  • Choose the settings (gear) icon.
  • Select Help > Quick Tours > T-Life.
Customer Support
  • From the Home tab, select the Manage or Account tab.
  • Choose the settings (gear) icon.
  • Select Help > Customer support.
Report issue
  • With the T-Life app open to issue, shake your device.
  • Select Report an issue.
  • Select the category of the issue or choose T-Life for issues not listed.
  • Type in your email address and a description of your issue.
  • Select the send icon to submit.

T-Mobile AppManager & AppSelector

AppSelector is a feature that gives you more control over the apps that can be installed on your device during the initial setup process.

45 days after activation, AppManager will recommend a list of unused apps you can choose to uninstall to free up space and optimize device performance. You will also get a recommendation for apps that you may enjoy. AppManager will run every 45 days unless you opt out of the service.

On this page:

  • About AppSelector and AppManager
  • Remove the notification
  • Uninstall
  • Compatible devices
  • Troubleshooting
  • FAQs

About AppSelector and AppManager

AppSelector
  • AppSelector gives you the ability to easily select and install various applications when you first begin setting up your new device. AppSelector is available on select Android devices. Review list below for eligibility.
  • AppSelector will automatically notify you approximately 15 minutes after setting up your new device, or when you have performed a master reset on an existing device. At this time, you’ll be able to open, delay or skip forever.
    • If you delay for later, a notification will appear in the status bar until it’s been turned off.
    • If you skip the notification, you’ll never be notified again.
    • If you open, it will ask you a few options for better app recommendations, then you select the apps you’d like to install including recommended apps.
  • Once the setup is complete, it can be found in your device app settings.
  • Installed apps will appear in the app tray, just like any other downloaded app.
  • All applications downloaded using AppSelector, are managed and updated through the Google Play Store after the initial setup is complete-just like any other app.
AppManager
  • AppManager is a quick and easy way to find and remove unused apps on your phone and discover new ones.
  • 45 days after activating your new device, AppManager will prompt you to review your apps.
    • You can either choose to open the application or dismiss the notification to be reminded in the future.
    • If you dismiss the notification, you will receive another notification in 24 hours. After 3 dismisses, notifications will stop.
  • AppManager uses the embedded app Adapt or Content Manager to check what apps are installed and push app updates & notifications.
  • Data usage information is shared with the app developer Unity for future improvements.
    • You must provide consent to share your data usage for AppManager to run.
    • To change permissions, search your Settings for Usage Data Access and choose Device Manager.

Remove the notification

If you choose not to utilize the AppSelector or AppManager experience and need help removing the notification, follow these steps:

  • Access the status bar and long press on the AppSelector or AppManager notification.
  • Select Turn Off Notifications.

Uninstall

If you would like to uninstall AppSelector or AppManager from your device, follow these steps:

  • Access the Settings app on your device.
  • Select Apps or Apps & notification settings.
  • Locate and select the AppSelector or AppManager app, then select Uninstall.

Compatible devices

  • AppSelector is available on most T-Mobile and Metro devices operating on Android 8.1 and above.
  • AppManager is currently available on LG K51 and Samsung A11 and A21 devices.

Troubleshooting

If you are experiencing issues with AppSelector, follow these troubleshooting steps.

Error message “Oops.. something went wrong” appears
  • Check that the device has at least 2 bars of signal.
  • Make sure the device has cellular data enabled.
  • Make sure that Airplane Mode is not turned on.
  • Test to make sure the device can connect to the internet, then open the app and select TRY AGAIN.
Apps that were selected do not appear in the app tray
  • Check that the device has at least two bars of signal.
  • Make sure the device has cellular data enabled.
  • Make sure that Airplane Mode is not turned on.
  • Make sure you wait between 5 to 10 minutes, to allow time to pass for apps to download.
  • If the apps do not appear after 10 minutes, download the apps through the Play Store.

FAQs

I accidentally dismissed AppManager and want to run it manually. How can I pull this back up?

Currently we do not have a way to launch AppManager directly. You must select the notification to access the app.

Is AppSelector required for me to get AppManager?

Yes. AppManager is a feature of AppSelector.

Is there a cost to use AppManager?

No, all applications in AppManager are free to download. However, individual apps may have associated costs directly from the 3rd party app providers such as in-app purchases or subscription offers.

Is AppManager available on both Android and iOS devices?

No, AppManager is only available on select T-Mobile Android phones.

Do I have to be on a specific rate plan to use AppManager?

No. Any T-Mobile customer with an eligible device can use AppManager.

Will the usage from AppManager deplete my monthly data allotment?

Yes, standard data rates will apply.

Why did I get a notification to provide consent to sharing information with Unity?

We work with our vendor Unity to recommend apps and make future improvements to App Manager. Google has a new policy update for their Mobile Bundled Applications which requires consent from our customers to share data with third parties.

What personal information are you sharing with Unity?

We are sharing your data usage information with Unity. Your personal information is protected.

T-Mobile Connected PC

Learn how to activate T-Mobile data on a Windows computer with eSIM.

On this page:

  • What you need to use it
  • Activate T-Mobile Service
  • Download your eSIM
  • Connect to T-Mobile data
  • Change your plan
  • Delete eSIM
  • Get Help

What you need to use it

  • A Windows based computer with an eSIM
  • Running Windows 10 Creator Edition (1703) or newer
  • Access to the internet over Wi-Fi or Ethernet
  • Be located inside the United States of America when activating

Activate T-Mobile Service

  • Visit https://www.t-mobile.com/resources/bring-your-own-phone to check your IMEI compatibility and activate T-Mobile service for your PC.
    • Visit https://prepaid.t-mobile.com/bring-your-own-phone to activate T-Mobile Prepaid service for your PC.
  • Once your line is active, follow the Download your eSIM steps below.

Download your eSIM

Use these steps if you’ve contacted T-Mobile to activate your account or need to transfer your service to a different computer.

  • On your computer, choose Start > Settings > Network & Internet.
  • Select Cellular > eSIM profiles > Add a new profile.
  • Get steps for Windows 11 or 10.
  • Choose Let me enter an activation code > Next.
  • Enter the SM-DP+ Address, then choose Next > Close.

Connect to T-Mobile data

  • On your computer, choose Start > Settings > Network & Internet.
  • Select Cellular > eSIM profiles and choose the T-Mobile profile.
  • Select Use and agree to using cellular data for your data plan.
  • When finished, follow steps 1 & 2, but choose Stop using instead.

Change your plan

Use T-Life or myT-Mobile to change your rate plan or manage services..

Delete eSIM

Deleting an eSIM profile does not cancel your T-Mobile account. Contact us for help with that.

  • On your computer, choose Start > Settings > Network & Internet.
  • Select Cellular > eSIM profiles and choose the T-Mobile profile.
  • Select Delete > Yes.

Get Help

Contact us if you have any questions or need help with your T-Mobile connected PC.

T-Mobile DIGITS app and web client

DIGITS is a T-Mobile-branded app available for Android and iOS devices that can also be accessed by computer through a web client. Use the app or web client to manage your DIGITS experience.

On this page:

  • Access DIGITS
  • Log in
  • Add/remove users
  • Use DIGITS
  • Use your numbers
  • Log out of your T-Mobile ID

Access DIGITS

Access is provided free of charge to all T-Mobile postpaid lines.

DIGITS app

The free DIGITS app for Android and iOS allows you to use your DIGITS on multiple Android and iOS devices.

  • Download DIGITS app for iOS or DIGITS app for Android to ensure you have the latest updates!
  • DIGITS app data usage counts toward your Domestic data roaming allotments allotment.
  • After the allotment is used, the app will not work until you return to T-Mobile coverage.
  • The DIGITS app is free to all postpaid customers. The DIGITS app requires:

Android 10/iOS 13 or later and a data connection

2mbps upload & download data speed

Location services enabled and permission granted to the DIGITS app

LineLink users must have a LineLink with DIGITS plan

Business accounts must have fewer than 12 lines

To access multiple lines, the lines must be linked through the DIGITS Portal or via Line Permissions settings in the DIGITS app.

DIGITS web client

The DIGITS web client allows you to use DIGITS on a computer.

  • Access DIGITS via the web using Chrome or EDGE browsers.
  • The DIGITS web client is free to all postpaid customers. The DIGITS web client requires:

Chrome or EDGE web browser

LineLink users must have the LineLink with DIGITS plan

Business accounts must have fewer than 12 lines for the DIGITS

Log in

Android & iOS

Android app: The app will ask for multiple permissions, these can be skipped and the app will open, however, the permissions must be accepted for the app to function correctly. A pop-up will appear for the needed permissions and must be accepted for the app to function.

  • Make sure you are around your T-Mobile phone when you are ready to log in to the DIGITS app.
  • Open the DIGITS app.
  • Login using your T-Mobile ID. If you don’t have a T-Mobile ID, learn how to get one.
    • New T-Mobile IDs cannot sign into DIGITS until 24 hours have passed, or recently changed security questions within 24 hours.
  • Complete 2-factor authentication. To verify your identity, T-Mobile will send a text to your phone number.
    • Or, if you have set up security questions on T-Mobile.com/profile, you can answer security questions rather than receiving a text to your T-Mobile phone.
  • If this is the first time using the app, agree to the Permissions requests.
  • The application will run through several automatic configuration screens.
  • Select to turn the desired DIGITS On, then choose Continue.
Web client
  • Make sure you are around your T-Mobile phone when you are ready to log in on your computer.
  • In a web browser, navigate to https://digits.T-Mobile.com and choose Log In. You can also download a PC or Mac client app to use DIGITS.
  • Sign in with your T-Mobile ID and password. If you don’t have a T-Mobile ID, learn how to get one.
    • New T-Mobile IDs cannot sign into DIGITS until 24 hours have passed, or recently changed security questions within 24 hours.
  • Complete the 2-factor authentication prompts to verify your identity through your preferred method, like a text or email message.
  • If prompted, select Agree and continue to agree to the terms and conditions.
  • Choose which DIGITS you wish to use and confirm your e911 address if prompted, then select Register.
  • If prompted to let DIGITS access your location, select allow. You can’t use DIGITS if you block your location.

Add/remove users

Enable users to access a line
  • In a web browser, visit mydigits.t-mobile.com.
  • Sign in with your T-Mobile ID.
  • On the Assigned tab, select the line you want to grant access to.
  • Choose Add me to this line to provide your T-Mobile ID with access to the line.
  • Choose Share this line with someone else to provide another user access to the line.
    • If the new user is not a T-Mobile customer, you can still grant them access to the line by entering their email.
    • The user will receive an email with steps and a link to create a T-Mobile ID to access that line only.
    • This option is only available for DIGITS Talk & Text lines.
    • Standard voice lines can only be assigned to the Primary Account Holder’s T-Mobile ID or a T-Mobile ID registered with the line on myT-Mobile.com.
Enable users to access a line - DIGITS web client
  • Go to DIGITS.t-mobile.com.
  • Sign in with the Primary Account Holder’s T-Mobile ID.
  • On the Unassigned Lines tab, choose the line that you wish to grant a user access to.
  • Choose Add me to this line to provide your T-Mobile ID with access to the line.
  • Choose Share this line with someone else to provide another user access to the line.
    • If the new user is not a T-Mobile customer, you can still grant them access to the line by entering their email.
    • The user will receive an email with steps and a link to create a T-Mobile ID to access that line only.
    • This option is only available for DIGITS Talk & Text lines.
    • Standard voice lines can only be assigned to the Primary Account Holder’s T-Mobile ID or a T-Mobile ID registered with the line on myT-Mobile.com.
Stop specific users from accessing your DIGITS
  • In a web browser, visit mydigits.t-mobile.com.
  • Sign in with your T-Mobile ID.
  • On the Assigned tab, select the line you want to remove access from.
  • Choose Remove myself next to the user’s email.
  • Choose Manage signed in devices at the top right.
  • Highlight the desired device, then choose Sign Out.
Stop specific users from accessing your DIGITS - DIGITS web client
  • Go to DIGITS.t-mobile.com.
  • Sign in with your T-Mobile ID.
  • Choose the line that you wish to remove user access from.
  • Hover over the email address you wish to remove access for, and select the Remove Line button.
  • If you wish to remove your access for a line on DIGITS, you can select the Remove myself option.
  • You can also select Manage signed in devices to sign out of any devices signed in with your T-Mobile ID.
Stop anyone from accessing your line via DIGITS (including yourself)
  • Log into T-Mobile.com.
  • Select Profile.
  • Select Multiple Devices.
  • Toggle the “Multiple Device status” switch to the OFF setting.
  • To prevent a user from having the ability to turn MDS back on, update their T-Mobile permissions to Restricted Access.

Use DIGITS

Change network settings
  • In the DIGITS app, select Settings and navigate to the Network Settings section:
    • iOS: Select Advanced options > Network settings.
    • Android: Choose the Menu icon with three lines, then select Advanced options > Network settings.
  • If you are on Wi-Fi or another carrier’s network, you must complete another SMS confirmation in order to use your T-Mobile minutes.
    • You can choose to skip this step. This will open your DIGITS app in “Data only mode,” meaning your calls will use your device’s data or Wi-Fi rather than your T-Mobile plan’s minutes.
    • Enter the phone number of the device you are using the app on and select Next. For example, if using a Verizon phone, enter the Verizon phone number.
    • Enter the six-digit code you received via SMS and select Next.
  • Choose from the following:
    • Cellular only: All your calls will use minutes from your primary line and all messages will use data.
    • Cellular fallback: Your primary line will continue to work normally. All other lines will use data over LTE, 4G, or Wi-Fi.
Customize DIGITS
  • In the DIGITS app, select Settings.
    • Android: Choose the menu icon.
    • iOS: Choose the Settings icon in the navigation bar.
  • Choose the desired DIGITS line to view and edit the following settings:
    • Line name
    • e911 address
    • Voicemail greeting
    • Ringtone (must be in Cellular fallback mode)
Do not disturb - DIGITS app

Set up the Do Not Disturb feature to send calls directly to voicemail or avoid notifications for text messages and voicemails.

  • In the DIGITS app, select Settings.
    • Android: Choose the menu icon.
    • iOS: Choose the Settings icon in the navigation bar.
  • Choose the desired DIGITS line.
  • Under Line settings, select Do not disturb.
  • Move the slider to enable do not disturb for the desired line. All notifications will stop.
Do not disturb - DIGITS web client

Set up the Do Not Disturb feature to send calls directly to voicemail or avoid notifications for text messages and voicemails.

  • Choose the Menu icon with three lines
  • Select the slider to enable Do not disturb to send calls directly to voicemail. This also prevents text and voicemail notifications.
  • To disable/enable certain line notifications, select Notifications, then select an option:
    • All notifications: Stop all line notifications
    • Receive notifications
      • Calls: stops new call notifications
      • Voicemails: stops new voicemail notifications
      • Messages: stops new message notifications
    • Alert notifications
      • Calls: stops sound for new call notifications
      • Voicemails: stops sound for new voicemail notification.
      • Messages: stops sound for new message notifications
Turn lines on or off - DIGITS app

If you’re using the DIGITS app on a device with an active SIM/eSIM, you can’t use the app to turn that line on or off. Use the web client instead.

  • In the DIGITS app, select Settings.
    • Android: Choose the menu icon.
    • iOS: Choose the Settings icon in the navigation bar.
  • Choose the desired DIGITS.
  • Choose the switch next to Line State to turn on or off. When a line is enabled/disabled, the primary line will receive a notification of the change.
Turn lines on or off - DIGITS web client
  • Choose the Menu icon with three lines.
  • Select Lines and choose one of the available lines.
  • Select the switch next to Register line to turn it on or off.
Sync your contacts

Syncing new contacts with the DIGITS server is no longer supported. Existing contacts thathave been synced are still accessible in the DIGITS app and Web Client.

Contact linking for Google and Microsoft accounts will be available in the DIGITS app soon.

Follow the steps below to link contacts in the DIGITS Web Client

  • Open the DIGITS Web Client
  • Choose the triple line menu, then select Contacts.
  • Choose Add a Google Account or Add a Microsoft Account
  • Follow the prompts to log-in and link the account.
Use Cellular Fallback - Android steps

To enhance the calling experience, the Cellular Fallback feature allows DIGITS calls to be converted from data to a cellular call to help with missed call concerns (due to delayed/undelivered issues). This is a great option if you get frequent missed calls.

  • If a call is not reaching the DIGITS app, the call is converted and appears in the Phone dialer instead of the DIGITS app.
  • Availability for Android (DIGITS App version 2.7.0 and above).
  • From the device settings, enable ‘Appear on top / Overlay’:
    • From the device settings, select Apps > DIGITS.
    • Choose Appear on top or Overlay, then select the Allow permission toggle to turn on.
  • From the DIGITS app, select Settings > Advanced Options > Network Settings.
  • Choose the Cellular fallback toggle to enable.
  • Enter the phone number associated with the device (not the DIGITS number) in the popup that appears. A SMS message is sent to the customer’s device.
  • Enter the PIN sent to the device in the popup that appears. Cellular fallback will be enabled when the PIN is correctly entered.
Use Cellular Fallback - iOS steps

To enhance the calling experience, the Cellular Fallback feature allows DIGITS calls to be converted from data to a cellular call to help with missed call concerns (due to delayed/undelivered issues). This is a great option if you get frequent missed calls.

  • If a call is not reaching the DIGITS app, the call is converted and appears in the Phone dialer instead of the DIGITS app.
  • Availability for iOS (DIGITS App version 2.7.2 and above).
  • From the DIGITS app, select the Settings icon.
  • Choose Advanced Options, then select Network Settings.
  • Choose the Cellular fallback option to enable.
  • Optional steps – you’ll be asked to enter phone number only when DIGITS app fails to read native device line number:
    • Enter the phone number associated with the device (not the DIGITS number) in the popup. A text message is sent to your device.
    • Enter the PIN sent to the device in the popup that appears. Cellular fallback will be enabled when the PIN is correctly entered.

Use your numbers

When you use DIGITS, text and picture messages that you send from your device don’t show up in the conversation thread in the DIGITS app or the DIGITS website.

  • iOS: Messages sent via iMessage will not sync in the DIGITS app. If you want to get the full conversation of sent and received messages in all instances of DIGITS, use the downloadable DIGITS app on your primary phone to send your outgoing messages.
  • Android: When you get a call from a verified number, you’ll get a “Number Verified” pop-up screen.
Place a call - DIGITS app
  • In the DIGITS app, select the Dial Pad.
  • Select which number you want to place a call from in the drop-down at the top of the screen.
  • Dial the number and select Call.
  • If in Cellular only mode: A popup appears with a random 413 number to dial. Press Call to continue the call and you will be connected to the original number you dialed. To stop this pop-up, switch the Network Settings to Cellular Fallback.
  • (Android only) To display caller ID in “Cellular only” mode, choose Settings > Apps > DIGITS > “Advanced” tab, and then select Appear on top: Allow permission.
Place a call - DIGITS web client
  • In the DIGITS web client, select Calls.
  • Select NEW CALL.
  • Enter the contact name or number. Alternatively, select the number pad icon at the bottom to manually dial the number.
  • In the From: field, choose the DIGITS you want to make the call with.
  • Choose the magenta Call button.
Conference call
  • Initiate a new call to the first contact.
  • Select Add to Call in the middle, the first call will automatically be placed on hold
  • Enter the desired contact name or phone number, then select the magenta Call button.
  • Once the call is connected, select Merge Call.
Using your contacts - DIGITS app
  • In the DIGITS app, select Contacts..
  • Use the search bar or the alphabet navigation to search your contacts.
  • Select which contact you want to call. This will pull up that contact’s details.
  • Select which number you would like to call.
  • If you are using multiple lines, select which line you would like to place the call from.
Using your contacts - DIGITS web client
  • In the DIGITS Web client, select Contacts in the upper middle of the page.
  • Select All contacts or the specific contact list you wish to view in the drop-down.
  • Use the search bar or scroll down to the desired contact.
  • Select the contact you want to call or message to pull up the contact details.
  • Select the number to call or message.
  • If using multiple lines, select the line to place the call or message from.
Send a message - Android steps
  • In the DIGITS app, select Messaging.
  • Use the drop-down at the top of the screen if you want to only view messages for one of your lines.
  • Choose the New Message circle.
  • If you are using multiple lines: Use the top drop-down menu to select which line you want to use.
  • Use the keypad to enter a recipient or multiple recipients. You can use numbers or letters.
  • Choose Next.
  • Start typing your message.
  • Attach any media files using the paper clip icon.
  • Choose the arrow to send.
Send a message - iOS steps
  • In the DIGITS app, select Messaging.
  • Use the drop-down at the top of the screen if you want to only view messages for one of your lines.
  • Choose the New Message icon.
  • If you are using multiple lines: Use the top drop-down menu to select which line you want to use.
  • Choose the To: line.
  • Use the keypad to enter a recipient or multiple recipients. You can use numbers or letters.
  • Choose Done on your keypad.
  • Start typing your message.
  • Attach media files using the photo or paper clip icons.
  • Choose the arrow to send.
Send a message - Web client
  • Select Messages in the upper-middle of the web page.
  • Select New Message.
  • Enter the desired contact name or phone number in the To field.
  • In the From line, choose the DIGITS line you want to send the message from.
  • Type your message in the Enter Message field. Add extras if necessary:
    • Select the paper clip icon to add a picture
    • Add an emoji using the face icon.
    • Add an audio message using the microphone icon.
    • Choose Send (paper airplane).
Check voicemail - DIGITS app

  • From the DIGITS app, select Calls on the navigation bar.

  • Choose Voicemail.

  • Choose the voicemail message you would like to listen to.

  • To delete a voicemail, swipe the voicemail.

  • To view voicemail only for a specific DIGITS line, use the drop-down menu at the top of the screen. Change voicemail greeting (Android only)

  • Choose the Menu icon with three lines.

  • Select the desired DIGITS line and choose Voicemail greeting.

  • Choose Personal greeting to set up your custom voicemail greeting.

Check voicemail - Web client
  • From the DIGITS web client, select the Voicemail tab in the upper middle of the screen.
  • Choose the desired voicemail.
  • Once selected, download the voicemail, delete, call, or message the number by selecting the icon with three circles.
  • Alternatively, select on the picture icon to delete a voicemail, then select the trash can icon at the top.
Transfer a call

During a call, choose Transfer Call > Switch device. The device you’re switching to must have the line you’re calling from turned on.

Log out of your T-Mobile ID

Android & iOS
  • Choose Settings.
    • Android: Choose the menu icon.
    • iOS: Choose the Settings icon in the navigation bar.
  • Choose Sign out.
  • Choose Sign out again to confirm.
Web client
  • Select the Settings gear.
  • Choose Sign out.
Experience feedback - DIGITS App
  • Choose Settings.
    • Android: Choose the menu icon.
    • iOS: Choose the Settings icon in the navigation bar.
  • Choose Help.
  • Choose Feedback.
Experience feedback - DIGITS web client
  • Select Got Feedback?
  • Fill out the requested information, then choose Submit.

T-Mobile FamilyWhere app

With T-Mobile FamilyWhere, a T-Mobile primary account holder can use the FamilyWhere Android app or T-Mobile.com to locate any phone on their plan that is on the T-Mobile network. Find out more about our Family and Parental Controls.

On this page:

  • Signing up
  • Add a Family Member
  • Locate and check-in
  • Android 10 location accuracy improvement: setting change
  • Canceling your subscription

Signing up

What you need to use it
  • An active T-Mobile account. FamilyWhere doesn’t track devices on suspended accounts.
  • A Primary Account Holder assigned on the account. Only the Primary Account Holder can activate FamilyWhere service and review located devices.
  • A T-Mobile data plan.
  • By design, FamilyWhere notifications can’t be disabled on a child’s phone. These notifications are required by FCC regulations and by T-Mobile Privacy and Safety policy.
  • The FamilyWhere app is available for Android only. For other devices, log in to your T-Mobile account​ and select My Account > Profile > Family Controls > FamilyWhere.
Sign up on T-Mobile.com
  • Log in to My T-Mobile.
  • Choose your name at the top right.
  • Select Profile > Permissions & controls.
  • Choose Parental and family controls > Family Where.
  • Select Get Started.
  • Enter the Basic Information.
  • Review and agree to the Terms of Service.
  • Select and name phones to locate.
  • Choose Done.

Add a Family Member

Add a Family Member via Android
  • Open the FamilyWhere app.
  • Access the app menu by selecting the Menu icon.
  • Select My Settings > My Family.
  • Select Add Family Member.
  • Allow FamilyWhere to access contacts.
  • Select the phone number linked to the Family Member.
  • Enter name, then select OK. The My Settings selection from the main menu offers a My Family option that allows adding a Family Member, but this option is only valid if there are phone numbers that can be added to the Family. If none are available, the app will highlight that.
Add a Family Member via T-Mobile.com
  • Log in to your T-Mobile account.
  • Choose your name.
  • Select Profile > Family Controls > FamilyWhere > Settings.
  • Select Add Family Member.
  • Select the phone number linked to the Family Member.
  • Enter a name and choose a photo, then select Add Family Member. The Add Family Member option is only listed if there is one or more phone numbers available to be added as Family Members. If none are available, the option will not be shown.

Locate and check-in

Locate a family member
  • Log in to your T-Mobile account.
  • Select My account.
  • Select Profile.
  • Select Family Controls.
  • Select FamilyWhere.
  • Select a name or mobile number to locate.
Locate a line after initial sign-in

The app automatically locates all lines on the list of locatable devices upon signing in. To locate a line after initial sign-in, choose the name of the device at the top of the screen. FamilyWhere will not work if all shortcodes are blocked on your account.

  • You can track up to a total of 10 lines on an account.
  • Only the approximate location (the nearest cell tower) of iOS (Apple) devices on your account will display in FamilyWhere.
  • Tablets are trackable to a location as long as they are associated with a T-Mobile number and have GPS enabled. However, T-Mobile can’t guarantee location accuracy on these devices.
  • All lines on the locatable devices list receive a text message when they become locatable and about once a month another text is sent.
Access check-in details
  • Open the check-in message that you received.
  • Choose the URL included in the text.
Send a check-in message
  • Launch the FamilyWhere Android app and select Check In.
  • Enter the recipient and message content.
  • Select Send.
Create Landmark via Android
  • Open the FamilyWhere app.
  • Use the map to designate the location for the landmark. Select and hold the location for two seconds.
  • Select Add a place.
  • Enter landmark name, then select OK. The Landmarks option from the main menu offers a Create Landmark option that allows creating a landmark by entering an address, but this option currently rejects many residential addresses. A landmark must be created if the ‘You must enter a valid address. Double-check the address and try again.’ error message is received.
Create Landmark via T-Mobile.com
  • Log in to your T-Mobile account.
  • Choose your name.
  • Select Profile > Family Controls > FamilyWhere > Create a Landmark.
  • Enter landmark address and name.
  • Select Save and create.

Android 10 Location Accuracy Improvement: Setting Change

Location precision when locating newer Android devices can be improved by changing a device setting from the default. The setting must be changed on the located device, not the device you are locating from.

Change settings

The path to change the setting varies by device manufacturer:

  • Samsung: Go to Settings > search for Service > select Service Provider Location > set to Allow All The Time
  • Google: Go to Settings > Location > App Permissions > … > Show System > Carrier Location > set to Allow All The Time
  • OnePlus: Go to Settings > search for Carrier > select Carrier Location Access > set to Always Allow
  • Motorola: Go to Settings > Location > select Carrier Location Attribution > turn On
  • LG: Go to Settings > search for Carrier > select Carrier Location Permission > select Permission Setting > set to Allow All The Time
Devices that require setting change:
  • Samsung Galaxy A71 5G
  • Samsung Galaxy Note 10 5G
  • Samsung Galaxy S10 Lite
  • Samsung Galaxy S20 5G
  • Samsung Galaxy S20 Ultra 5G
  • Samsung Galaxy S20+ 5G
  • Samsung Z Flip 5G
  • Google Pixel 4
  • Google Pixel 4 XL
  • OnePlus 7T
  • OnePlus 7T Pro 5G
  • OnePlus 8
  • Motorola G Fast
  • Moto E
  • Moto G8 Power
  • Moto G8 Stylus
  • LG Aristo 5
  • LG Stylo 6
  • LG V60 ThinQ

T-Mobile Prepaid eSIM app

The T-Mobile Prepaid eSIM app lets you activate new T-Mobile prepaid service on an iPhone or Android with eSIM. For other devices, check the compatibility to bring your device to T-Mobile Prepaid.

Looking for Prepaid plans and devices? Visit the T-Mobile Prepaid website.

On this page:

  • About the app
  • Activate T-Mobile service
  • Re-download eSIM
  • Errors and support
  • Full terms

About the app

The Prepaid eSIM app was built for travelers coming to the U.S., existing T-Mobile customers who want a secondary pre-paid line, and anyone who wants to take the Un-carrier out for a test drive to try out America’s fastest 5G network.*

  • The app can only activate a T-Mobile prepaid line.
  • For postpaid accounts, check out T-Mobile eSIM.
  • Only available for iPhone or Android devices with eSIM.
  • The app requires:
    • You have a data connection, through either Wi-Fi or Cellular.
    • You either purchased the device from T-Mobile, or else you must first SIM unlock it. (Contact the original provider if you need help.)
  • There are no fees to activate a device with an eSIM.
  • You must be located in the US when activating service.
  • To activate your eSIM on another wireless provider or manage eSIM settings, check out our Tutorials.

Activate T-Mobile service

  • Download the T-Mobile Prepaid eSIM app:
    • Apple App Store
    • Google Play Store
  • Open the app and choose what type of plans to explore:
    • See travel plans shows limited duration plans designed for travelers
    • Explore other plans shows plans other than travel
  • Enter the following information, then choose Next:
    • Email addresss
    • 6-15 digit PIN
    • Your U.S. ZIP code
  • If prompted, allow the app access to your location while you’re using the app.
  • Review your order to make sure everything looks correct.
  • Enter your Credit Card informaiton, including CVV and billing ZIP code, then select Place order.
  • Wait while we set up your T-Mobile service.
  • Follow the prompts on your device to complete your eSIM download, including giving it a name and choosing a primary line.
  • If you want to use a phone number from another provider or from another line, contact us to get this started.

Re-download eSIM

Sometimes, you may need to replace the eSIM you received through the app.

  • You accidentally deleted your eSIM.

  • You upgraded your phone and want to transfer your eSIM line of service to your new phone.

  • You lost connection when downloading your eSIM, and it didn’t get installed properly on your device. If you’re switching from one iPhone to another, you can transfer your phone number during Quick Start or through device settings. Otherwise, you’ll need to call us at 1-877-778-2106. Make sure you have:

  • Your Prepaid eSIM phone number or your OrderID. Your OrderID will display if you encounter an error in the app.

  • Your account PIN code, which you set up to complete your order in the T-Mobile Prepaid eSIM App.

Errors and support

Here are some error messages you may receive using the app and tips to solve them.

Something went wrong – Check your internet connection
  • This means the app lost its connection to the internet when trying to set up service.
  • Make sure you have good Wi-Fi or Cellular signal, then try again.
  • If possible, try again using a different Wi-Fi network.
Looks like your device isn’t compatible
  • This means your device doesn’t have an eSIM or is locked to the service provider you purchased it from.
  • If you have an iPhone, make sure it’s the Apple iPhone Xs or newer.
  • If you have a Samsung, make sure it supports eSIM.
  • Contact the service provider who sold you the device to request an unlock.
This email address is already in use. Try a different email
  • This means the email address you’re trying to use is already set up with an existing T-Mobile account.
  • Try again with a different email address to create a new account.
Error 504: Oops, something went wrong
  • This means that the app had an issue loading the next screen.
  • Make sure you have a strong Wi-Fi or Cellular data connection, then try again.
  • If it’s still not working, contact us for help.
Error 505: There was an issue completing your order
  • This means there was an issue processing your payment.
  • You can try again with a different payment method.
  • If you’re currently outside of the United States, try again when you arrive.
  • If it’s still not working, contact us for help.

T-Mobile Video Calling

T-Mobile Video Calling is a feature that’s built-in as part of the dialer on some T-Mobile phones, giving you easy access to high-quality video calling.

Go to:

  • What is T-Mobile Video Calling
  • How it works

What is T-Mobile Video Calling

T-Mobile Video Calling provides a streamlined way to communicate with family and friends through high-quality video calling. There’s no extra charge to use it, but it does use your high-speed data.

If you’re looking for information about third-party video calling apps like Skype or Google Duo, we have some helpful links here. Skype or Google Duo calls cannot be answered with the T-Mobile Video Calling feature.

Since it’s built into your phone’s dialer, there’s no need to download additional apps or sign into a separate account. T-Mobile Video Calling uses Video over LTE (also known as VoLTE) to let you make and receive high-quality video calls. You can make video calls over LTE or Wi-Fi.

How it works

For it to work properly and to receive all the benefits of the service, all phones participating in a video conversation must support T-Mobile Video Calling. The software needed for it to work on your phone is available either out-of-the-box when you purchase your phone or through a software update of your current phone.

When you use Video Calling, make sure that:
  • Both participants are using a T-Mobile Video Calling phone (limited to two participants). If one of the phones moves out of range of the required network, the video will be lost and the call reverts to voice only.
  • If you need help with some of these steps on your phone, visit our Device tutorials select your phone, or use the search bar and enter your phone name.
    • If any participant is connecting by LTE, VoLTE must be enabled.
    • If any participant is connecting through Wi-Fi, then Wi-Fi calling must be enabled.
    • A software upgrade may be required to enable T-Mobile Video Calling on your phone. Not all phone have the software or hardware required for video calling.
  • Video Calling only works with domestic T-Mobile numbers; it doesn’t work with international numbers. However, it will work for T-Mobile customers on Wi-Fi in another country. This feature uses high-speed data. Because of the bandwidth needed to make a video call, once you exceed your high-speed data limit, you won’t be able to use T-Mobile Video Calling again until your next billing cycle. If you want, you can always change your service to add more high-speed data. Or, you can switch to Magenta. Or, connect over Wi-Fi and you won’t use any of your data.

T-Mobile Visual Voicemail app

T-Mobile Visual Voicemail app (VVM) for Android allows you to listen to and view messages in any order, on your phone. VVM is available on other phone models.

On this page:

  • Read me first
  • Settings menu
  • Save and delete messages
  • Voicemail to text

Read me first

  • This app is only for Android devices, Apple iOS devices use a built-in voicemail app. For help with the iPhone app, review Check your voicemail on iPhone - Apple Support.
  • If you need help with voicemail, check out Voicemail troubleshooting.
  • For Voicemail, to listen and download messages by phone call, check out Voicemail
  • Voicemail messages will automatically be deleted after a specific amount of time and cannot be retrieved. Learn more about save and delete messages.
  • If you need help with these steps on your device, visit our Device tutorials select your device, or use the search bar and enter your device name.

Settings menu

Call settings
  • Select Visual Voicemail.
  • Choose the message you want to listen to.
    • Call voicemail
      • Select the Menu button (three vertical dots).
      • Choose Call Voicemail.
    • Return a call
      • Select the Call button.
      • Wait for the call to initiate.
    • Speaker
      • Select the Speaker button.
      • Select the Play button.
Contacts
  • Launch the Visual Voicemail app.
  • Select the picture icon by the phone number you wish to add as a contact.
    • Add new: Select Create Contact.
    • Edit: Once you select the icon, the option to edit the contact appears.
  • Follow procedures by device to create a new contact.
Greeting
  • Select Visual Voicemail.
  • Select the Menu button (three vertical dots).
  • Select Settings.
  • In the ‘Greetings & Pin’ section, select the currently active greeting in the first section. This may be labeled as Default, Greeting 1, or any other name you previously selected.
    • Record a greeting
      • Select the microphone icon in the upper right and corner of the screen.
      • Name your greeting.
      • Select the Record button once to begin recording, and again to stop recording.
      • Select Save.
    • Set active greeting
      • Choose the name of the greeting you wish to set as active.
      • Select Set as Active.
    • Delete a greeting
      • Choose the name of the greeting you wish to delete, e.g., ‘Old Greeting’.
      • Select Delete.
      • Select OK.
Notifications

Some of these steps work only on Android 8 and up.

  • In the phone’s Settings, select Apps or Apps & Notifications.
  • Sort the apps listed until Visual Voicemail shows and select the app.
  • Under ‘App settings’, select Notifications.
  • Move the slider to ON / OFF, or select each notification category to modify the notification.
Additional settings
  • Select Visual Voicemail.
  • Select the Menu button (three vertical dots).
    • Change pin
      • Select Settings.
      • Choose Change PIN.
      • Enter the current PIN in the ‘greetings in PIN’ section. Dial #793# to reset the password.
      • Enter and confirm the new PIN.
      • Select OK. A confirmation message appears if the change was successful.
    • Change the sort options
      • Choose one of the following options:
        • Sort alphabetically
        • Sort by unviewed
    • Delete multiple messages
      • Select the Trash Can icon at the top.
      • Select all messages to delete.
      • Select Delete.
    • Manually set the language
      • Select Settings.
      • Go to the language section and select the active language.
      • Select the desired language.
    • Sync the inbox
      • Select the Menu button.
      • Select Refresh.

Save and delete messages

Visual Voicemail messages stay on your phone until you delete them. You can also download messages to your phone, forward to email, or save to an SD card.

Save

After you’ve listened to your voicemail message, it’s automatically saved to the VVM app.

Save a voicemail to the SD card

  • Select Visual Voicemail.

  • Select and hold a message, then select Save message to.

  • Enter the file name.

  • Select Save to copy the message to the memory card. Send a voicemail by email

  • Select Visual Voicemail, then the message you want to send to email.

  • Select and hold the desired message.

  • Select Forward to.

  • Select the preferred email client.

  • Complete the email. Check out Voicemail for another way to save messages.

Delete

If you’ve listened to your voicemail and deleted it, it can’t be retrieved! There is no way to retrieve the deleted voicemail message once it’s been moved to the trash. When Visual Voicemail messages are deleted on the phone, the voicemail system will delete the message when the voicemail system syncs with the phone. Syncing happens when new messages are received or when you synchronize Visual Voicemail using the Menu in the Visual Voicemail Inbox.

Migration

How to use Music Freedom

Music Freedom is enabled automatically if you’ve got an eligible plan - there’s nothing you need to do! However, we’ve got a few tips on how to avoid using data:

  • Use the specific music streaming app on your device.
  • Don’t stream to devices using Mobile Hotspot or tethering.

Non-music streaming data

  • Non-music data does count against your high-speed data bucket. The amount of data varies by streaming partner and the device being used.

Roaming experience

  • International availability of streaming services does vary, so make sure to check with your streaming service provider before you go.

Voicemail

T-Mobile provides multiple options for voicemail: Voicemail, Visual Voicemail (VVM), and Voicemail to Text (VTT). Former UScellular customers can use these voicemail steps to access their messages and greetings.

On this page:

  • Read me first
  • Set up your voicemail
  • Reset your voicemail PIN
  • Settings menu
  • Save and delete messages
  • UScellular customers

Read me first

You must set up your voicemail from the device associated with the voicemail on your plan or through the Visual Voicemail app.

If you need help with voicemail or Visual Voicemail, check out the Voicemail troubleshooting page.

To get messages in any order on your phone, check out T-Mobile Visual Voicemail app (Android) or Check your voicemail on iPhone. *

Voicemail messages are automatically deleted after a specific amount of time and cannot be retrieved. Learn more about how to save and delete messages.

If you need help with these steps on your device, visit our Device tutorials page and select your device, or use the search bar and enter your device name.

T-Mobile Voicemail features, including Voicemail to Text (VTT), may not be compatible with Live Voicemail on iPhones. For iOS duplicate VVT notifications, update your service to add on the $0 VVT block feature online through your T-Mobile account or contact us for assistance.

Set up your voicemail

  • Press and hold the 1 key on the device associated with the voicemail on your plan, or open the Visual Voicemail app to connect to your voicemail.
  • Enter a PIN during first-time setup. Use your default PIN, or hang up and dial #793# to reset your PIN.
  • Receive an SMS with a temporary PIN after dialing #793#, then enter the temporary PIN using your keypad.
  • Create a new PIN when prompted after entering the temporary PIN. PINs must be 4 to 7 digits, should be easy for you to remember, and difficult for others to guess.
  • Record your greeting and name when prompted to complete setup. Your voicemail is ready to use once recording is complete.

Reset your voicemail PIN

Use these steps if you forget your voicemail PIN or need to reset it.

  • Dial #793# on your phone.
  • Receive an SMS with a temporary PIN after dialing #793#, then enter the temporary PIN using your keypad.
  • Create a new PIN when prompted. Choose a 4 to 7 digit number that is easy for you to remember and difficult for others to guess.

Settings menu

  • To access your voicemail setting menu, long press the 1 key or open the voicemail app.
  • If this doesn’t work, dial 1-805-637-7249, enter your 10-digit number and while the voicemail greeting is playing, select * (star key) and enter the password.
  • If you’re traveling internationally, read our International roaming checklist to learn how to check your messages.
  • Once you’re connected, select the keypad number assigned to the setting menu step for more options.
1 - Listen to messages

  • 5 - Date/Time info

Save and delete messages

Voicemails are deleted if the auto-save period is reached. The auto-save period can be from 14 to 30-days, depending on the type of voicemail. If you hear “You have (# of vm) voicemail message(s) which is due to automatic deletion…” check out the steps on this page to save the messages.

Save

After you’ve listened to your voicemail message, select the 9 key to save the message. You can repeat this to save the message in your voicemail box before the auto-save period runs out.

Delete
  • If you’re listening to your voicemail and delete it, don’t hang up! A voicemail message can be retrieved before the same call is disconnected.
  • Once the call has ended there is no way to retrieve the deleted voicemail message.

UScellular customers

As part of UScellular’s move to T-Mobile, your voicemail and messages are moving to T-Mobile’s systems to provide easier access on the T-Mobile network. Once your account is moved to the T-Mobile network, you’ll receive a new voicemail box. You can create a new PIN and greeting the first time you call your voicemail.

Accessing your voicemail messages and PIN
  • Your old UScellular voicemails will be moved to your new T-Mobile voicemail box automatically within 72 hours .
    • Option 8 will no longer be available in the main menu after your voicemails move to your new T-Mobile voicemail box.
    • If you need to access your previous messages prior to 72 hours, you need to use your original UScellular voicemail box PIN which will be different on T-Mobile once the move is complete.
  • If you forgot your voicemail PIN or if you need a new one on T-Mobile, review the Set up your voicemail or Reset your voicemail PIN details above. This process will be available once the move is complete (up to 72 hours).
  • If you are on the T-Mobile network, but your old UScellular voicemails have not been moved to the T-Mobile voicemail box, restart your phone and then access your messages by completing one of the following:
    • Long press 1 to call your voicemail.
    • Press option 8 in the main menu.
    • You may be prompted to enter a voicemail PIN - This is your previous UScellular voicemail PIN.
  • Once you are on the T-Mobile’s network, and your old UScellular voicemails have been moved to the new T-Mobile voicemail box, restart your phone and then access your messages by completing one of the following:
    • Long press 1
    • Dial your own phone number
    • Dial 123 to access your voicemail.
    • Dialing *86 will no longer work with your new voicemail box.
  • If you are still on the UScellular network, you can listen to your messages by completing one of the following:
    • Call your voicemail by dialing your phone number
    • Dial *86
    • Long press the 1 key.
Your voicemail greeting
  • If you are on the T-Mobile network and you set up your new T-Mobile voicemail greeting, the T-Mobile greeting will be the new active greeting.
  • If you are on the T-Mobile network and you do not set up a new T-Mobile voicemail greeting, your previous UScellular greeting will be your active greeting (You can choose to keep it or record a new one).
Visual Voicemail on iPhones
  • Once you are on the T-Mobile network, restart your phone, and you will see a Set Up option that you can tap to create a PIN and greeting.
  • If the Visual Voicemail setup is not done, no new deposited voicemails will display on the app until the setup is complete.
  • All your previously saved voicemail messages on your iPhone will stay on your iPhone.

Web Guard device content filter

Web Guard is a free service for T-Mobile customers that you can use to help restrict adult content from being seen or accessed by family members under 18 years old.

On this page:

  • Web Guard
  • Safe Search
  • Add or manage Web Guard

Web Guard

  • Web Guard prevents access to adult web content only when your device is connected to T-Mobile’s cellular network with Web Guard enabled.
    • If there is an Access Denied error when trying to open certain web pages, Web Guard might be active on your line.
    • Web Guard is not available on all devices and might not work at certain times or in certain locations.
    • Web Guard isn’t foolproof and shouldn’t be a substitute for taking steps to monitor access to content.
  • T-Mobile customers with Web Guard enabled are not be able to use iCloud Private Relay and will receive a device notification that their current rate plan does not support iCloud Private Relay. Web Guard can be turned off to use Private Relay instead.
  • Content filtering may not be compatible with certain products or services, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs). Apple Private Relay must be toggled off for T-Mobile content filtering to work.
Web Guard Filters

Web Guard has multiple filters (High, Medium, and Low) that uou can set for restricting content. For eample:

  • Low Filter
    • Phishing Attacks, Malware, Command and Control Callbacks, Web Spam, Proxy / Anonymizer, Potentially Harmful Domains
    • Adult themes, Nudity, Sexuality, Pornography, Tasteless, Child Abuse Content
    • Hacking, Hate/Discrimination, Illegal Downloads, Weapons, Drugs
  • MediumFilter
    • Everything listed above for low filters.
    • Safe Search enabled to automatically filter pornography and other offensive content that’s built into search engines
  • High Filter
    • Everything listed above for low and medium filters.
    • Adware, Visual Search Engines, Classifieds, Blog, Games, Lingerie/Bikini,
    • Information on Alcohol, Gambling, Illegal Activities, Terrorism, and Dating
    • Chat, Instant Messaging, Forums/Message Boards, Social Networking, Video Sharing, Photo Sharing, Webmail, and File Storage, P2P / File Transfer
Web Guard Exceptions

Web Guard is unable to block the following content types:

  • Browsing over Wi-Fi
  • Email, text messages, instant messaging
  • Some third-party web browsers
  • Content in device apps

Safe Search

Safe Search is an automated filter of offensive content that may result from internet search results.

  • High and Medium Web Guard levels enable Safe Search automatically.
  • Results will be filtered from most common search engines such as Google, YouTube, Bing, and DuckDuckGo.
  • When Safe Search is enabled, you may receive one of the following messages when search results include explicit content:
  • “You don’t have permission to turn SafeSearch off. It’s locked by the device or network you are browsing on.”
  • “Some results have been removed because Restricted Mode is enabled by your network administrator.”

Add or manage Web Guard

The Primary Account Holder (PAH) and any user with Full Permission can manage or remove Web Guard using their T-Mobile account, T-Life, or by calling Customer Care. Check out Set online permissions for more information about PAH and other roles,

T-Mobile or T Life app
  • Access the T-Mobile or T Life app on your device.
  • Select Manage, then choose a line.
  • Choose All Account Settings > Family controls.
  • If you have multiple lines on your account, select the line you want to make changes to.
  • Select Web Guard, then select High, Medium, Low, or No Filtering (this means Web Guard is off).
  • Choose View more information on blocked categories to see what each filter does.
  • Select Save changes.
T-Mobile.com
  • Log into your MyT-Mobile account.
  • Click your Profile name in top right corner and then select Profile.
  • Select the line you want to make changes to if you have multiple lines on your account.
  • Scroll down and select Family Controls.
  • Select Web Guard.
  • Slect High, Medium, Low, or No Filtering (this means Web Guard is off).
  • Select View more Info to see what each filter does.
  • Click Save changes.

Wireless Emergency Alerts

Learn more about Wireless Emergency Alerts (WEA) on the T-Mobile network.

On this page:

  • About Wireless Emergency Alerts
  • Types of alerts
  • Turn off alerts
  • Get help

About Wireless Emergency Alerts

Wireless Emergency Alerts (WEA) is a public safety notification system that enables authorized agencies to send text-like messages to consumers with capable wireless devices to alert them of emergencies in their area. Alerts are geographically targeted, so only those in the threat area will receive the alert.

For more information, read about WEA on the FCC website and T-Mobile’s information and list of capable devices on www.t-mobile.com/wea.

Types of alerts

There are four types of messages:

  • National Alerts
  • Imminent Threats to Life and Property Alerts
  • AMBER Alerts
  • Public Safety Messages Authorized state and/or local government agencies may send test alerts to mirror actual alert conditions. These agencies are expected to include conspicuous language that make it clear that these messages are only tests and do not reflect actual emergencies. State and Local Test Alerts are disabled by default on all WEA-capable devices.

Turn off alerts

  • Select your device for the steps.
  • Check your user manual for additional questions about turning off or receiving Emergency Alerts on your device.
  • Find support for your T-Mobile device with our Tutorials.
  • You can’t disable National alerts, which are issued by the authority of the President of the United States or FEMA Administrator.
Android

Settings can usually be found in the following two locations:

  • Search your Settings app for Emergency or Wireless Alerts.
  • In the messaging app, select the Menu icon with three dots, then select Settings > Emergency Alerts.
Apple
  • Select Settings > Notifications to adjust alert settings.
  • Dial 500525371# to turn on WEA test messages and 500525370# to turn them off.

Get help

If you need to report an emergency, call 911.

If you received an emergency alert and have additional questions, contact your local public safety agencies as soon as possible. You can also visit the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) website or the FEMA website to try and locate an alternate point of contact. Authorized government agencies (such as state and local emergency management organizations and public safety agencies) determine the content of the WEA messages broadcast by T-Mobile, and T-Mobile is unlikely to have additional information about particular alerts.

5G Signal Spot

Set up

&amp;nbsp;

Video not loading? Please reload this page and try again.

  • Plug the included Cat5e/Cat6 cable into the WAN port on the 5G Signal Spot and connect the other end to your broadband router or switch. Your connection must support Gigabit speeds, a minimum of 200 Mbps dedicated per unit is required (1 Gbps recommended).
  • Connect the RGPS antenna to the RGPS port and place it near a window or any location with a clear, unobstructed view of the sky.
  • Power the device using either the included 12V/10A AC adapter (plug into the AC port) or a PoE++ source (IEEE 802.3bt Type 4). Only one power source is needed.
  • The device automatically begins provisioning and establishes a secure IPSec tunnel to the T-Mobile 5G Core. Allow 20–30 minutes for initial setup and network registration. All four LEDs will turn solid blue when the device is ready. Backhaul and port requirements

Reduced broadband connections will result in reduced unit performance.

  • A minimum broadband connection of 200 Mbps is required dedicated to each unit. 1 Gbps dedicated to each unit is recommended for most installations.
  • Router must allow outbound traffic on ports.
  • When possible, UPnP should be enabled on the router.
  • A secure IPSec tunnel is established to the T-Mobile 5G Core for service connectivity. Firewall Port requirements

Update the address of use (E911)

The 5G Signal Spot has to be registered to the location where it’s installed for E911 compliance. Update the address before moving to a new location so that service remains uninterrupted.

  • Log in to T-Platform and update the address.
  • Once updated, power on or power cycle the device (unplug for a full minute and reconnect).
  • Allow 15–20 minutes for address updates to propagate and re-register with the network.

LED indicators and ports

LED indicators

The front of the device has four LEDs displaying the status of the device. When all 4 are solid blue, the Signal Spot is working and broadcasting 5G. Red or blinking LEDs indicate an issue that needs attention.

Troubleshooting

Set up
  • No LEDs are illuminated: Check power source (AC adapter or PoE++) and try a known working outlet or switch port.
  • Sync LED remains red for more than 20 minutes: Reposition the GPS antenna to a better location.
  • 5G LED is red or blinking for more than 30 minutes: Confirm Ethernet connection and verify required ports are open.
  • All LEDs are blue, but performance is low: Verify available ISP bandwidth and reduce local network load.
  • All LEDs are blinking red or issues persist: Contact us.
