  • AutoPay
  • Payment arrangements

Make a payment

Limits on payment amounts
  • The maximum amount for a one-time payment using a debit or credit card is $25,000.
  • The maximum amount of a one-time ECP (Electronic Check Processing) transaction is $9,999.99.
  • You can make multiple payments within a 24—hour period using the same payment method as long as each payment differs by at least $0.01.
Make a payment
  • Log in to Account Hub to go to Billing. If you have multiple accounts, select the desired one.
  • Select Make payment to enter the Payment Amount and Payment Date.
  • Choose your payment method (bank transfer or credit/debit card) or select Pay in installments to set up a payment arrangement.
  • Select Submit to complete the payment process.
Equipment Installment Payments (EIP)
  • Log in to Account Hub to select Billing and choose the desired account.
  • Select Equipment Installment Plans and select the device or line for which you want to make a payment.
  • Select Make Extra Payment and enter the payment details, including amount, date, and payment information (bank transfer or credit/debit card).
  • Enter the billing address and click on Submit.
  • A payment receipt, updated EIP loan information will be displayed, and an email confirmation will be sent to the address on file. You can also view EIP information, such as down payments made, loan balance, loan ID, and the number of payments remaining.
Bill pay from your bank

Once set up is authorized by you, all scheduled payments will be handled by your bank. If payment issues arise, T-Mobile does not have access to view or modify your scheduled bank payments.

  • Contact your bank or log in to your bank account online to set up or change bill pay.
  • Add T-Mobile as a provider through your bank if setting up bill pay for the first time.
  • Provide your bank with the following payee details:
    • T-Mobile account number, which can be found on the Account tab in the T-Mobile app, in your account online, or on your paper bill.
    • Payee name: T-Mobile
    • Payment address: T-Mobile, P.O. Box 742596, Cincinnati, OH 45274-2596

Payment history

  • Log in to Account Hub and go to Billing. If you have multiple accounts, select the desired account.
  • Go to the Payments tab. Recent payments are displayed or enter payment number to search.

AutoPay

  • Log in to Account Hub and go to the Billing section. If you have multiple accounts, select the desired one.
  • Go to the Settings tab and select AutoPay.
  • Select one of the options: Enroll Now, Edit, or Turn Off Auto Pay.
  • Enter payment type details (credit card or direct deposit from bank) then select Save changes.

Payment arrangements

Set up a payment arrangement
  • Log in to Account Hub.
  • Go to Billing. If you have multiple accounts, select the desired account.
  • Go to the Settings tab.
  • Select the Make Payment button.
  • Select the Pay in installments radio button under Payment amount.
  • Enter first payment installment amount. Must be at least 20% of balance due.
  • Select first payment installment date.
  • Enter second payment installment amount. Must be for remaining balance due. Over-payment not permitted.
  • Select second payment installment date.
  • Enter credit/debit/banking details, billing address, and installment plan notification preferences.
  • Enter the phone number for validation and to receive a text confirmation notification.
  • Select Submit. A confirmation screen with a summary of the payment arrangements will appear.
Edit a payment arrangement (payment method changes only)
  • Log in to Account Hub.
  • Go to Billing. If you have multiple accounts, select the desired account.
  • Go to the Settings tab.
  • Select the three dots for the selected account, then select Edit Payment Arrangement. You can only change the payment method (not the amount) and it cannot be changed within 24 hours of a scheduled installment.
Locate payment arrangement history
  • Log in to Account Hub.
  • Go to Billing. If you have multiple accounts, select the desired account.
  • Go to the Settings tab.
  • Go to Manage Accounts, select Transactions. On the Transactions screen, the payment arrangement success notification will be displayed. Learn about ways to view your bill and usage on the Account Hub billing page.

Account Hub registration

Account Hub is an online self-service portal and account management tool for T-Mobile for Business customers. Use these steps to register for and set up the Account Hub.

On this page:

  • Register for Account Hub
  • Use Google Authenticator
  • Reset a password

Register for Account Hub

Self-registration

Self-registration – T-Mobile for Business

Use this process after your T-Mobile Business account has been activated. You must first set your account security PIN before completing self-registration..

If you’re unable to complete these steps, contact your Account Executive or the T-Mobile for Business Care Team at 1-800-375-1126.

  • Go to https://tfb.t-mobile.com. Global users will receive a unique registration link from their employer.
  • Select Sign Up.
  • Enter a T-Mobile billing account number or phone number.
    • Account Number Entry (Business Owners or Administrator Access): If you are an Account Administrator, managing either a single account or multiple accounts across an organization, enter your T-Mobile account number.
    • Phone Number Entry (End User Access): If you will only manage your line, enter your T-Mobile phone number.
  • Select Continue.
  • Choose your intended role if prompted.
  • Search for the billing account(s) on the list and select the checkbox next to each one you want to access.
  • Enter the associated account PIN(s).
    • Business owners and administrators must verify the correct PIN for each selected account to gain access.
    • Approval settings are determined by the Business Owner in Account Hub > Global Settings.
  • Verify your access based on your user role:
    • For end users:
      • Receive a One-Time PIN (OTP) sent to your T-Mobile phone number.
      • If approval is required, you’ll receive a message confirming your request has been submitted and an email once the admin approves it.
      • If no approval is required, you’ll proceed directly to account setup.
    • For global users:
      • Receive a One-Time PIN (OTP) sent to your email address.
      • If approval is required, you’ll receive a message confirming your request has been submitted and an email once the admin approves it.
      • If no approval is required, setup continues automatically.
  • Select Next.
  • Enter your first name, last name, and email address.
  • Select Next.
  • Complete the verification step.
  • Select Verify.
  • Create your T-Mobile ID and password.
  • Set up your security options:
    • Choose and answer security questions
    • Enable Google Authenticator (optional)
  • Access the Account Hub Dashboard upon successful registration.
Registration by invitation email

If you were invited to use the Account Hub, you’ll receive a registration email from t-mobileforbusiness@notifications.t-mobile.com. If you didn’t receive a registration email, be sure to check your spam/junk folder.

  • In the welcome email, select Register now to sign up for a T-Mobile ID and establish password and security questions.
  • If you already have a T-Mobile ID, selectthe Account Hub link in the registration email to log in.
  • If you’re using the T-Mobile app, you won’t automatically be redirected to the Account Hub. You must log in to Account Hub using a browser.
  • During the registration process, you’ll have the option to set up Google Authenticator once the password and security questions are created.

Use Google Authenticator

You have the option to enable Google Authenticator in the Account Hub during the registration process. If you didn’t enable it then, use the steps below to turn it on.

  • Select your user profile link on the left navigation to access the user profile.
  • Select the User Details box.
  • Select the Edit button for Password.
  • Choose the Set up option for Google Authenticator.
  • Enter the verification code that was sent to your email, then select Continue.
  • When the Secure your account with Google Authenticator message appears, select Get Started.
  • To download the Google Authenticator app, scan/enter the barcode, then select Continue setup.
  • Enter the code displaying in the Google Authenticator app, then select Confirm Code. A confirmation message indicating that setup is complete displays.

Reset a password

  • Select Forgot password? on the Account Hub login page.
  • Choose a verification method:
    • Email: follow the directions in the email to change the password.
    • Security questions: Provide the correct security answers, select NEXT to enter a new password
    • Google Authenticator: Must have been enabled prior to attempting a password reset. For additional steps to complete portal set up, visit Account Hub Global Settings page.

Account Hub reporting

With the Account Hub reporting tool you can generate customized billing reports for your T-Mobile for Business accounts.

On this page:

  • Tool details
  • Create report
  • Report dashboard

Tool details

Subscribed reports

If you have subscribed reports, Contact Business Care before making any hierarchy changes in the reporting tool, as they may affect your report results.

Bill cycle date

To get the most current data in your recurring reports, choose a subscription date that is at least six days later than the bill cycle close date. This is because the T-Mobile billing system needs some time to reconcile the charges.

Create report

Account size, hierarchy level, and data points affect how long it takes to generate the report. If you want an email alert when your larger reports are done, select Notify.

Select a report to generate
  • After logging in to Account Hub navigate to the Reporting page by selecting Reporting from the side panel.
  • On the Reporting page, switch to the Reports tab.
  • Choose the billing cycle for the report from the Billing Period Menu.
  • Choose the level of detail for the report from the Hierarchy menu.
  • Browse the list of reports and find the one you want. Select Customize to modify the report settings.
Select report data points to have in the report

Follow these steps to choose and arrange which data points to include in the report.

  • Select the data point to be included in the version of the report in the column selection and ordering section of the report builder.
  • All data will be selected by default.
  • Deselect the boxes next to the column to be removed from the report.
  • Move the selected column into the order to be displayed on the report output.
  • Once you have selected the data point and added any optional features, select Create Report.
Column option

Sort the columns in the report by ascending, descending, or hiding blank values using the column option feature.

Subscribe options

Schedule reports automatically using the Subscriptions option in the report builder by selecting the frequency and time of delivery. Note that billing base reports will only show changes when the monthly bill cycle is completed.

Use the subscription feature to get reports automatically at set intervals. Follow these steps:

  • Select the box to subscribe to the report.
  • Choose how often you want to receive the report from the drop-down menu. Pick one of these options:
    • Weekly
    • Biweekly
    • Monthly
    • Custom
  • Use the Subscription Date Calendar for the report to be created. If you want the report to show the latest billing data, make sure you select a date that is at least six days after the end of your bill cycle.
Notify option

You can get an email when your report is ready, but billing base reports with intervals shorter than a month will only update after your bill cycle ends.

To be notified by email when your report is ready, follow these steps:

  • Select the Send me an Email Notification box to receive an email notification when the report is ready.
  • Select the second email box and ADD additional emails separated by commas if you want other people to get the email notification.

Report dashboard

Manage my report

The delete action cannot be reversed. Reports are also automatically deleted 15 days after they are created. For ordered reports, you can use the action icon to access different options:

  • Open: This will open the HTML view in the reporting tool.
  • Subscribe: This will allow you to add a subscription to any ordered report that you have not subscribed yet.
  • Download: This will prompt you to download the report in PDF or CSV format.
  • Manage: This option is only available for report subscriptions. Update the subscription detail for a subscribed report.
  • Delete: This will manually delete the report from the dashboard never to be accessed after deleting.
View report details

To view the details of a report, follow these steps:

  • Log in to Account Hub.
  • select Reporting on the side navigation panel.
  • Locate the report to view details.
  • Select the down arrow by the report name to display the following details:
    • Description: A brief summary of what the report contains and why it is useful.
    • Accounts: Account numbers included in the report
    • Date and time report created: The date and time when the report was generated.
    • Current status: The report status such as ready, pending, or failed.
    • Frequency: How often the report is generated, such as daily, weekly, or monthly.
    • Format: The format of the report file, such as PDF, CSV, or Excel.
    • Recipients: The email addresses of users who receive the report via email. You can also see if the report is shared with other users on the Account Hub.

Account Hub user management

Manage your T-Mobile for Business Account Hub user profiles to perform account maintenance, billing, payments, place orders, and identify the assigned Account Manager.

User roles & permissions

Available roles with permissions in Account Hub:

Business Owners

Can manage all accounts, transactions, and assign different roles to Account Managers. They can also request approval for account transactions like ordering from End Users.

Account Managers

Have limited access and capabilities on the accounts they are assigned by the Business Owner and may need End User approval for some actions.

End Users

Can only access and perform transactions on lines assigned to them by the Business Owner or Account Manager.

Manage roles & permissions

  • Log in to Account Hub and go to Manage Users.
  • Select the Roles & Permissions tab.
  • Select Add Administrative Role to create a new role. Enter a name and an optional description for the role. Choose the permissions and approvals for the role.
  • Select Edit next to the role name to edit an existing role. Change the name, description, permissions, or approvals as needed.

Add a new user

  • Log in to Account Hub and go to Manage Users.
  • From the Manage Users tab, select Add new user.
  • Enter first name, last name, email, and role.
  • Select Add user.
  • An email with the registration link will be sent to the new user.
  • Users will need to follow the directions in the registration email to complete the registration. For complete steps, check out the Account Hub registration page.

Manage users

  • Log in to Account Hub and go to Manage Users.
  • From the Manage Users tab, select the three dots for the desired user you want to edit.
    • You can perform Quick access functions such as edit role, edit assigned accounts, block or unblock user, resend invitation, delete user, or remove role.
    • You can also select Edit user details to modify the name, email, portal access, assigned accounts, marketing preferences, roles, and permissions of the user.
  • Select Save after making any changes to apply updates.

Sensitive Transaction Notification List

Use these steps to create a list of users to receive a notification when a sensitive transaction is submitted in Account Hub.

  • Log in to Account Hub and go to Manage Users.
  • Select the three dots for the desired user you want to edit from the Manage Users tab.
  • Enter preferred notification method (email or SMS).
  • Select or deselect the transaction(s) you would like the line to receive notifications.
  • Click Save. For additional info to manage lines, visit the Manage your account page.

Upgrade

Account Management Approval Dashboard: Account Hub

Some account actions need approval before they take effect. You can turn on this feature from the dashboard in Account Hub for your organization.

Account Management Approval Dashboard

  • Select the Approval Dashboard tab.
  • From the list of transactions, select one or more checkboxes. From the Actions menu, select Approve or Reject.

Billing Responsible Party and authorized users - Business and Government

If you’re the person named as responsible for paying your T-Mobile bill as the account holder, you are the Billing Responsible Party, also known as BRP. As the BRP, you can assign authorized users on the account.

On this page:

  • Who is the Business and Government Billing Responsible Party (BRP)?
  • Who is an authorized user?
  • Adding or removing authorized users

Who is the Business and Government Billing Responsible Party (BRP)?

  • Business account BRPs are financially responsible for the account.
  • Government account BRPs belong to local, state, or federal government. Invoices are sent to the agency for airtime used for government purposes.
Permissions

On Business and Government accounts only, authorized users function as the BRP and have full BRP rights and can do the following:

  • Account type conversion requests
  • Add or remove authorized users
  • Change the bill cycle
  • Update the billing name
  • Cancel or resume canceled lines
  • Change of responsibility requests
  • New device purchase or upgrades using EIP within the first seven days of the account being activated. Learn more about device payment plans.
  • Manage the PIN/Passcode
  • Add or update the Primary Account Holder (PAH):
    • The PAH has full access to account management options when using the T-Mobile app, as well as online at T-Mobile.com.
    • They are able to set access and permissions for other lines, as well as view account activity.
    • For more information about the PAH, refer to Set up & manage your T-Mobile ID and Set up line permissions.

Who is an authorized user?

Authorized users can make changes to an account that could cause charges to your bill without prior permission of the BRP. Only the BRP, and authorized users on Business and Government accounts, can add or remove authorized users. They must be at least 18 years old or at least 21 in Puerto Rico.

Permissions

Authorized users can do the following:

  • Change the rate plan which could result in the loss of a retired plan and increase your monthly payment
  • Add or remove services or features
  • Receive notices and disclosures on behalf of the BRP
  • Purchase devices for use with T-Mobile service, including on an EIP after the initial seven days of the account being activated Learn more about device payment plans. Authorized users must provide the account or mobile number and the security PIN/passcode for account access outside of Account Hub and the T-Life/T-Mobile app (as well as a photo ID or business documentation if they visit a store).

Adding or removing authorized users

For Business and Government accounts, the BRP or an authorized user can contact us or use Account Hub.

Control Center automation

Automation rules use IF-THIS-THEN-THAT (IFTTT) logic to automatically manage, monitor, and configure your SIMs without manual intervention. Use them to reduce manual effort, control costs, and improve reliability across your connected devices.

On this page:

  • Set up automation rule
  • Set up IMEI change notification
  • Setup usage monitoring rule

Set up automation rule

  • Log in to Control Center and go to Devices.
  • Select Actions and Create New.
  • Select the rule type that fits your needs: Rule type

What it does

Available options

SIM Provisioning

Monitors SIM changes and triggers a follow-up action automatically.

SIM rate plan change, SIM state change, SIM customer field change.

Security

Triggers a rule when the network detects a change to a SIM’s IMEI.

IMEI change.

Subscription management

Triggers an action when a SIM hits a data threshold, approaches its expiration date, or completes its term.

SIM data limit, SIM expiration, SIM plan completion.

Tip: Check Frequently Used for quick access to the most common rules.

Usage monitoring trigger options

Trigger

What it monitors

Too many connections (Cycle to Date)

Triggers if a SIM establishes a set number of sessions during the billing cycle.

Number of session connections (24 hours)

Triggers if a SIM establishes a set number of sessions within 24 hours.

No connection

Triggers if a SIM does not establish a connection in a certain amount of hours.

Registration in a zone

Triggers if a SIM connects to a specific zone within the past 24 hours.

Cycle to date data usage

Triggers if a SIM reaches a set amount of data in a billing cycle.

Cycle to date usage in a zone

Triggers if a SIM reaches a set amount of data in a billing cycle within a specific zone.

Monthly pooled data usage

Triggers if a pool reaches a set percentage of its included data.

Recent data usage (24 hours)

Triggers if a SIM uses a set amount of data within 24 hours.

Recent SMS usage

Triggers if a SIM receives a set number of SMS messages within 24 hours or the billing cycle.

Monthly pooled SMS usage

Triggers if a pool reaches a set percentage of its pooled SMS usage.

Set up IMEI change notification

  • Log in to Control Center and go to Automation.
  • Select Actions and Create New Rule.
  • Select Security and IMEI Change.
  • Choose Send an Email and enter the email address and any desired fields.
  • Under Filters, set the SIM state to Activated.
  • Add any additional filters for rate plan, SIM state, or customer as needed. If no filters are applied, the rule will apply to all SIMs.
  • Enter a name for the rule.
  • Select Activate Rule.

Set up usuage monitoring rule

Monthly pooled usage

Monitor data consumption across all SIMs in the pool throughout the billing period. Your pool size is determined by the number of activated SIMs multiplied by the data amount defined per SIM.

  • Log in to Control Center and go to Automation.
  • Select Actions and Create New Rule.
  • Select Usage Monitoring and Cycle to Date Data Usage.
  • Set your usage threshold.
  • Choose Send an Email and enter the email address and any desired fields.
  • Enter a name for the rule.
  • Select Activate Rule. Cycle to date usage email notification

Monitor data usage per SIM throughout the billing cycle and send an email alert when a SIM approaches or exceeds its defined data limit.

  • Log in to Control Center and go to Automation.
  • Select Actions and Create New Rule.
  • Select Usage Monitoring and Cycle to Date Data Usage.
  • Set your usage threshold.
  • Choose Send an Email and enter the email address and any desired fields.
  • Enter a name for the rule.
  • Select Activate Rule. Cycle to date usage rate plan change

Control Center can automatically move a SIM to a higher data rate plan when it gets close to its current plan’s limit.

  • Go to Automation and select Actions and Create New Rule.
  • Select Usage Monitoring and Cycle to Date Data Usage.
  • Set your usage threshold. Select Exceeds a specified data limit of and enter the value converted to KB.
  • Choose Change Device’s Rate Plan and select the rate plan the SIM should move to when the rule is triggered, typically a higher data tier.
  • If needed, enable the option to revert to the original rate plan at the end of the billing cycle.
  • Under Filters, select the base rate plan, SIM state, or customer to narrow which SIMs the rule applies to.
  • Enter a name for the rule.
  • Select Activate Rule.

View bill and invoice reports

Control Center registration

Control Center empowers organizations to optimize their T-Mobile IoT experience.

On this page:

  • Control Center vs Account Hub
  • Register for Control Center

Control Center vs Account Hub

  • Control Center is used to add users and manage SIM connectivity, statuses, automations, and other service configurations. It can be accessed using the standalone portal.
  • Account Hub is used to add users and manage your T-Mobile account, including billing and ordering new SIMs and solutions. It can be accessed within Account Hub or Control Center.
    • Note: Government accounts do not have Account Hub access. Invoices are on the Inseego portal and users are managed on the User Management Portal.

Register for Control Center

After approving your order, you’ll receive a welcome email.

  • In the welcome email, click the custom link to create a user ID.
    • The first user is set up with the ACCOUNTADMIN role and can create additional users who can view and manage the devices in the account’s global network​.
  • Go to Control Center (link will not work until the user ID is created) or Account Hub for platform access.

SIM management

    • Static IP.

Process batch updates

  • Log in to Control Center and go to Devices.

Data Direct

T-Mobile for Business accounts on the TFB1 bill format can use Data Direct to set up and manage existing services with T-Mobile for Business via the Account Hub Reporting tool.

On this page:

  • Things to know
  • Data Direct Explained
  • Data Direct Setup
  • Manage Data Direct

Things to Know

This provides information on modifications, known issues, and enhancements for the Data Direct Tool, which is only available to customers on the TFB1 bill format.

Data Direct Explained

Data Direct allows customers to access their invoice data in an electronic file format, instead of relying on paper documents. It provides a secure and convenient way to download or transfer invoice data in a pipe (“I”) delimited text file. Data Direct can help customers automate their business processes and reduce the effort required to process large bills. Each Data Direct file corresponds to one invoice.

Data Direct Setup

Create Data Direct file
  • Log in to Account Hub.
  • Search by account to ensure you’re accessing the correct account.
  • Select Reporting from the navigation panel.
  • Select the Enhanced Delivery tab.
  • Select Data Direct from the data format option drop-down menu.
  • Enter the corresponding data in each of the required fields:
    • Name
    • Email
    • Contact Phone Number
    • Include Usage Details: Select Yes or No
    • GPG Key. This is the public GPG key text block. This is used to encrypt the file. File encryption is required.
    • GPG Recipient Key. This is in email address format.
    • Delivery method: Select ‘Manual Download from Website only’ or ‘SFTP and Manual Download from Website’.
    • If SFTP delivery method is selected include the following:
      • Destination IP address
      • Destination DNS Name
      • Destination Username
      • Destination Full Directory Path
      • Destination Server File
  • Enter any optional fields. An optional field not commonly used is the Exclude Ban Filter list. By default, a Data Direct file is created for all accounts under your organization. You may choose to exclude accounts from having a Data Direct file created. Any account not on the excluded list then has a Data Direct file created.
  • Select Create once all required and optional fields are populated.
  • If SFTP and Manual Download from Website is selected above, send an email with the following details to eftapplicationteam@t-mobile.com:
    • Destination Server Hostname (name of the customer’s server, e.g., abc.def.com):
    • Destination Server IP Address:
    • Destination Server sFTP Port (i.e., secure File Transfer Protocol):
    • Destination Server Directory Path (file delivery location):
    • Choose an Authentication Mode:
      • Username & Password
      • Username & SSH Key for Passwordless authentication
    • Username that T-Mobile will use for logging in:
    • File Destination Team Contact (one email address or email distribution list):
    • Choose the Required Notification Type:
      • Failure only
      • Success only
      • Both
    • Notification Contact (one email address or email distribution list):
  • The file setup request will be sent to an office billing team for set up and to coordinate testing for the SFTP connection. The file will be available for download or transfer the first billing cycle after enrollment.

Manage Data Direct

Edit existing Data Direct
  • Log in to Account Hub.
  • Search by account instead to ensure you’re accessing the correct account.
  • Select Reporting from the Navigation panel.
  • Select the Enhanced Delivery tabs.
  • Select Edit next to the Data Direct product you currently have. This loads the Data format and delivery options page for that product.
  • Edit the required and optional fields as needed and click Update.
Download Data Direct file
  • Log in to Account Hub.
  • Search by account instead of company name to ensure correct account access.
  • Select Reporting from the Navigation panel.
  • Select the Enhanced Delivery tab.
  • Locate the file from the Enhanced Delivery Dashboard.
  • Select Download next to the file for the needed bill cycle.

Still need help?

Contact your T-Mobile for Business Dedicated Expert for additional support with Data Direct.

DIGITS: Account Hub

Access the DIGITS portal

Visit the Account Hub User Management page if you cannot complete these steps, as you may need more permissions from your Account Admin or Business Owner.

Electronic Data Interchange (EDI)

Some T-Mobile for Business accounts can use the Account Hub Reporting tool to set up and manage Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) services.

On this page:

  • EDI explained
  • Set up EDI
  • Manage EDI

EDI explained

This capability is a way of sending and receiving large files securely and efficiently between different organizations. It uses standard file formats that need special software to translate them, specifically ANSI X12 file format. EDI Tool features are only for some bill formats.

Benefits
  • Direct download
  • Encrypted STFP file transfer
  • Data security during the transfer
  • Data access control
  • Minimized effort for large bills

Set up to create EDI file

  • Log in to Account Hub. If you have multiple accounts, select the desired account.
  • Select Reporting from the navigation panel.
  • Select the Enhanced Delivery & Formats tab.
  • Select the + icon by the New Data Delivery option to load the data format and delivery options page.
  • Select Electronic Data Interchange from the data delivery options menu.
  • Enter the corresponding data in each of the required fields:
    • Name
    • Email
    • Contact Phone Number
    • Included usage details: Select Yes or No
    • Delivery method: Select STFP or Manual download.
    • If SFTP delivery method is selected include the following:
      • Destination IP address
      • Destination DNS Name
      • Destination Username
      • Destination Full Directory Path
      • Destination Server File
    • ISA07 Interchange ID Qualifier
    • ISA08 Interchange Receiver ID
    • GS03 Application Receiver Code
    • Select the component Element separator
    • Select the Segment separator
  • Enter any optional fields. An optional field not commonly used is Excluded BANs list. The option to choose to exclude accounts from the EDI file for billing data for specific accounts. Any account not on the excluded list will have the billing data for that account sent in the EDI file for that organization.
  • Select Create once all required and optional fields are populated.
  • If SFTP and Manual Download from Website is selected above, send an email with the following details to eftapplicationteam@t-mobile.com:
    • Destination Server Hostname (name of the customer’s server, e.g., abc.def.com):
    • Destination Server IP Address:
    • Destination Server sFTP Port (i.e., secure File Transfer Protocol):
    • Destination Server Directory Path (file delivery location):
    • Choose an Authentication Mode:
      • Username & Password
      • Username & SSH Key for Passwordless authentication
    • Username that T-Mobile will use for logging in:
    • File Destination Team Contact (one email address or email distribution list):
    • Choose the Required Notification Type:
      • Failure only
      • Success only
      • Both
    • Notification Contact (one email address or email distribution list):
  • The file setup request will be sent to an office billing team for set up and to coordinate testing for the SFTP connection. The file will be available for download or transfer the first billing cycle after enrollment.

Manage EDI

Edit existing EDI
  • Log in to Account Hub. If you have multiple accounts, select the desired account.
  • Select Reporting from the navigation panel.
  • Select the Enhanced Delivery and Formats tabs.
  • Select Edit by the current EDI product. This loads the Data format and delivery options page for that EDI product.
  • Edit the required and optional fields as needed and click Update.
Download EDI file
  • Log in to Account Hub. If you have multiple accounts, select the desired account.
  • Select Reporting from the navigation panel.
  • Select the Enhanced Delivery and Formats tab.
  • Locate the attachment list from the Enhanced Delivery and Formats dashboard.
  • Select Download next to the file for the needed bill cycle. Check out our Billing articles for additional bill support.

Hierarchy Management tool

The Hierarchy Management Tool is an online self-service portal to manage changes to the hierarchy to fit your specific needs.

On this page:

  • What to Know
  • Hierarchy Management
  • Node Management
  • DAC Management

What to Know

Use this section for tool release modifications info, hierarchy tree, and minimum basic hierarchy requirements.

The Hierarchy Management Tool

With the tool you can design a hierarchy tree that matches your business and for your accounting needs, you can produce customized reports and invoices.

Minimum Basic Hierarchy

This is a node structure that enables the TFB1 bill format and the TFB reporting tool. The hierarchy is made up of the Root node, MCCID group node, and the account reporting nodes under that MCCID.

MCCID

This is a number that identifies all accounts with the same tax ID for billing and reporting purposes.

Hierarchy Management

Use this section to make hierarchy changes in the tool.

Create hierarchy

Use these steps to set up a basic reporting structure for your organization if it was not done at activation.

  • Log in to Account Hub and use the left navigation panel to select the Hierarchy tool.
  • Create a reporting tree for the account if you receive a prompt that one does not exist.
  • Select Create Reporting Tree.
  • Provide the required information in the Root name field in the pop-up window. The Root description and MCCID description fields are options but allow you to provide relevant information.
  • Select Next once the required fields are complete.
  • Select Confirm on the confirmation screen to create the reporting tree.
Edit an existing hierarchy

Use these steps to create a reporting tree with a child node for each account under the MCCID.

  • Log in to Account Hub and search by account to select the desired account from the list.
  • Use the left navigation panel to select the Hierarchy tool.
  • View the existing reporting tree if a reporting tree exists for the account. Select View reporting tree. Use the Add node steps below to add nodes above or below the existing account reporting nodes to complete the Hierarchy Reporting tree.

Node Management

Use the steps in this section to make node changes in the tool.

Add above the account reporting node

If no Reporting tree exists for the account, create a hierarchy.

  • Log in to Account Hub.
  • Search by account instead of the company name to ensure you’re accessing the correct account in Account Hub. If you have multiple accounts, select the desired account.
  • Select the Hierarchy tool using the left navigation panel.
  • Select the three vertical dots by the MCCID GROUP.
  • Select Add Child.
  • Use the drop-down to select the node type to add:
    • Division
    • Region
    • Cost Center
    • Sector
    • Line of business may be added above an account reporting node.
  • Select the type of node from the drop-down.
  • Enter the node name in the node name field.
  • Enter optional description information if needed in the node description field.
  • Select Add once the required data is entered.
  • Verify the new node appears in the Reporting tree. If it doesn’t appear, select the refresh icon.
Add nodes below the account reporting node

Any child node added below the account reporting level in the Hierarchy tool will reflect on the printed, PDF invoice, and the digital presentment in the Billing section of Account Hub once the next bill cycle closes.

If no Reporting tree exists, create a hierarchy. Either node type may be selected to add.

  • Log in to Account Hub.
  • Search by account instead of the company name to ensure you’re accessing the correct account in Account Hub. If you have multiple accounts, select the desired account.
  • Use the left navigation panel to select the Hierarchy tool.
  • Locate the account Reporting node to add a child node
  • Select the three vertical dots by the account reporting node
  • Select Add Child.
  • Use the drop-down menu in the pop-up to select the node type to add.
    • Department
    • Branch
    • Sub-Branch
    • DAC (Department Accounting Code) may be added below the account Reporting node. For the DAC to report properly they must be attached to a department.
  • Select the type of node to add.
  • Enter the node name in the node name field.
  • Enter the optional description information if needed in the node description field.
  • Select Add once the required data is entered.
  • Verify the new node appears in the Reporting tree. If it doesn’t appear, select the refresh icon.
Move a node

When moving a node, the entire hierarchy under that node will be moved. This will limit the ability of some nodes to move, such as a node that contains lines assigned in the billing system to another node with a different account. To move these nodes, remove the lines and add them to the correct nodes after they have been moved into the billing system.

If Reporting tree does not exist for the account create a hierarchy.

Some nodes, such as Root, MCCID, Division, and Department are not to be moved due to the nature of those nodes.

  • Log in to Account Hub.
  • Search by account instead of the company name to ensure you’re accessing the correct account in Account Hub. If you have multiple accounts, select the desired account.
  • Use the left navigation panel to select the Hierarchy tool.
  • Locate the node to move and highlight it.
  • Select the three vertical dots icon.
  • Select Move.
  • Verify the full reporting tree path for that node displays.
  • Select the target location node to move the node.
  • Notice a pop-up of the new location of the node displays.
  • Select Confirm once you verify the new location is correct.
  • Moved node at new location displays.
  • Refresh the reporting tree using the refresh icon. If the node move location was not eligible an error detail will display.
Remove a node

A node that contains lines assigned in the hierarchy below it cannot be removed. To remove these nodes, first remove the lines from the DACs below the node that will be removed, then remove the node, or move the DAC to another node within the same account Reporting node.

If no Reporting tree exists for the account, create a hierarchy.

  • Log in to Account Hub.
  • Search by account instead of the company name to ensure you’re accessing the correct account in Account Hub. If you have multiple accounts, select the desired account.
  • Using the left navigation panel select the Hierarchy tool.
  • Locate the node to remove.
  • Select the node.
  • Select the three vertical dots by the node name.
  • Select Remove.
  • Confirm the removed node display.
  • Select Confirm once you verify the correct node to remove. The node, if eligible to be removed should no longer display in the reporting tree.
  • Refresh the reporting tree using the refresh icon.
Edit an existing node

If no Reporting tree exists for the account, create a hierarchy.

  • Log in to Account Hub.
  • Search by account instead of the company name to ensure you’re accessing the correct account in Account Hub. If you have multiple accounts, select the desired account.
  • Use the left navigation panel to select the Hierarchy tool.
  • Locate the node to edit and select it.
  • Select the three vertical dots icon and select Edit.
  • Pop-up displays and edits to node name may be completed if eligible. Edits to the node description are optional.
  • Select Next once the edits are complete.
  • Verify the information is correct in the pop-up window and select Confirm.

DAC (Department Accounting Code) Management

Use this section to make DAC changes in the tool.

Add an address to a DAC

Use the steps to add an address to the DAC. This action triggers a statement to be sent to the DAC address for just those listed under that DAC. Any account-level services will not be included in the DAC courtesy statement but will be on the invoice that is sent to the account address.

  • Log in to Account Hub.
  • Search by account instead of the company name to ensure you’re accessing the correct account in Account Hub. If you have multiple accounts, select the desired account.
  • Hover over a specific DAC in the Hierarchy Management tool, and look for the Courtesy Statement indicator to determine if a DAC has a courtesy statement address. You can edit existing DAC nodes by following the steps on this page to Edit an existing node.
  • In the Add Child Node screen, once you add child nodes, you’ll have the option for the Courtesy Statement indicator.
    • To populate an address box, select the toggle to Send Courtesy Statement, then select Add. This will open the mailing address box.
    • By default, this indicator is off.
  • Complete the mailing address fields, then select validate. Addresses are validated with the USPS database.
    • Invalid addresses generate a ‘Not Valid’ error message in red. Correct the address.
    • Valid addresses generate a ‘Valid’ indicator in green.
  • Select Add. DAC courtesy statement is sent starting the next statement cycle.
  • To remove a DAC courtesy statement address, follow the steps on this page to Edit an existing node. Then toggle Send Courtesy Statement to off. You’ll get a yellow message stating Once confirmed, DAC Courtesy Statement will not be generated. Select Confirm.
Add lines to a DAC

If no Reporting tree exists, create a hierarchy.

  • Log in to Account Hub.
  • Search by account instead of the company name to ensure you’re accessing the correct account in Account Hub. If you have multiple accounts, select the desired account.
  • Use the left navigation panel to select the Hierarchy tool.
  • Locate the DAC node to add a line and select it.
  • Notice that once selected, a pop-out menu will appear. This menu displays all currently assigned subscriber lines on this DAC.
  • Select Add Subscriber to add a line to DAC.
  • Locate the phone number of the lines to add by either selecting through the unassigned subscribers from the account or using the search field to enter the phone number. To confirm the line, use the dropdown arrow by each line to expand the details section and view the line identifiers for each phone number. Line identifiers populated in Account Hub will be present in the Hierarchy tool.
  • Select Add by the line once the phone number/s to add have been located.
  • Select Confirm on the pop-up confirmation if the phone number selected is correct.
Remove lines from a DAC - Department Accounting Code

If an account Reporting tree doesn’t exist, create a hierarchy.

  • Log in to Account Hub.
  • Search by account instead of the company name to ensure you’re accessing the correct account in Account Hub. If you have multiple accounts, select the desired account.
  • Use the left navigation panel to select the hierarchy.
  • Select the DAC node to add a subscriber.
  • Notice a menu will pop out once selected. This menu displays all the current assigned subscriber lines on this DAC.
  • Select Add Subscriber in the pop-out menu to add a line to DAC.
  • Locate the phone number/s of the lines to remove by either selecting through the assigned subscribers on the DAC or using the search field to enter the number. To confirm the line, use the dropdown arrow by each line to expand the details section and view the line identifiers for each phone number. Line identifiers populated in Account Hub will be present in the Hierarchy tool.
  • Select Add by the line once the number or numbers to remove have been located.
  • Select Confirm on the pop-up confirmation if the number selected is correct.

LED Indicators, Ports & Buttons

LED Indicators

The front of the router has a device status LED, a cellular status LED, and a Wi-Fi status LED. Each LED changes colors and blinks or glows solid to communicate current states for the device. You can turn off the indicator LEDs in the Admin web UI with Settings > Preferences.

Ports

The two ethernet ports on the back of the router can be configured as WAN or LAN.

The FX4100 features 2 x SMA connectors for external antennas.

Device display

The device display provides device information and alerts, and allows you to perform actions, like pair with a mesh node or check for a firmware update.

  • Use the display button to navigate through the display:
    • Short press (<1 second): cycles through the display menu or submenu options.
    • Long press (>3 seconds): initiates an action or accesses/exits a submenu.
  • The device display times out after 60 seconds. Main menu

Set up

  • Plug the power cord into the router and plug the power adapter into an AC wall outlet.
  • Scan the QR code on the bottom of the router titled Scan for Inseego mobile app. You can also visit inseego.com to download the app.
  • Follow the instructions to connect to the FX4100 and identify the ideal location from the app.
  • Optional: Register device using the admin password located on the bottom label.
  • Optional: External Antenna
    • Finger tighten your external antennas to the CELL1 and CELL2 external antenna ports.
    • To enable external antennas, toggle the antenna switch on the back of the router (located between the external antenna connection ports) to Ext Ant On. The FX4100 does not have a software antenna enablement option.
    • When using antennas, the following conditions are needed:
      • Selected antenna covers the appropriate cellular frequencies.
      • Antenna has higher gain than the device itself (including cable loss).
      • Device is in a mid to low coverage area (<~100 dBm RSRP). No additional router configuration is needed to enable Static IP.

Monitor & Manage

You can manage and monitor the FX4100 remotely through Inseego Connect. This option is offered as an add-on service. You can also access the web UI on at http://192.168.1.1 for a full set of device management features. The Inseego Mobile app also offers basic device monitoring and management when accessed locally.

Change Wi-Fi (Access to the network) password

  • Access Web Gateway User Interface (GUI): Inseego FX4100 Gateway Device by navigating to http://192.168.1.1.

  • Select > from the Home page Wi-Fi panel or select Wi-Fi from the side menu.

  • Select the Primary Network tab or Guest Network tab.

  • Enter a new password in the Password Field, or you can use the Generate New Password button to insert a strong random password in the Password Field.

  • If this setting is greyed out, first disable MLO, make changes, and then re-enable MLO.

  • Select Save Changes. Change the Administration (Admin) password

  • From the local Web UI: Select the down arrow next to Sign Out in the top-right corner of any Admin Web UI page and select Change Password.

  • From Inseego Connect: Select Device > Admin Password from the Configure side menu.

  • Enter your current Admin password, then enter a new password and confirm it. The new password must have a length between 14 and 32 characters and contain at least one special character and number.

  • Select a security question from the drop-down list and type an answer to the question. Answers are case-sensitive.

  • Select Save Changes. A confirmation appears.

  • Select OK. The next time you sign in to the Admin web UI, use the new Admin password. If you cannot remember the password, select Forgot Admin password. After you correctly answer the security question you set up, the current password is displayed.

Restore Factory Settings

It can take over two minutes for the router to restart after the first time a factory reset is performed. Any changes made to settings will be lost.

  • Verify that your router is powered on.
  • Locate the reset button on the back of your router.
  • To reboot the router: Press the reset button for one second.
  • To reset to factory settings: Press the reset button for five seconds until the device resets. The display will show “device initiated reset”.

Inseego FX4100 Router Troubleshooting

Troubleshooting for the Inseego FX4100 cellular router.

On this page:

  • Device Placement
  • LED Alerts
  • Toggle Network Mode
  • Check Antenna Switch
  • Wi-Fi SSID

Device Placement

  • Ensure you have chosen a good location for your router:
    • Ideally on an exterior wall
    • Near a window but not in direct sunlight
    • On or above ground level (not in a basement)
    • Clear from obstructions and interference from other electronic devices
    • Outside of cabinets or locations that can get excessively hot
  • Try different locations to try to get a better signal.
    • Move the router, then check the LED behavior:
      • The device LED is the middle LED with the bars.
      • It is blue for a great signal, green for a good signal, and yellow for a fair signal.
    • Use the Inseego app:
      • Download the Inseego app from the App Store or Google Play.
      • Connect to the device’s Wi-Fi and open the Inseego app. From the home page, select your device and select Go to location survey.
      • Follow instructions in the app to find the best place for your device.
      • It may take the router 1-2 minutes to boot up after it’s moved.

LED Alerts

The FX4100 has an LED display with alerts.

  • To view the alert, select the display button to toggle through the menu options.
  • The last option is Alerts.
  • Press the display button for 3 seconds to review. LED Display Message

Troubleshooting

Show display with x through routing arrows

Contact us for help.

Invalid SIM

Contact us for help.

SIM Error

  • Power off the device.

  • Reinsert the SIM and try again.

  • If issue persists, contact us for help. No SIM

  • Power off the device

  • Reinsert the SIM and try again.

  • If issue persists, contact us for help. No Service

The device cannot detect the LTE/5G network.

  • Change Network Technology to Auto to expand network search.
  • Refer to Toggle Network Settings below. No Mobile Network

No mobile networks are detected.

  • Review device placement guidelines.

  • Change Network Technology to Auto to expand network search.

  • Refer to Toggle Network Settings below.

  • If issue persists, contact us for help. Updates Available

  • A firmware update is available.

  • You can install from the LCD screen or wait, and the update will be installed automatically or on the next device reboot. Update Failed, No Changes

  • Reboot the device and the device will re-attempt the firmware update.

  • If this happens repeatedly, contact us for help. 90% Data; Fees Possible

  • This alert is set by the user and does not reflect T-Mobile Network data usage.

  • Change these alerts in the Web GUI under Data Usage.

  • To view T-Mobile Network Usage, refer to the Account Hub. Data Limit Hit, Fees Apply

  • This alert is set by the user and does not reflect T-Mobile Network data usage.

  • Change these alerts in the Web GUI under Data Usage.

  • To view T-Mobile Network Usage, refer to the Account Hub. Wi-Fi Is Off

  • Reboot the router.

  • If this doesn’t work, then turn Wi-Fi on by connecting to the router using an Ethernet cable.

  • If this doesn’t work, then factory reset the router.

  • If the issue persists, contact us for help. Device Hot, Turning Off

  • The device will turn off.

  • Follow the device placement guidelines above. No 5G SA, Check Mode

  • Change 5G Network Mode to Auto (NSA/SA) or NSA.

  • Refer to Toggle Network Settings below. No 5G NSA, Check Mode

  • Change Network Technology to Auto (LTE/5G).

  • Refer to Toggle Network Settings below.

Toggle Network Mode

Depending on your location, changing the Network Settings may help.

  • Option 1: If the router is online, change the setting using Inseego Connect.
    • Select the device from the list, then Configure > Mobile Network > Carrier Settings.
    • Ensure Network Technology is set to Auto.
    • Change 5G Network Mode to NSA.
    • The device will reboot.
    • Use your phone to conduct a speed test.
    • If the device is not faster, change 5G Network Mode back to Auto.
  • Option 2: Change settings using the Web GUI:
    • On your phone or laptop, verify you are connected to the Wi-Fi of the Inseego FX4100 router.
    • Navigate to http://192.168.1.1.
    • Go to Settings > Advanced tab > select continue.
    • On the Cellular tab, ensure Network Technology is set to Auto.
    • Change the 5G Network Mode to NSA.
    • The device will reboot.
    • Use your phone to conduct a speed test.
    • If the device is not faster, set 5G Network Mode back to Auto.

Check Antenna Switch

The FX4100 has a hardware switch.

  • On the back of the FX4100, there is a label SIM / External Antenna.
  • Remove the back plastic cover on the router, and ensure the switch is set to Ext Ant OFF.

Wi-Fi SSID

If you can’t see the Wi-Fi SSID, or you can see the Wi-Fi SSID but can’t connect.

  • Verify you can see the Wi-Fi SSID from other devices.
  • If you can’t see the Wi-Fi SSID from any device:
    • Reboot the router.
    • If a reboot initially resolves the issue, but then it comes back, disable DFS (dynamic frequency selection) from the WebGUI (http://192.168.1.1) under Wi-Fi Settings.
    • If available, connect to the router with an ethernet cable to validate Wi-Fi is turned on.
      • Navigate to http://192.168.1.1
      • Select Wi-Fi. From the Settings tab, ensure Wi-Fi is enabled.
      • From the Primary Network and/or Guest Network tab, ensure Broadcast primary network name (SSID) is checked.
    • Factory reset the router by holding down the reset button on the back of the router for five seconds.
    • If the issue persists, contact us.
  • If you can see the SSID from other devices, but just can’t with one:
    • This is rare and can happen with older devices, especially printers.
    • Go to the Wi-Fi settings in Inseego Connect and under 802.11 mode, select 802.11bgn.
    • Try connecting with the device again.
  • If you can see the SSID but can’t connect:
    • If the device can see the Wi-Fi network but not connect, change the security type to WPA2 Personal or WPA/WPA2 mixed mode.
    • If you continue to have issues, contact us.

Inseego X700 Mesh

Connecting the X700 Mesh Wi-Fi to your existing FX4100 Wi-Fi network expands Wi-Fi coverage by removing dead spots and areas with weak signal. The X700 Mesh Wi-Fi is only compatible with the FX4100. You can add up to three X700 Mesh Wi-Fi’s to each FX4100 to expand your Wi-Fi footprint to ~5000 sq. ft.

On this page:

  • Device images
  • Tech Specs
  • Front LED
  • Set Up and Manage
  • Reboot or Reset

Back

  • Operating temperature with limitations • 14°F to 122°F (-10°C to +50°C) Power adapter

  • Full power AP Wi-Fi (~30dBm)

Indicator LED

Device/signal status

Front LED

The LED is located on the front of the device. The visual LED display allows you to quickly obtain the current condition.

Set up

Before Starting Set Up

  • Both the router and mesh node must be powered on and ready to pair.

  • The router and mesh node should be close together to pair.

  • You must pair the router and mesh node within 30 seconds of one another when pairing via Wi-Fi.

  • The multicolor LED on the X700, and the device display and Wi-Fi status LED on the FX4100 help guide the pairing process. Set up steps

  • Power on the FX4100.

    • You can connect up to three mesh nodes to one FX4100, pairing one at a time.
    • When the FX4100 Wi-Fi status LED is solid green, it is ready to pair.

  • Power on the X700. Plug it in using the provided AC adapter, a USB powered hub, or a USB-powered delivery device. When the Mesh LED is blinking green, it is ready to pair.

  • Pair the X700 with an FX4100 using Wi-Fi or Ethernet.

    • Pairing with Wi-Fi using the FX4100 device display
      • Select the device display button on the FX4100 repeatedly until you see Wi-Fi Mesh: Hold button to add.
      • Select and hold the device display button.
      • When prompted by the display, Select the Mesh button on the back of the X700 within 30 seconds.
      • The LED on the X700 and the Wi-Fi status LED on the router blink blue while pairing. Pairing typically takes 2-3 minutes.
      • When the display shows Wi-Fi Mesh: Paired! and the LED on the mesh node is a solid color, pairing is complete.
    • Pair using the Admin web UI
      • Go to http://192.168.1.1 to access the Admin web UI for the FX4100. Navigate to Wi-Fi > Mesh.
      • Select Add Node on the UI Mesh tab.
      • Within 30 seconds, select the Mesh button on the back of the X700.
      • The LED on the X700 and the router blink blue while pairing. Pairing typically takes 2-3 minutes.
      • When the Wi-Fi status LED on the router is solid blue and the LED on the mesh node is a solid color, pairing is complete.
    • Pairing with Ethernet
      • Connect an Ethernet cable from the X700 to the LAN port on the FX4100.
      • Pairing is automatic. The LED on the X700 blinks blue while pairing. When pairing is complete the LED is solid.
      • When you disconnect the Ethernet cable, the X700 remains paired via Wi-Fi.

  • Find a location for the X700

    • Adjust the location of the X700 using the LED color as a guide. Solid blue indicates a great signal. Solid green indicates a good signal.
    • Location suggestions:
      • Use the FX4100 Admin web UI, navigate to the Wi-Fi Mesh tab to ensure X700 nodes are using 5GHz as the Connection Type.
      • With 5GHz coverage, mesh range is up to 50 feet.
      • Walls, floors, appliances, furniture, pets, and people between the X700 and FX4100 reduce range.
      • 1 wall = approximately 10 feet reduction in range. Managing the X700

You can manage the X700 mesh node(s) through the FX4100’s Admin web UI or Inseego Connect settings:

  • Admin web UI: Access the web UI at http://192.168.1.1.
    • Use Wi-Fi Settings > Mesh to view all mesh nodes paired with your FX4100, add or remove a mesh node, or reboot a mesh node. You can also see the connected devices for each mesh node.
    • Use Connected Devices to view more details on connected devices. You can also block or unblock devices from internet access.
    • You can monitor mesh nodes with the Inseego Mobile™ app.
  • Inseego Connect: All T-Mobile owned Inseego FX devices come with the option of purchasing the Inseego Connect Add-on. Work with your Account team to order the Inseego Connect Add-on, which provides Manager access.

Reboot or Reset

  • To reboot the X700: Press the reset button for one second.
  • To perform a factory reset (removes pairing): Press and hold the reset button for five seconds.

Manage Line Identifier: Account Hub

The Line ID integrates across all the pages on the T-Mobile for Business Account Hub to enable users to update active, suspended, and reserved lines only. It carries line ID information to the new phone number and account such as account-to-account line moves and phone number changes.

Set or change Line Identifier

  • Log in to Account Hub.
  • Go to Manage Accounts. If you have multiple accounts, select the desired account.

Manage services: Account Hub

Use these Account Hub steps to make service changes to your T-Mobile for Business account.

On this page:

  • Change services
  • Block or unblock international services
  • Auto Deploy and Enable Bill to BAN
  • Turn on or turn off SIM protection
  • Turn on or turn off transfer protection

Change services

  • Log in to Account Hub and go to Manage Accounts to select the desired account if you have multiple accounts.
  • From the Manage Lines tab, select the three dots for the desired line and select Change service. The Change Services window appears.
  • Select or deselect the active service(s) you’d like to add or remove. Select Review changes.
  • Review the changes and select the checkbox to agree to the Terms and Conditions.
  • Select Submit changes and receive a transaction number, which can be viewed on the Transaction History page.

Block or unblock international services

  • Log in to Account Hub and go to Manage Accounts to select the desired account if you have multiple accounts.
  • From the Manage Lines tab, select the line you want to change the service preference on and then select the number.
  • Within the Plans & Services tab, select the toggle on/off option for Block Stateside International Calling or Block Data on International Roaming.
  • Select Confirm to submit your changes.

Auto Deploy and Enable Bill to BAN

Use these steps so Authorized Users to Enable Auto Deploy Block Auto Deploy.or Enable Bill to BAN at a line level.

  • Log in to Account Hub.

  • Go to Manage Accounts. If you have multiple accounts, select the desired account.

  • From the Manage Lines tab, select the line you want to change the service preference on and then select the number.

  • Within the Plans & Services tab, Select International Data Passes

  • Choose either Enable Auto Deploy Block Auto Deploy or Enable Bill to BAN and toggle on or off.

  • Select Confirm to submit your changes. Enable Auto Deploy – The International Pass Auto Enroll feature enables the Account Holder to enroll a specific line with the Automatic International Data Pass deployment functionality.

  • Block Auto Deploy – The Block International Pass Auto Enroll sub feature enables the Account Holder to block enroll a specific line with the Automatic International Data Pass deployment functionality.

  • Enable Bill to BAN – The International Pass Bill to Account feature enables the Account Holder to allow a specific line to select “bill to account” when purchasing an International Data Pass.

  • Select Confirm to submit your changes.

Turn on or turn off SIM protection

  • Log in to Account Hub and go to Manage Accounts to select the desired account if you have multiple accounts.
  • From the Manage Lines tab, select the three dots for the desired line and select the SIM protection preference.
  • Request and validate one-time PIN.
  • Select the three dots for the desired line and select the SIM protection preference.
  • Confirm transaction and receive a transaction number, which can be viewed on the Transaction History page.

Turn on or turn off transfer protection

  • Log in to Account Hub and go to Manage Accounts to select the desired account if you have multiple accounts.
  • From the Manage Lines tab, select the line(s) you would like to make changes to.
  • Select the More Actions button on the top right taskbar.
  • Select to turn on or off transfer protection.
  • Request and validate one-time PIN.
  • Confirm transaction and receive a transaction number, which can be viewed on the Transaction History page. Visit the Account Hub User Management page if you cannot complete these steps, as you may need more permissions from your Account Admin or Business Owner. Military plan verification: Account Hub

Confirm your military status through the Account Hub within 45-days of starting your service if you have a T-Mobile Military plan. This will help you get the benefits and discounts that are offered on up to 12 lines of the plan.

Verify Military status

  • Log in to Account Hub and go to Manage Account to select the desired account.
  • Select the Account action menu, then select Verify Military Status.
  • Enter required info into the form for the military person on the account or the registered family member if selecting Gold Star.
  • Select Submit Information. You will get a text or an email confirmation within 48 hours whether your credentials are verified or not.

You will need to provide proof of service if your credentials are not verified, and upon completion you will get an email within 24 hours.

Visit the Account Hub User Management page if you cannot complete these steps, as you may need more permissions from your Account Admin or Business Owner.

Reading your bill: T-Mobile for Business

Get all the information you need to help you understand all the details and various sections on your T-Mobile for Business billing statements, which can also be found in the Account Hub.

View bill

On this page:

  • Monthly statement section
  • Before this bill section
  • Account details section
  • Monthly reports section
  • Charges and usage section

Monthly statement section

This section of the bill includes a welcome message and a thank you for choosing T-Mobile. The billing statement shows the total amount due for this bill that is based on the previous balance, current charges, and taxes/fees. Find more details about charges, due date, balance in the charges/summary section, and compare recent monthly charges.

Before this bill section

This section is a summary of payments, credit, and adjustments that affect the balance and applicable taxes. Credits and adjustments applied before the billing cycle ends appear as a credit.

Account details section

This section shows the total charges for your account and each line, as well as the usage details per line.

Monthly reports section

This section gives an overview of the factors that affect your bill, such as highest usage costs, highest plan costs, monthly discounts, and equipment installment plans.

Charges and usage section

Detailed Charges

This section details your account and the taxes that apply to your charges. You can see how your charges are grouped by plan, equipment, T-Mobile fees and charges, and government taxes and fees. You can also find a summary box for each plan that explains the benefits of talk, text, and data for that line.

Charged Usage

The charged usage section shows the costs of talk, text, data, T-Mobile services and purchases, and third-party purchases for each line.

Stackable Usage

This section shows how much talk and data each line used from the shared pool and how much you were charged for any overages or additional services.

Usage Details

This section gives a breakdown of charges per line, including the amount and rate of talk, text, and data usage for each line.

Learn more about billing settings or how to download your bill on the Account Hub billing page.

Start your line activation

Switch your numbers to T-Mobile

  • Transfer your numbers from your previous carrier, if applicable.

Start using your service

What you need for CAT

  • The latest software on your Android or iOS device
  • Must be subscribed to T-Mobile Direct Connect
  • iOS: Wi-Fi assist must be turned off.

Download & log in

  • Download the app from the Google Play or Apple App store.
  • Follow the on-screen steps to complete first-time activation.
    • You’ll be prompted to send a text message & authenticate your subscription. Don’t change it before sending.
    • Once you’ve sent the message, navigate back to the TDC app.
  • If activation fails and you were provided a User ID and password, tap Log in with Username on the error screen.
    • The first time you log in, you’ll need to change your password to something you’ll remember.
    • Select Forgot Password to send a password reset email.
  • Read and agree to the End User License Agreement.
  • Select the Menu icon with three lines and choose Tutorial to get familiar with using the app.

Radio Mode

Radio mode optimizes the TDC app for TalkGroup communication, providing an experience like Land Mobile Radio (LMR), including:

  • Zones to segment channels into logical groups
  • Support for up to 96 TalkGroups
  • Include TalkGroups in the scan list
  • Modified app layout Radio mode is set by the TDC administrator.

Direct Connect calling

Making calls

1:1 call with automatic answer

  • From Contacts, choose the contact you want to Direct Connect with.
  • Select and hold the DIRECT CONNECT icon. The icon changes color and a chirp tone is heard when you have the floor.
  • Begin speaking. To let someone else speak, release the DIRECT CONNECT icon.
  • Choose End Call to end the call. Calls to offline or DND contacts

If a contact is Offline or in Do Not Disturb status, you’ll get a message to try again later.

TalkGroup Connects

  • Select the TalkGroup you want to Direct Connect with.
  • Select and hold the DIRECT CONNECT icon. The icon changes color and a chirp tone is heard when you have the floor.
  • Begin speaking. To let someone else speak, release the DIRECT CONNECT icon.
  • Choose End Call to end the call. Broadcast TalkGroup Connects

Broadcast TalkGroup Connects make it possible to deliver important information quickly to a large TalkGroup. Only designated TalkGroup members, called broadcasters, may initiate a one-way high-priority call to a TalkGroup with up to 500 members. A Broadcast TalkGroup Connect preempts any ongoing DIRECT CONNECT call and receiving TalkGroup members cannot call back or reject the call. Once a broadcaster takes the floor, the broadcaster will not be preempted by another broadcaster. You only see a broadcast TalkGroup if you are a designated broadcaster by your administrator.

  • Select the Broadcast TalkGroup you want to Direct Connect with.

  • Choose Call to confirm that you wish to start a broadcast call.

  • Select and hold the DIRECT CONNECT icon. The icon changes color and a chirp tone is heard when you have the floor.

  • Release the DIRECT CONNECT icon when you’re done speaking, then choose End Call. Dialing a manual call

  • Select the Menu icon with three lines, then choose Manual Dial.

  • Dial the number using the on-screen keyboard, then select the DIRECT CONNECT icon.

Receiving calls

1:1 call with automatic answer

  • When you receive a Direct Connect call, the TDC app is brought to the foreground and the DIRECT CONNECT icon changes color.
  • You can continue the conversation by touching and holding the DIRECT CONNECT icon.
  • Choose End Call to end the call. Broadcast TalkGroup Connects

An incoming broadcast TalkGroup Connect looks like any other TalkGroup Connect but preempts other DIRECT CONNECT calls in progress except emergency calls. You can recognize a broadcast TalkGroup Connect because there is a distinct tone played followed by an announcement. During the call, only the broadcaster can speak, and you cannot take the floor. These calls also override your Do Not Disturb (DND) status if your administrator has set the TalkGroup to do so.

Only designated TalkGroup members may make broadcast TalkGroup Connects. If you are not allowed to make calls to a TalkGroup, you do not see it listed in the TalkGroup tab. If you try to call a broadcast TalkGroup from history, you see a message indicating that the call cannot be completed.

Broadcast Call History

Outgoing broadcast calls are shown in call history like other calls, but with a different icon and call type indicated. A summary of call delivery status for the broadcaster is shown in the TalkGroup tab history detail for the selected TalkGroup. The number of TalkGroup members who received the call is shown along with the total number of TalkGroup members.

Call volume & speaker

Set Direct Connect call volume

During a DIRECT CONNECT call, the speakerphone or earpiece volume can be increased or decreased using the volume up and down keys. The volume adjusted during a DIRECT CONNECT call is used for subsequent calls including cellular calls.

Turn Speaker on or off

On the Call screen, there is a toggle that indicates whether the speaker is ON or OFF for DIRECT CONNECT calls. When the speaker is OFF, you hear the DIRECT CONNECT call audio in the phone’s earpiece and when it is ON the audio is heard through the speaker.

How Direct Connect interacts with your device

Silent or sound modes

When your phone’s ringer is set to silent or vibrate-only, DIRECT CONNECT calls are played over the phone’s earpiece. To hear a DIRECT CONNECT call, you should hold the phone to your ear as during a cellular phone call. You can temporarily switch to the loudspeaker using the on-screen speaker on/off button for the current call. The next DIRECT CONNECT call again uses the phone’s earpiece while the phone is in silent mode.

Privacy Mode allows you control how incoming DIRECT CONNECT calls are handled whenever your phone ringer setting is set to “silent” or “vibrate-only.” With Privacy Mode, you can control whether an incoming DIRECT CONNECT call is heard normally or if the DIRECT CONNECT call uses the phone earpiece.

Direct Connect & Cellular Calls

Cellular calls while on a Direct Connect call

If you receive an incoming regular phone call while you are in DIRECT CONNECT call, then an incoming phone call is rejected (device restrictions apply), and DIRECT CONNECT call continues.

If you receive an incoming regular phone call while you are in DIRECT CONNECT Group Connect, then the user is presented with a dialog to either accept or reject the call as per native device behavior (not controlled by DIRECT CONNECT application). If the user answers the cellular call, the DIRECT CONNECT Group Connect is put in the background. DIRECT CONNECT voice is lost during ringing, that is, normal device behavior for a cellular call while on a data session.

When the regular call ends, if the DIRECT CONNECT Group Connect is rejoined, it comes to the foreground. The DIRECT CONNECT Group Connect can also end silently in the background.

If Call Priority setting is set to Phone, an ongoing DIRECT CONNECT call ends if a cellular call is answered.

Direct Connect calls while on a Cellular call

If you receive a DIRECT CONNECT call while you are on a regular call, the ongoing cellular call continues, and an incoming DIRECT CONNECT call is rejected with user busy indication. You receive a missed call alert along with an alert tone and a pop-up message is displayed as an indication that a DIRECT CONNECT call occurred during the cellular call.

If Call Priority setting is set to Phone, an incoming DIRECT CONNECT call is rejected. After the current regular call ends, you can make a DIRECT CONNECT callback to the caller from the missed call alert displayed in the DIRECT CONNECT application.

Call behavior in the background

If Background Mode is turned on, the TDC app won’t jump to the foreground with an incoming Direct Connect call. This is great if you have a dedicated Direct Connect button or Bluetooth accessory, since you can take the floor without bringing up the app.

History & Favorites

Access & search history

  • Choose the search bar to search for names or TalkGroup.

Favorite Contacts & Groups

The Direct Connect favorite contacts and favorite groups are separate from the group list on the phone.

Add

  • Select the Menu icon with three lines, then choose Favorites.
  • Choose either Favorite Contacts or Favorite Groups.
  • Select Add (plus sign).
  • Choose one or more contacts/groups, then select Save. View/edit

The Favorite Contacts screen shows a list of all your favorite DIRECT CONNECT contacts as well as their current presence status. You can view or edit favorite contacts using the Contact Details screen.

Delete

  • Select the Menu icon with three lines, then choose Favorites.
  • Choose either Favorite Contacts or Favorite Groups.
  • Select Remove (minus sign).
  • Choose one or more contacts/groups, then select Save.
  • Select Yes to confirm the removal.

Access & search contacts

  • Choose the drop-down arrow (v) to switch between your contacts and the global directory.
  • Select the search bar to search for contacts.
  • Choose the Sort icon at the bottom (three lines) to switch between Alphabetical and Availability sorting.
Add/edit contact

  • Choose Add (plus sign) at the bottom of the screen.
  • Choose how you want to add the contact:
    • Import PTT Contact: Add the contact from your device’s contact list.

You can only edit contacts that you create yourself. An administrator-managed contact name cannot be edited. However, you can add or change an avatar, add or change a color, and add a contact to favorites.

  • Touch and hold on the desired contact.
  • Select Details and update the desired information.

You can only delete contacts that you create yourself. An administrator-managed contact cannot be deleted.

View & search TalkGroups
  • Select the Menu icon with three lines, then choose TalkGroups.

Add/edit TalkGroup

Add

  • Select the Menu icon with three lines, then choose TalkGroups.
  • Choose the Add icon (plus sign) at the bottom of the screen.
  • Enter the desired name for the group.
  • Select Add Members, choose the desired members, then select the Check at the top.
  • Customize the avatar and color, and choose if it’s a favorite, then select the Check at the top. View/edit

You can only edit groups that you create yourself. An administrator-managed TalkGroup name cannot be edited. However, you can add or change an avatar, add or change a color, and add a TalkGroup to favorites.

  • Select the Menu icon with three lines, then choose TalkGroups.
