Integrated Secure Messaging

Integrated Secure Messaging allows you to send and receive secure text messages, multimedia content, and location information to and from other DIRECT CONNECT users.

  • Touch and hold on the desired user or group, then select the chat bubble.
  • Send and receive messages like you would any other chat program.
  • Choose the down arrow to create and send Quick Messages.
  • Use the icons under the chat bar to send:
    • A call alert
    • A location
    • Images or videos
    • Voice recordings
    • Files

Accessories & Bluetooth

Wired Audio Headset

You can use a headset plugged into your phone for Direct Connect (DIRECT CONNECT) calls. Whenever you connect the headset, DIRECT CONNECT calls are heard automatically over the headset instead of the loudspeaker. You must still use the DIRECT CONNECT button on the phone to take the floor to speak, even if your headset has a multimedia control button on it. When you disconnect the headset, the loudspeaker again is used for DIRECT CONNECT calls.

Bluetooth

By default, whenever your phone connects to a compatible Bluetooth device, the DIRECT CONNECT application uses that Bluetooth device for calls. If you turn off or unpair your Bluetooth device, the DIRECT CONNECT call automatically switches to the loudspeaker. The DIRECT CONNECT application supports the following Bluetooth profiles: Hands- Free (HFP), Headset (HSP), or Advanced Audio Distribution Profile (A2DP). When using DIRECT CONNECT over Bluetooth, you must use the DIRECT CONNECT button on the phone to take the floor and speak.

Car Kit

Many cars allow you to connect your phone to the car audio system using Bluetooth. Check the owner’s manual for your car to see if your phone is compatible with your car. Once you connect your phone to the car’s audio system, DIRECT CONNECT calls also use the Bluetooth audio. You must use the DIRECT CONNECT button on the phone to take the floor.

External Direct Connect button

You can use a compatible Bluetooth Smart (Low Energy Bluetooth) DIRECT CONNECT button with your DIRECT CONNECT service. This button can be used in addition to the on-screen DIRECT CONNECT button.

Bluetooth for Direct Connect

If your phone can connect to your car audio system and you receive regular cellular calls, DIRECT CONNECT calls also work. In the rare circumstance that there is a compatibility problem using DIRECT CONNECT with your car audio, but you still want to use Bluetooth for regular cellular calls, you can turn off DIRECT CONNECT over Bluetooth from within DIRECT CONNECT application settings.

Remote Speakerphone Microphone

A Remote Speaker Microphone (RSM) is an accessory made especially for handling DIRECT CONNECT calls. The RSM has a loudspeaker and DIRECT CONNECT button built-in which lets you remotely control your phone’s DIRECT CONNECT application. There are two types of RSMs: those that connect by wire to the phone’s headset connector, and those that use Bluetooth.

Wired

A wired RSM connects to the phone’s USB-C connector. The RSM has a loudspeaker and microphone, along with a DIRECT CONNECT button. The DIRECT CONNECT button allows you to take the floor during a DIRECT CONNECT call and speak. The DIRECT CONNECT button on the RSM works just like the DIRECT CONNECT button on the phone. Depending on the specific RSM, there may also be a connection for you to use a headset with the RSM. Check the RSM owner’s manual for information specific to the accessory. With a wired RSM, you control the loudspeaker volume using the volume keys on the phone and using the volume buttons on the RSM.

Bluetooth

A Bluetooth-connected RSM gives you all the features of a wired RSM without being tethered by a cord. In addition to having a loudspeaker and DIRECT CONNECT button, a Bluetooth RSM also has a volume control. You do not use the volume buttons on your phone to control the volume, but rather the volume control on the RSM itself. A Bluetooth RSM must be “paired” to your phone before it can be used. For instructions on how to pair the RSM with your phone, please refer to the documentation that comes with the RSM.

Additional Settings

Background Mode
  • Select the Menu icon with three lines, then choose Settings.
  • Touch the toggle next to Background Mode to turn on or off.
Network Connectivity

Direct Connect over cellular

Using DIRECT CONNECT over 4G LTE and 5G networks ensure the fastest speed, least delay, best voice quality, and best performance during DIRECT CONNECT calls and when using DIRECT CONNECT services.

Use of DIRECT CONNECT over cellular data networks less than 4G may be restricted based on a system-wide configuration. While the application is restricted, the behavior is the same as having no network connection and a “No Connection” message display. You may be provided an audible and visual indication of loss of connection to the network based on the application settings. Upon detection of 4G LTE or 5G, the application will reconnect to the DIRECT CONNECT server and may give an audible indication based on the application settings.

Direct Connect over Wi-Fi

Using DIRECT CONNECT over Wi-Fi can provide effective in-building coverage and leveraging Wi-Fi access points within organizations and hotspots. By default, the DIRECT CONNECT application will use Wi-Fi when it is available. You can adjust this behavior with the Use Wi-Fi setting.

Location Accuracy
  • Select the Menu icon with three lines, then choose Settings.
  • Choose Location Change Accuracy and choose from the following:
    • Approximate
    • GPS
DIRECT CONNECT Key

The DIRECT CONNECT key setting allows you to assign an alternate key as a DIRECT CONNECT key. This setting only applies if your phone does not have a hard key to use as a DIRECT CONNECT button.

Logout
  • Select the Menu icon with three lines, then choose Settings.
  • Choose Logout > Yes.

What you need for CAT

View & Edit users

Activations

To activate Desktop Dispatch

While creating a user, an email is automatically generated when you enter the email address as a User ID. The user just needs to follow the link in the email and create a new password. Select the Envelope icon if you need to resend the email.

To activate Wi-Fi & Cross Carrier

  • Give the User ID & temporary password to the user so they can log into the TDC app. They’ll be prompted to set up a new password.

Group Sharing allows you to create TalkGroup and share the Groups with other corporations for intercommunication between the members. The owner is the creator of the TalkGroup. Interop Connections

What are Interop Connections?

Interop Connection is a special type of user, which facilitates communication between Land Mobile Radio (LMR) and Broadband Direct Connect (DIRECT CONNECT) networks. These users are restrictive and corporate admin cannot assign any contacts to these users. Because of this limitation, the assign contacts and assign user sets buttons are disabled. In addition, these users can be members of only one TalkGroup. The addition of Interop users to more than one TalkGroup is not allowed.

There are the following types of Interop Connection users:

  • LMR User: These connections are used for one-to-one communication during P25 interoperability.
  • LMR TalkGroup: Provides link between Broadband DIRECT CONNECT TalkGroup and LMR TalkGroup during an Interop call. You can assign LMR User as a contact to a Broadband DIRECT CONNECT user for one-to-one communication. The LMR User name assigned by you is the talker identity during those calls. You cannot add LMR User to a Broadband DIRECT CONNECT TalkGroup.

You can link LMR TalkGroup to only one Broadband DIRECT CONNECT TalkGroup. The talker identity during the Group Connect uses the LMR TalkGroup name that you assign. To communicate on an Interop call, a Broadband DIRECT CONNECT user must have Interop User MRC feature provisioned from the Billing Interface. There is a special icon display for the DIRECT CONNECT user when the feature is provisioned. You can add a user without Interop User MRC feature in a linked Broadband DIRECT CONNECT Group, however, the Interop call is not connected to a DIRECT CONNECT user unless Interop User MRC feature is provisioned for the user.

Create an Interop TalkGroup
  • Select TalkGroups, then choose Create TalkGroup.
  • Choose Standard as the TalkGroup Type.
  • Enter the name of the TalkGroup and select an avatar.
  • Choose Assign Members and assign members. The TalkGroup automatically changes to Interop when at least one Interop is added.
  • Select Create, then select OK.
View/edit Interop Connection
  • Select Interop Connections.
  • Choose Show More (an arrow) to view details on an Interop TalkGroup.
  • Choose the Edit icon (a pencil) to edit details of the TalkGroup, like the name and members.

TFB Tech Support Portal

TFB Tech Support Portal is an online tool used to engage T-Mobile Specialists for assistance with your T-Mobile for Business product solutions. Use these instructions for TFB Tech Support Portal setup and case management.

On this page:

  • Create a Case
  • Update a Case
  • Close a Case
  • Emails
  • Proposed Solutions
  • Watchlists
  • Notifications

Create a Case

  • Sign into the TFB Tech Support Portal.
  • Click All and select Service Catalog from the main screen.
  • Select TFB Support under Categories.
  • Select the Issue Type:
    • 5G ANS: 5G ANS Related problems
    • API: API Access to Control Center
    • Control Center Portal: Support for Self-Service Portal Functionality
    • In-Building Coverage: Report issues with your in-Building Cellular Solutions
    • IoT Connectivity: IoT Connectivity and SASE related problems
    • IoT Invoice/Billing Support: Support for T-Mobile IoT Charges
    • TFB High Speed Internet: Config Requests
    • Wireless Related Issue: T-Mobile Wireless Related Issues (If applicable)
  • Click Submit.

Update a Case

Cases in a New, Open, Awaiting Info or Resolved State can be updated. Use these instructions to update a TFB Tech Support Case.

  • Sign into the TFB Tech Support Portal.
  • Select All Cases or select Case and All Cases from the banner.
  • Locate and click the Case Number.
  • Navigate to Compose, type an update.
  • Click Send.

Close a Case

  • Sign into the TFB Tech Support Portal.
  • Select All Cases or select Case and All Cases from the banner.
  • Locate and click the Case Number.
  • Click Close Case.

Emails

As a case creator, emailed notifications keep you informed of the progress of a TFB Tech Support Case. To receive emailed notifications, the user must be opted in for notifications.

Email Type
  • Open confirmation
  • Update notification
  • Proposed solution
  • Closure notification
  • Update attempt on closed case
  • Case open for internal user

Proposed Solutions

You will receive an email with a suggested solution after identifying your issue. Either accept or decline the solution within seven days. If no response after seven days, the case will be marked as closed and you won’t be able to reopen it.

Accept or reject via email
  • Click Accept if you agree to the solution.
  • A new email will be opened – do not make any changes to the body.
  • Click Send.
  • Click Reject if you do not accept the solution.
  • A new email will be opened – do not make any changes to the body.
  • Click Send.
  • Declining a solution via email will place the TFB Suport Case in an open State and will be reinvestigated by the T-Mobile Specialist.
Accept or reject via TFB Tech Support Portal
  • Sign into the TFB Tech Support Portal.
  • Select All Cases.
  • Click a case number to open it.
  • Navigate to Actions.
  • Select Accept Solution or Reject Solution.
    • If the solution is Accepted: the TFB Support Case is placed in a Closed state.
    • If the solution is Rejected: the TFB Support Case is placed in an Open State and reinvestigated by the T-Mobile Specialist.

Watchlists

Individuals within your organization with access to the TFB Tech Support Portal can be added to a watchlist for email updates on Cases. Watchlist recipients can be added or removed at any time.

Adding to the watchlist
  • Sign into the TFB Tech Support Portal.
  • Select All Cases from the main screen or select Case and All Cases from the banner.
  • Locate and click the Case Number.
  • Locate Watch list.
  • Type the contact’s name, locate, and select. Click Save.
Removing from the watchlist
  • Sign into the TFB Tech Support Portal.
  • Select All Cases from the main screen or select Case and All Cases from the banner.
  • Locate and click the Case Number.
  • Locate Watch list.
  • Click X next to the name to remove someone from the watchlist.
  • Click Save.

Notifications

To manage notification settings for yourself, complete these instructions.

  • Sign into the TFB Tech Support Portal.

  • Select your name on the right corner from the main screen. Click Profile.

  • Enter email. Ensure the notification dropdown is set to enabled. If you have the Customer Case Manager role, follow these instructions to modify the notification settings of another contact.

  • Sign into the TFB Tech Support Portal.

  • Navigate to the Contacts tab.

  • Search for the contact whose notification settings you want to change.

  • Click on the contact name to open the contact details page.

  • Click on the Edit button next to the Notification Preferences section on the contact details page.

  • Select the notification channels and frequency that you want to apply to the contact.

  • Click on the Save button to confirm the changes.

TFB Tech Support Portal Registration

TFB Tech Support Portal is an online portal used by T-Mobile for Business customers to engage T-Mobile Support for assistance with their T-Mobile for Business product solutions. Use these steps to register for and set up the TFB Tech Support Portal.

On this page:

Register for TFB Tech Support Portal

Register for TFB Tech Support Portal

Use this process after your T-Mobile Business account has been activated. First, request access to relevant Access Packages and complete 2FA setup. Access Packages will be able to be requested after a First-Time user has been created by T-Mobile, or after an Administrator creates a new user .

Register by Invitation Email

New Users must be created in the TFB Tech Support Portal before Access Packages can be requested.

  • An email will be sent to the first-time admin containing a link with instructions to request the Access Package.
  • Search and select ServiceNow CSM: External: Access: User: TFB.
  • Enter a business justification for the request if prompted. Click submit.
  • Allow three business days for processing.
  • Open the email with approved access to the Access Package . Click Get Started.
  • Download the Microsoft Authenticator app on your mobile device. Click Next.
  • Add an account to the Microsoft Authenticator app and select “work or school.” Click Next.
  • Scan the QR code to connect the Microsoft Authenticator App to your account. Click Next.
  • Enter the number seen on the screen in the mobile app. Click Next.
  • Two-factor authentication has been successfully enabled. Click Done.
  • Sign into the TFB Tech Support Portal with your company’s credentials.
Register using MyAccess Portal

New Users must be created in the TFB Tech Support Portal before Access Packages can be requested.

  • Sign into Microsoft’s My Access portal.
  • Click Access Packages.
  • Search and select ServiceNow CSM: External: Access: User: TFB.
  • Enter a business justification if prompted. Click Submit.
  • Allow three business days for processing.
  • Open the email with approved access to the Access Package. Click Get Started.
  • Download the Microsoft Authenticator app on your mobile device. Click Next.
  • Add an account to the Microsoft Authenticator app and select “work or school.” Click Next.
  • Scan the QR code to connect the Microsoft Authenticator App to your account. Click Next.
  • Enter the number seen on the screen in the mobile app. Click Next.
  • Two-factor authentication has been successfully enabled. Click Done.
  • Sign into the TFB Tech Support Portal.

TFB Tech Support Portal User Management

Manage your T-Mobile for Business Tech Support user profiles to control who can create and view cases within your organization.

On this page:

  • User roles & permissions
  • Manage roles & permissions
  • Add a new user
  • Manage users
  • Disable users

User roles & permissions

Available roles with permissions in TFB Tech Support Portal

Customer Case Managers

Can view all tech support cases and create or manage all users, including assigning different roles.

Customers

Have limited access to only view cases they have created.

Manage roles & permissions

  • Sign into the TFB Tech Support Portal.
  • Click Contacts from the banner.
  • Click Manage Contacts.
  • Select the user.
  • Click Edit Roles.
  • Select an available role
    • sn_customerservice.customer
    • sn_customerservice.customer_admin
  • Click update.

Add a new user

  • Sign into the TFB Tech Support Portal.
  • Select Contacts from the banner.
  • Select Create a Contact.
  • Fill out the form: [* indicates a required field]
    • First Name*
    • Last Name*
    • Title
    • Role* is Customer or Customer Case Manager
    • Account*: [cannot be changed]
    • Email*
    • Business Phone
    • Mobile Phone
    • Language
  • Click Submit. New users will receive an invitation for an Access Package. All new users must complete first time use instructions before accessing the TFB Tech Support Portal.

Manage users

  • Sign into the TFB Tech Support Portal.
  • Click Contacts from the banner.
  • Click Manage Contacts.
  • Select the user.
  • Update any of the available fields.
  • Click Save.

Disable users

  • Sign into the TFB Tech Support Portal.
  • Click Contacts from the banner.
  • Click Manage Contacts.
  • Select the user.
  • Click Disable Login.

User approval dashboard: Account Hub

Use these steps to approve users who self-register for access to the T-Mobile for Business Account Hub.

On this page:

  • User registration settings
  • Approve / reject user request

User registration settings

Account Manager and End User approval requirements are set to ON by default. To change the requirement settings, use these steps:

  • Log in to Account Hub and select Global Settings.
  • Go to User Registration Settings and select the toggle ON or OFF to control the registration approval process.

Approve / reject user request

  • Log in to Account Hub and go to Manage Users.
  • Select User Approvals.
  • Select View Details from the list of requests and select the desired request.
  • Select Approve or Reject.
  • Confirm the registration and add optional comments in the pop-up window. The submitter will receive an email with comments and approval or rejection of the registration. Visit the Account Hub User Management page if you cannot complete these steps, as you may need more permissions from your Account Admin or Business Owner.

Miscellaneous

Android anti-theft

The Android anti-theft feature makes it more difficult for anyone else to use or sell your Android device if you ever lose it.

On this page:

  • What’s Android anti-theft?
  • Returns and exchanges
  • Troubleshooting

What’s Android anti-theft?

With Android anti-theft enabled, your Google account ID and password will be required before anyone can reset your device. This can help you keep your device secure, even if it is in the wrong hands. You can improve your chances of recovering it, erase your device remotely, and even prevent it from reactivating without your permission. All you need to do is turn on Android anti-theft, and use the Find My Device app with your Google account ID and password.

Returns and exchanges

Returning or exchanging with Android anti-theft active will not void your warranty. Just remember to always turn off Android anti-theft and erase your device before selling or giving them away to ensure the new owner can activate and use the device normally.

Troubleshooting

Android anti-theft is fully supported by Google. Please contact Google with any questions about the service. If the Google Account ID and password are not known, use the Google Account Recovery process.

Apple Find My iPhone Activation Lock

Learn all about Find My Activation Lock.

What is it?

Activation Lock is a feature of Apple Find My that secures your device against anyone else trying to use or sell your lost or stolen device. When this feature is emabled, the Apple ID and password you use for iCloud is securely stored on Apple’s activation servers and linked to your device.

When Find My is turned on, your Apple ID and password will be required to:

  • Turn off Find My
  • Delete your iCloud account from the device
  • Erase All Content and Settings on the device
  • Overwrite or restore an device through iTunes

How to disable Find My

You should always turn off Find My and erase your device before selling them or giving them away to ensure the new owner can activate and use the device normally. You can confirm that Activation Lock is disabled by signing into a device when purchasing second-hand. If you have Stolen Device Protection enabled, you’ll want to do these steps from a familiar place, like Home.

  • In a web browser, visit icloud.com and log in with your Apple ID.
  • Select All Devices, then choose the device you wish to disable Find My on.
  • Choose Erase.
  • When the device has been erased, select Remove from Account. You can also learn more about this feature and find additional steps for using another device on Apple’s website.
